News.title: Woman sexually assaulted by running man in park before he fled as cops launch manhunt
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PARK ASSAULT Woman sexually assaulted by running man in park before he fled as cops launch manhunt

A WOMAN has been sexually assaulted by a man who was running past her in a park.

Police have launched a manhunt after the suspect fled after the assault by touching in Harrogate at around 8.30pm on September 6.

The woman was walking on The Stray between Knaresborough Road and Wetherby Road.

The suspect has been described as a white man of skinny build.





He was said to be wearing shorts, a blue/green running jacket and a white baseball cap.

North Yorkshire Police have urged anyone with information to make themselves known.

Witnesses can call, email, report via the forces website or live chat.

A spokesperson for the force said: “We’re appealing for information about a sexual assault by touching that occurred in Harrogate.



“It happened at approximately 8.30pm on Sunday 6 September, on The Stray, between Knaresborough Road and Wetherby Road.

“The victim has been walking on The Stray when an unknown man has sexually assaulted her whilst running past her. The suspect has then ran off in the direction of Wetherby Road.

“We’re appealing for information about the suspect or anyone who was in the area at the time, and who witnessed the incident.

“The suspect has been described as a white man, skinny build, tall, wearing shorts, a blue/green running jacket and a white baseball cap.”

News.title: Fury as unions draw up ‘wish list for wrecking Britain’ with demands to tear up anti-strike laws
News.content:
UNIONS are drawing up a “wish list” for wrecking Britain by demanding a new raft of new protections for workers, the Tories say.

Pressure is being heaped on Andy Burnham to go beyond the existing employment rights despite reforms already costing business £1 billion a year.



The warning comes from the NASUWT teaching union as the trade union movement meets in Brighton for its annual rally.

The organisation is demanding a second workers’ rights bill that repeals all anti-trade union laws and introduces sectoral collective bargaining.



Shadow Business Secretary Julia Lopez said: “This is a wish list for wrecking Britain.

“Labour’s first Employment Rights Act has killed thousands of jobs, whacked up the cost of hiring, and has been a minefield for businesses. We do not need another.”

But Matt Wrack, boss of the NASUWT, last night said: “Fourteen years of the Conservative approach to employment rights left the UK economy in a productivity black hole.

“The result was crumbling public services, rapidly diminishing opportunities, sickening levels of inequality and a cost of living crisis that will be remembered for decades.

“What does boost productivity? Empowered workers in strong unions.

“But perhaps the Shadow Business Secretary does not wish to boost productivity, or equality in the workplace. Perhaps she seeks to boost billionaires’ profits at workers’ expense.”



Labour has brought in changes including reducing the qualifying period for the right to claim unfair dismissal from two years to six months.

Concerns have also been raised over bosses having to inform workers of their right to join a trade union.

News.title: Romanian van driver who killed Team GB triathlete when he smashed into her during race will be deported
News.content:
JUSTICE SERVED Romanian van driver who killed Team GB triathlete when he smashed into her during race will be deported

A ROMANIAN van driver who killed a Team GB athlete when he smashed into her from behind during a cycling race will be deported.

Rebecca Comins, 52, was riding on a clear sunny day with a flashing light attached to her bike when the tragedy unfolded.



The mum-of-two was sent flying through the air after Vasile Barbu struck her from behind on a dual carriageway in 2022.

Rebecca was taking part in a time trial cycling event organised by Monmouthshire Cycling Club while Barbu was delivering furniture to a driver in Calais.



Barbu was jailed for four years but has now lost his appeal against deportation.

The crown court sentencing judge had told reckless Barbu: “It remains difficult to understand, having reflected on all of the evidence, why this collision occurred.”



An immigration tribunal heard he moved to Britain in 2002 to become a pub chef and eventually owned the bar.

Barbu married a Romanian woman in 2004 and had twins.

Barbu said he identified closely with British culture and traditions and regarded the UK as his permanent home.

But an immigration judge said: “The nature of the offending is important. This was not an accident. It was not a slight misjudgement.



“It was committed using a vehicle which should not have been on the road. It was overladen and deficient.

“These matters compound the nature and seriousness of the offending.”

Judge Ian Boyes added :”I find that the decision to deport him would not constitute a disproportionate interference with his right to respect for private and family life under Article 8 ECHR.



“The very significant public interest in deportation outweighs the appellant’s private and family life considerations.

“Accordingly, I conclude that deportation would not breach the United Kingdom‘s obligations under Article 8 ECHR.”

Cardiff Crown Court previously heard how Rebecca had been taking part in a time trial cycling race organised by local club Monmouthshire Wheelers at the time of the tragedy.

Cyclists had been setting off at one minute intervals along the dual carriageway, which had signs in place warning drivers about the race.

Barbu failed to manoeuvre around Rebecca just moments after he “buzzed” another biker while passing.



Following his arrest, the driver was unable to explain how the collision took place and told police he gave the athlete a two-metre gap.

The court heard he accepted he must have collided with Rebecca and admitted causing death by careless driving before he was sentenced and later jailed in July 2024.

Rebecca, known as Becky, had represented Great Britain in both European and world championships.

She came ninth in the 2018 Tartu ETU Triathlon European Championships, and 30th in the 2019 ITU World Triathlon Grand Final Lausanne.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At the time of her death, she was the Vintage Veteran Champion of the Welsh Triathlon Super Series.



Rebecca had also represented Wales the weekend before the crash.

News.title: Chancellor planning Budget boost for White Van Man as he promises to help millions of self-employed Brits
News.content:
CHANCELLOR John Healey said yesterday he is drawing up plans to help White Van Man accelerate profits.

Mr Healey said Britain’s four million self-employed have had it “tough”.



He vowed to put them at the heart of his October Budget and admitted that the nation’s grafters were hit by red tape and high costs.

Research shows one in three are in a fragile financial position.



Since becoming Chancellor, Mr Healey said he had been committed to easing costs of doing business.

Writing in The Sun, he says: “The white van drives Britain’s economy.

“I want Brits who are self-employed or running their own businesses to make more profit . . . they’re at the forefront of my mind.”

Organisations representing the self-employed are calling for the reversal of the National Insurance hike as it has dampened demand and hit business confidence.

Grafters also want an expansion of the Employment Allowance which lets firms reduce their National Insurance liability by up to £10,500 at the moment.

To give more certainty for those who need their motors, self-employment association IPSE is calling for a “clear path” on fuel duty rather than late extensions.



Mr Healey will be under pressure to freeze fuel duty and extend the temporary 5p cut which ends at the start of January.

Josh Toovey, from IPSE, said: “People are having to make big decisions about their businesses with almost nothing solid to plan against.

“This Budget is the Government’s chance to give the self-employed some certainty for once. At the moment it feels like they’re being left to fend for themselves.”

Andy Burnham, who will today meet business leaders in Downing Street, said the Government must be on the side of those “who take risks, start companies, create jobs and bring new ideas to life”.

News.title: Moment terrified passengers scream ‘we will die’ as flight hit by extreme turbulence & pilot fails to land 3 times
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment screaming passengers feared for their lives as a pilot aborted three landing attempts in extreme turbulence.

Heart-stopping video shows the cabin plunge into a sudden free-fall as one passenger screams “we will die”.



The flight from Istanbul was approaching Tunis-Carthage International Airport in Tunisia when bad weather turned the routine landing into a nightmare.

Passengers screamed in terror when the plane “started to plummet” after the pilot failed to land the aircraft a number of times.



Marina Maiskaya shared video from Thursday to Instagram which showed the passengers gripping their seats as the aircraft shakes.

Terror rippled through the cabin as the plane looped in the sky for a third time, awaiting its chance to attempt another touch down.



Marina said the flight itself was smooth but things turned terrifying as soon as they made their initial decent.

She said: “I have never in my life feared for my life like that.



“We were shaken violently each time, and on the third attempt, we actually started to plummet.”

The aircraft was ultimately force to divert to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport, about 60 miles south of Tunis.

Relived passengers clapped the pilot when the flight landed safely.



More and more, airplane passengers are capturing terrifying footage of extreme turbulence.

In early August at least 12 people were injured after an Air India flight suddenly took at 300ft plunge.

Cracks appeared in the cabin ceiling after the plane took a nosedive just 90 minutes after departing from Thailand.

The plane was carrying 134 people when it went downwards unexpectedly, leaving 10 passengers and two crew members wounded.

The jet departed from Phuket en route to Delhi, India, when it was rocked by severe turbulence.



Many passengers were reportedly asleep at the time of the horror drop.

The aircraft managed to land safely at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Emergency services rushed to the scene and were waiting on the tarmac for the injured passengers.

Some of the hurt people were seen being taken away in wheelchairs.

News.title: Fears Boris Johnson’s train was REAL target of Putin’s terrifying drone attack… but was ‘saved’ by earlier departure
News.content:
BORIS Johnson’s train may have been the target of a terrifying Russian drone attack in Ukraine, rail chiefs claimed tonight.

The ex-PM was travelling close to the Polish border when the service behind his was blown up by Vladimir Putin’s forces.



The train carrying Mr Johnson and various European diplomats had left early amid fears of Russian strikes.

He hit out at the “random and senseless” attack on a stationary locomotive at around 5am local time, and questioned Putin’s “warped logic”.



The strike, around a mile from the Poland’s border, came shortly after he and the UK’s most senior security adviser, Jonathan Powell, had passed through the line heading to Warsaw.

Ukraine’s state railway company said Mr Johnson’s train had left Yahodyn station earlier than expected, and it could have been Russia’s target.

The firm, Ukrzaliznytsia, said in a statement: “It is entirely possible that the Russian drone’s intended target was the diplomatic train.”

It added that the service “departed the station earlier than scheduled after train timetables were adjusted in real time because of the constant threat of Russian strikes”.

Former Tory leader Mr Johnson, a staunch ally of Ukraine, shared footage of the damaged locomotive and the railway track.

He said: “I don’t know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary locomotive on the Polish border this morning.



“What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day — even on civilian railways.

“So far Putin has been responsible for the deaths of 1,700 staff of Ukrzaliznytsia — Ukrainian Railways.

“They and their daily passengers are absolutely heroic.”



He had been in Kyiv at the Yalta European Strategy summit over the weekend, where officials held talks with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky over a possible peace plan with Russia.

Following the incident, he said it was time for allies to give Ukraine the armaments they need in a bid to speed up their victory over Moscow.

Mr Johnson asked: “When are we going to give them the air defences they need? Why won’t we unfreeze Putin’s cash and give it to Ukraine?

“There is more than €140billion in a Belgian bank account – and about £10billion in London. Britain could show a lead. The Ukrainians are going to win — that much was clear from the last three days in their wonderful country. But we will get this dreadful war over much faster if we all get serious and give them what they need and deserve.”



Mr Johnson’s train was allowed to carry on its journey.

Poland’s foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski described Russia’s increasing attacks on Nato’s doorstep as “an escalation”.

Moscow is also understood to be behind several recent attacks in Europe, including on a warehouse in Britain and an airport in Germany.

He said: “It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand.”



The train which was struck was carrying 206 people from Kyiv to Warsaw.

An evacuation order was sounded some 15 minutes before the strike from a jet-propelled drone.

Some passengers were seen running from the locomotive in fear for their lives after the incident.



Ex-Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt was also on the diplomatic train along with Mr Johnson.

He said: “This wasn’t our train (that was hit), but the one minutes after us by the [Polish] border crossing.

“It was evacuated as the drone approached and no one was hurt.”



Pressure is now mounting on PM Andy Burnham to urgently speed up Britain’s defence spending.

The UK has pledged to hit Nato’s target of 3.5 per cent by 2035 and will set out a target date for three per cent at the spending review next year.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the UK “continues to stand firm with Ukraine”, and it was working with allies to “bolster European security”.



He posted on X: “The strikes on Ukraine today, including on the gas works near Nato’s border, serve as a stark reminder of the bombardment that Ukrainians face every day.”

As PM, Mr Johnson was a firm ally of Ukraine, before and after Russia’s incursion.

His resignation in 2022 was celebrated by the Kremlin. At the time, Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: “He doesn’t like us and we don’t like him either”.

Stuart Anderson, Shadow Minister for War Readiness, said last night: “Boris Johnson led the world in standing up to Putin’s illegal invasion of Ukraine, and continues to play a significant role in supporting our friends there. Russia’s attack is a stark escalation. It is yet another reminder Russian aggression is a real and growing threat to European security and, ultimately, our own national security.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The train attack came hours after US President Donald Trump warned Mr Zelensky to stop targeting Russia’s diesel fuel infrastructure in retaliatory attacks.



He said it was “causing a shortage of diesel” which is “hurting the world”.

News.title: Thug brothers attacked Uber Eats driver in ‘vicious’ assault after he took too long to deliver McDonald’s burgers
News.content:
VILE ATTACK Thug brothers attacked Uber Eats driver in ‘vicious’ assault after he took too long to deliver McDonald’s burgers

TWO brothers brutally attacked an Uber Eats driver after they thought he had taken too long to deliver their McDonald’s order.

Charlie Campbell, 21, and Tyler Campbell, 23, assaulted Stephen Onwuegbule on January 13 after they’d ordered fast food to their home.



The brothers, from Chatham, Kent, became aggressive and attacked the courier when he arrived and berated him for “being late”.

They surrounded and then charged at him before hitting him with their fists until he was pushed to the floor.



The assault continued until Mr Onwuegbule’s lip was split and one of his eyes was bloodshot.

The siblings were later charged and they admitted assault occasioning actual bodily harm (ABH) when they appeared in court in June and pre-sentencing reports were ordered.

They were sentenced at Medway Magistrates’ Court on August 27.

Both were given 12-month community orders, with Tyler to complete 15 rehabilitation sessions and Charlie carry out 20.

As well, they were both ordered to carry out 300 hours of unpaid work, and each pay the victim £250 in compensation.

They will also pay what they owe the court at a rate of £20 a month.



At their sentencing hearing, Alan Balneaves, prosecuting, told the court: “It was a McDonald’s delivery and it was 3.20am.

“He found the address, and both came out berating him for being late, but this was not the victim’s fault.

“It was a group attack on one person. Both have no previous convictions.”

The brothers admitted what they had done when the police arrived at their home, the court heard.

Defending, James Langridge said both his clients were young men who had a volatile upbringing and had suffered some significant trauma.



He added: “This can be dealt with by way of a community order which the report recommended; they would also welcome the chance to pay compensation to the victim.”

The chairman of the bench described the incident as “extremely serious” and said jail time or a suspended sentence order had been considered.

The magistrates though added that due to the recommendations in the pre-sentencing report, the early guilty pleas and that they were both of previous good character, the bench could mark the offences with high-level community orders.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The chairman said: “You did come close; the victim doesn’t deserve that sort of behaviour, but you have shown remorse.”

No restrictions were put in place on the brothers ordering again from Uber Eats.

News.title: Moment car flies over circuit barrier after 170mph crash with rival in drag racing championship – as ‘three injured’
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a car flies over a circuit barrier after a 170mph crash during a drag racing championship.

The horror high-speed collision took place at the Santa Pod Raceway in Bedfordshire, on Friday.



Excited fans had lined up as two cars went head-to-head in a thrilling battle of speed.

But as the grey car surged ahead of his opponent in the red and black motor, he appeared to lose control of the wheel.



Footage captured him desperately spinning directly into the path of the red car who had no time to brake.

The grey car was sent flying into the air and over a circuit barrier as the motors smashed into eachother at high speed.



Terrified onlookers could be heard gasping and shouting with shock after the dangerous collision.

Thankfully the driver of the red car – known as Mr Boost according to race footage – had quickly deployed an emergency parachute.



But his car was still thrown into the walls, eventually hitting both sides of the track.

The grey car screeched to a halt near a grassy verge as paramedics and track staff came hurtling over to help.

Parts of the car were left scattered across the racetrack as both cars came to a shuddering halt.



The footage then quickly came to an end following the dangerous incident with no knowledge of the drivers’ injuries at the time.

Both riders thankfully posted on social media that they had come away largely unscathed from the horror crash.

Santa Pod Raceway also confirmed they were miraculously safe and well despite the severity of the incident.

A marshal outside the track was also understood to have sustained minor injuries.

Santa Pod Raceway said in a statement: “Following yesterday’s incident, we’re pleased to confirm that all parties involved are okay without as much as any broken bones to report.



“The safety equipment did exactly what it is designed to do.”

One of the drivers, known as Mr Boost, posted on Facebook: “We will be back and will be faster again. I would have got back in the car today if I could.

“I appreciate all the love and support and messages I’ve received and will go through all of them as soon as I can.”

There is also a gofundme set up after his car was badly damaged, you can donate here.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Located in Podington, Bedfordshire, England, Santa Pod Raceway was built on a disused Second World War Royal Air Force airbase, known as RAF Podington.



It was once used by the USAAF’s 92nd Bomb Group but is now a drag strip.

News.title: Over two million children's sweets recalled in America over 'choking hazard'
News.content:
Over two million children's sweets recalled in America over 'choking hazard'

The sweet products sold since January 2023 have been recalled as they pose a risk of serious injury or death from choking hazard accroding to officials

View 2 Images Over two million sweets have been recalled

Over two million sweets have been recalled in America due to a choking hazard that could lead to serious injury or death.

‌



The sour candy bottles by Ricky Joy sold in the US have been recalled as the rolling ball on the bottles can detach and become a choking hazard, the Consumer Product Safety Commission announced on Thursday.

‌



The commission warned: “The rolling ball on the recalled candy bottles can detach, posing a risk of serious injury or death from choking hazard."

‌



View 2 Images The products were stocked online at Walmart (Image: Alexander Farnsworth via Getty Images)

The products were sold individually as well as in multipacks of three and 12.

They were available in blue raspberry, strawberry, green apple and watermelon flavors.

‌



They were sold at several stores nationwide in America, including online at Walmart from January 2023.

The sweets were sold for around $3 per bottle and between $13 and $32 for a pack.

They contain 1.85 fluid ounces of sour liquid candy to be applied through the bottle’s rollerball top.

Article continues below

No injuries have been reported due to the product.

The Ricky Joy Company will issue a full refund to customers who contact them.

They warn customers to dispose of the item immediately and ensure they are not left in reach of children due to the choking hazard.

News.title: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd set to be sentenced for violently assaulting partner
News.content:
Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd set to be sentenced for violently assaulting partner

Jack Shepherd, who was jailed for the manslaughter of Charlotte Brown after a River Thames speedboat crash 11 years ago, is now set to be sentenced for another crime

View 2 Images Jack Shepherd pictured in custody in Georgia (Image: PA)

Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd is due to be sentenced after he admitted to violently assaulting his girlfriend, including attacking her with a set of barbecue tongs.

The 39-year-old pleaded guilty in July to two counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and damaging property. He has admitted pinning down the woman and punching her in February 2025, striking her in the chest with barbecue tongs in June 2025, and damaging her keys in that same month.

He is expected to appear at Isleworth Crown Court on Monday (September 14) for sentencing. The assaults sparked Shepherd’s recall to prison.

He was originally jailed for 10 years for manslaughter in 2018 over the death of 24-year-old Charlotte Brown when his speedboat crashed during a first date. Shepherd skipped his Old Bailey trial while on the run in Georgia, before he was eventually extradited back to the UK to serve his sentence.

He was set free on licence in January 2024, but faced recall to prison in September last year after he was accused of violence towards a new partner. According to a prosecution summary of the case, he started dating the woman – who is in her 50s – in August 2024, but towards the end of the year she accused him of being abusive and threatening.

View 2 Images Charlotte Brown was tragically killed aged 24 on a first date with Shepherd (Image: PA)

In February 2025, Shepherd admitted pinning down the woman and “punching her several times, causing bruising to her arm and top of leg” during an argument. In the second incident, in June 2025, Shepherd got angry with his partner for burning a pizza during a barbecue, and “proceeded to hit her with the barbecue tongs on her left breast which caused a permanent scar”.

In his manslaughter trial, the court heard that Shepherd, a web developer, met Ms Brown, from Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, for a first date, and offered to take her on a ride along the River Thames on his speedboat. They had both been drinking champagne, and Shepherd handed the controls of the boat to Ms Brown just before it struck a submerged tree and overturned, tipping both of them into the cold water.

He was plucked from the Thames alive, but Ms Brown was found unconscious and unresponsive. Shepherd denied manslaughter by gross negligence, but skipped the trial while on the run and did not give any evidence in his own defence.

After being brought back to the UK to serve his sentence, he was also jailed for four years at Exeter Crown Court in 2019 for a drink-fuelled attack on a barman on March 16, 2018 at The White Hart Hotel in Newton Abbot, Devon.

News.title: Horror head-on crash on busy Sydney motorway leaves 9 injured - including 3 kids
News.content:
Horror head-on crash on busy Sydney motorway leaves 9 injured - including 3 kids

Nine people have been taken to hospital after a pick-up truck crashed head-on into an SUV, causing a three-vehicle collision late at night on a busy motorway

View 2 Images Investigators are looking into whether anyone is criminally responsible for the incident (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

Nine people have been taken to hospital after a horrific three-car crash. Among those hurt are three children and two teenagers.

‌



The head-on crash occurred in Sydney's southwest at Cabramatta, late on Sunday, September 13.

‌



An eight-year-old suffered facial injuries, while two other children sustained lacerations from their seatbelts their seatbelts.

‌



A 50-year-old man sustained critical head injuries.

Investigators are looking at whether anyone is criminally responsible for the incident that unfolded around 11.15pm a busy motorway.

Police said in a statement that a BYD pick-up truck was travelling eastwards when it collided head-on with a Lexus SUV.

‌



View 2 Images Police said in a statement a that BYD pick-up truck collided head-on with a Lexus SUV (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

The Lexus then hit a Mazda sedan and all three vehicles came to a stop.

The man in his 50s was driving the Lexus and became trapped in the vehicle.

Article continues below

He was cut out by firefighters and was taken to Westmead Hospital with head injuries, a police spokesperson said.

The male BYD driver was treated at the scene and also taken to hospital.

A male driver of the sedan and his three occupants – a woman and two teenage girls – were taken to hospitals as a precaution.

News.title: Girl, 6, dies in school bus tragedy as workers 'leave her on board' in scorching heat
News.content:
Girl, 6, dies in school bus tragedy as workers 'leave her on board' in scorching heat

Two workers have been arrested after the autistic 6-year-old was left on the school bus in blistering heat and found unresponsive

View 3 Images Winter Jones died at the scene (Image: Obituary)

A six-year-old girl tragically died after being left on a school bus in blistering hot weather in the US.

‌



Childcare workers were supposed to be looking after autistic Winter Jones, 6, ensuring she was dropped off at school after being left under the car of Kid University in Memphis on August 13.

‌



However, she never made it to Macon-Hall Elementary School that day.

‌



View 3 Images Tametria Norry was arrested and has been identified as the driver (Image: Shelby County Sheriff's Office)

Winter was discovered unresponsive in a bus parked outside the school that afternoon and was declared dead at the scene.

The weather reached into the high 90s (above 36C), according to National Weather Service records reviewed by WMC.

‌



Childcare workers Sabrina Powe, 43, and Tametria Norry, 49, have been arrested and face charges of aggravated child neglect, criminally negligent homicide, and destruction of and tampering with governmental records.

A third employee, Amilya Hardin, was also indicted in connection with the girl's death, reports the Express US.

Norry has been identified as the driver of the van, while Powe was the assistant director of Kid University and Hardin works as a daycare assistant.

‌



View 3 Images Sabrina Powe faces serious charges (Image: Shelby County Sheriff's Office)

After Winter's tragic death the Tennessee Department of Human Services found that Kid University had failed to comply with multiple transportation safety requirements.

The investigation revealed that staff members allegedly failed to adhere to correct vehicle inspection protocols after children were offloaded and the transportation record contained errors.

Article continues below

The authorities also confirmed that compulsory walk-throughs to ensure all children had departed the vehicle were not carried out.

Winter's mum found out the horrific news over the phone, with an employee informing her "Winter was left on the bus" and "she's barely breathing."

Her father described the circumstances as an "absolute nightmare" and said it occurred due to "people who were too busy doing nothing to where they couldn't make sure Winter was taken care of properly."

News.title: Three killed and 15 injured in shooting near school as tense Philippines election looms
News.content:
Three killed and 15 injured in shooting near school as tense Philippines election looms

Three people have been killed and 15 others injured in a shooting ahead of an election - the vote is seen as a crucial step in the quest for self-determination

View 3 Images The shooting took place ahead of an election (Image: GMA NEWS)

Three people have been killed and at least 15 others injured in a shooting incident Cotabato City, in the Philippines, according to reports.

Local media outlet GMA reports that a shootout broke out between rival political supporters outside a school on the eve of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections.

Initial information shared by the Cotabato City Police Office said the incident occurred around 11.41pm between several armed men in front of Datu Usman Mampen Elementary School in Cotabato City.

View 3 Images According to reports, the incident occurred around 11.41pm (Image: GMA NEWS)

Footage from the scene showed the flashing lights of an ambulance as heavily armed officials stood nearby.

Voters in an autonomous southern Philippine region will cast their ballots Monday in the region's first parliamentary elections.

The election is seen as a crucial step in the quest for self-determination and lasting peace after decades of insurgency and violence.

The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, or BARMM, covers five provinces, three cities and 63 villages across eight special geographic area clusters.

View 3 Images The region has seen decades of intermittent but bloody conflicts (Image: GMA NEWS)

It has nearly 2.4 million voters, with election officials aiming for an 80% turnout after polling was postponed for several years.

Centuries of colonialism by Spain, the US and Filipino Christian settlers turned Muslims into a minority group in resource-rich Mindanao, the southern third of the Philippine archipelago from which the BARMM was carved out.

The region has seen decades of intermittent but bloody conflicts over land, resources and political power.

The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

News.title: Forgotten items uncovered during the restoration of Buckingham Palace include betting slips
News.content:
Forgotten items uncovered during the restoration of Buckingham Palace include betting slips

The forgotten belongings, which have remained hidden at Buckingham Palace for decades, offer a fascinating glimpse into the people who worked and lived at the royal residence

View 6 Images Some interesting items have been found hidden away at Buckingham Palace (Image: Ben Whitley/PA Wire)

Everyday items have unearthed under the floorboards of Buckingham Palace, with a Football Pools betting slips from 1957, an empty cigarette packet and an almost 140-year-old West End theatre listings from a newspaper discovered by workers.

‌



A ticket to the Royal household’s social club nearly 80 years ago is also among a collection of forgotten items uncovered during the restoration of the iconic building, along with a rundown of instructions for hosting a grand royal reception.

‌



The items have remained hidden for decades, preserved within the fabric of the property, before being found during the refurbishment. The Palace has been undergoing a £370 million reservicing for the past decade to rewire its electrics, upgrade its plumbing and heating, and overhaul the iconic building's infrastructure to prevent long-term damage.

‌



Meghan Markle gives glimpse of clip of life so far in UK after bombshell return READ MORE :

View 6 Images Everyday items have been found beneath the royal floorboards (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

The blank Littlewoods Football Pool betting slips from 70 decades ago, a pair of battered black hobnail boots and the Silk Cut cigarette pack were among the everyday objects unearthed. There was also a fragment of the theatre listings from The Standard newspaper in 1889.

Also found was a detailed, typed schedule with all the timings and directions required for Queen Elizabeth II’s hosting of a diplomatic reception in her Silver Jubilee year of 1977, revealing the monarch would work the room in a “clockwise direction”.

‌



The misplaced belongings, found beneath the floorboards or other areas of the royal residence during the building work, offer a glimpse into the lives of the people who worked and lived behind the scenes at monarchy HQ.

View 6 Images The blank betting slips show the football teams in the different divisions (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Examples of electrical wire covered with Vulcanised Indian Rubber (VIR) cabling, which posed the greatest risk of fire to the building, were also located – with the cabling, which becomes brittle with age, removed as a priority when the project, which is due to be completed next year, began in 2017.

‌



Some 2km of the rubber cabling has been replaced so far – the equivalent to the length of 40 Olympic sized swimming pools.

The small once-white Whist Drive ticket, priced at 6d, a sixpence, and dated April 14 1949, during the reign of the King’s grandfather, George VI, was found embedded in a lump of building rock.

The pass to the staff social club gathering in the Palace, where people would have played progressive rounds of the classic trick-taking card game, reads “Royal Household Social Club – Buckingham Palace: A Whist Drive to be held on” followed by the faded, stamped date “14 APR 1949”.

‌



View 6 Images A pack of Silk Cut was discovered by workers (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

In April 1949, Queen Elizabeth II was still Princess Elizabeth and been married to Prince Philip for less than 18 months, and their eldest son, the now-King, then prince Charles, was only five months old.

Also discovered were pages from the Daily Express newspaper in 1966 detailing the “maximum security” prison housing the Great Train Robbers, picturing inside Durham Prison and revealing that “the men who were found guilty of stealing a fortune in mailbags spend their week stitching them for nine shillings”.

‌



The instructions for Royal Household staff for the 1977 Diplomatic Corps reception revealed that the Queen and other members of the royal family would move round the Ball Room in a “clockwise direction”.

View 6 Images A copy of the Daily Express from Tuesday February 1st 1966 was found (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Aides were also asked to encourage the 350 British guests to mingle with the diplomats at the glittering annual gathering, where the dress code would have been white tie and decorations or national dress, with the royal women wearing tiaras.

‌



“The British guests will be distributed throughout the State Rooms, except the Music Room and West Gallery, where they should be encouraged to talk to the Diplomats,” the manually typed sheet read.

It added: “In the Ball Room, Her Majesty and other Members of the Royal Family will move round the room in a clockwise direction”.

View 6 Images A pair of Hobnail boots, which are now on display (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Article continues below

It also warned that smoking was banned in the certain state rooms with the reception kept to a strict timetable, saying: “Drinks will be served to guests in the Blue Drawing Room, State Dining Room and West Gallery between 9.30 and 10.00pm.

“Guests allotted to the Ball Room will be served drinks in the Ball Room Annexe from 9.30pm until approximately 10.15pm. Smoking will not be permitted in any of these rooms."

Other findings included a section of Minton decorative ceramic tiles from a fireplace hearth, with the design dated around the mid-1800s, an aged Pewter tankard, a bottle of Schweppes Still Malvern English Spring Water, a wooden junction box, and a faded box containing six Christmas cards.

News.title: Ministers face calls to act after US diplomat 'flown out of UK over indecent images'
News.content:
Ministers face calls to act after US diplomat 'flown out of UK over indecent images'

An American diplomat accused of possessing indecent images of children has been removed from the UK by US officials without informing the British police first

View Image UK ministers are understood to be in contact with the US embassy (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

The Government is facing calls to act after US authorities secretly flew a US diplomat accused of possessing indecent images of children out of the UK.

US officials are reported to have raided the diplomat’s London flat last month, seizing him and taking him to an American airbase for removal without informing the British police first.

American personnel have no powers of arrest in Britain and there was no formal request for the man to be extradited.

UK ministers are understood to be in contact with the US embassy over the incident, which could further strain relations between London and Washington.

UK weather maps reveal 3C cold snap with 108 counties plunging below 10C READ MORE :

Trump responds to backlash over support for united Ireland and 'loves' what he said READ MORE :

In a letter to Justice Secretary Alex Norris, his Conservative counterpart Nick Timothy said he was concerned that the US actions represented “a cover-up” and the diplomat may have committed offences in the UK.

He said: “If this is the case, the diplomat should face trial in an English court.”

A Government spokesperson declined to comment due to the ongoing US investigation, but said Britain expects all foreign diplomats to obey the law while in the UK “in the same way we expect all UK diplomats to do so when posted overseas”.

A spokesperson for the US embassy said it was “aware of allegations” about one of their staff, and expected “all personnel to adhere to the highest standards of conduct”.

Saying they could not comment on the specifics of the case, the spokesperson added: “We quickly informed UK law enforcement and took swift action, and we will continue to work closely with our law enforcement partners regarding these allegations.

“The individual in question has been reassigned to the United States in conjunction with an ongoing investigation. The embassy has informed British authorities of the case.”

A spokesperson for the Metropolitan Police said: “On Tuesday August 25, US authorities made us aware of an investigation they are conducting into suspected offences in London relating to indecent images of children. We continue to liaise with them regarding this matter.”

In his letter, Mr Timothy added that the incident was part of a “concerning pattern” in which US authorities prosecuted cases against American servicemen accused of offences against British civilians while based in the UK.

He referenced the case of an American fighter pilot who avoided a trial under English law for strangling a woman in Cambridge while off-duty.

Captain Jacob Wulfson was tried at a court martial on a US airbase and was jailed for six months after being convicted of strangulation. He was acquitted of charges of sexual assault and aggravated sexual contact.

Mr Timothy said he had received reports of other offences that had been dealt with in the same way, writing: “These cases should have been investigated by the English police, and prosecuted in our courts.

“I ask you to urgently explain what action you are taking to address this, and what will be done to ensure the accused diplomat faces a proper investigation in this country.”

The diplomat’s case has also been likened to that of US State Department employee Anne Sacoolas who caused the death of teenager Harry Dunn in a car crash in 2019.

Sacoolas was able to leave the country shortly after causing the fatal collision after the US asserted diplomatic immunity on her behalf. She eventually pleaded guilty to causing death by careless driving at a virtual High Court hearing in December 2022 and was sentenced to eight months in prison, suspended for a year.

News.title: KEVIN MAGUIRE: 'Farage’s billionaire backers are trying to buy influence – voters must show democracy isn't for sale'
News.content:
Bought lock, stock and ­barrel by ­billionaires, bankrolled ­puppet Nigel Farage is about to ­discover fair-minded voters won’t be sold as a job lot to his highest bidders.

The record £36million apiece from a crypto tycoon based in Thailand and another just returned from China, £72m in all, is a giant moneybomb that will explode in Reform’s face. Tactical voting will be turbo-charged in every general election seat in the country as disgusted citizens revolt against the hard-right oligarchy.

City slicker Farage’s portrayal of his as the “party of the people” is destroyed by the international filthy rich’s loot and a Reform facing multiple probes into their cash.

View 4 Images Donor Ben Delo has been pardoned by Donald Trump after a money laundering conviction

‌



They include Farage’s personal £5m gift. Pocketing another fortune only emphasises this lot are a financial elite apparently plotting to hijack democracy.

The Labour government, like predecessors were, has been too slow and weak to protect Britain from super-rich magnates buying influence and championing their interests, leaving capping all individual ­donations whether at £500,000, £50,000 or (my preference) £5,000 a national emergency priority.

Labour MPs and TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak grasp the urgency yet Housing ­Secretary Angela Rayner sounded shackled by Downing Street caution on the Sunday morning TV round.

View 4 Images Farage claims policies will be 'properly costed and workable' (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The political funding disparity underlines how eager crypto masters are to buy Britain the way they already possess the US, big bucks helping purchase Donald Trump’s victory.

Reform’s £102.5m in the past year dwarfs the Tories’ £14.5m, Labour’s £11.7m and Lib Dems’ £6.4m.

The hard-right party’s sponsor Ben Delo was pardoned by Donald Trump after a money laundering conviction and his £36m comes after he moved back to the UK from Hong Kong.

View 4 Images Christopher Harborne says he loves Britain - but not enough to live here (Image: George Cracknell Wright/LNP)

‌



Thai-based Christopher Harborne, who professes to love Britain but not enough to live here, ratcheted up his support for Farage’s causes to £61m with his £36m and the £5m pressie for his pal Nigel was on top.

What do these deep-pocketed benefactors want in return? Nothing, they insist. Reform has no social care or defence spokesperson.

But it does have a detailed policy to rocket-power a crypto sector earning these men ­gazillions. Hmmm…

Rule by the 21st-century equivalent of medieval warlords, men rich beyond avarice flooding constituencies with hired propagandists, funding national misinformation and internet blizzards, would impoverish us all.

‌



It’s why a people’s revolt against Farage, Reform and his gilded puppeteers is our only hope to save Britain.

News.title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights
News.content:
A cross-party group of MPs and peers has identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) which existing laws, they argue, are ill-equipped to cover.

The Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.

"Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel.

A government spokesperson said AI is "advancing at an extraordinary pace" and is creating both opportunities and risks.

They said: "We're leading global efforts to test and understand AI, with the best-resourced security institute in the world, that will help us develop the standards and safeguards necessary to keep people safe."

On Saturday, the head of the US AI company Anthropic, Dario Amodei, proposed a plan calling for the regulation of AI.

Amodei's plan includes global regulation, industry-wide regulation and independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed.

He also urged the pace of development to be slowed down and the bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk, said they agreed with him.

One human rights concern raised in recent years is that AI can display biases against particular groups if trained on large datasets scraped from the internet which can include racist, sexist and other undesirable material.

AI could also be used to create and spread misinformation.

News.title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England
News.content:
There will be a boost for fresh fruit and vegetables and deep-fried food will be banned in what the government has called the biggest shake-up to school dinners in England in over a decade.

Under new school food standards, fibre and wholegrains will also be increased, and breakfast clubs will have to follow nutrition rules for the first time, with schools also being monitored.

The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) welcomed the changes, but said they hoped the new rules would not become "another stick with which to beat head teachers".

The changes will come into effect from 2027 and be funded with existing money for schools, the government said.

As part of the new framework, sweet desserts, like cake, will be reduced from a regular lunch offer to twice a week in secondary schools, and once a week in primary schools. They also must now be served with a portion of fruit.

Servings of processed meats such as ham, sausages and chicken nuggets have been reduced to once a week and must come with a side of vegetables or fruit.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said they were "once-in-a-generation changes" which would "transform school food for children across the country".

News.title: I had 11 years of chemotherapy for a cancer I didn't have
News.content:
Becky Jones was just 21 when she was told she had a terminal brain tumour and months to live.

She had not long met her partner and dreamed of a career in policing, but suddenly the future was looking bleak.

The diagnosis, by an experienced cancer consultant, led to 11 years of chemotherapy treatment which changed her life. She regularly felt sick, she was unable to take part in family events, her career was curtailed and she felt constantly "on eggshells".

Now 33, she has recently learned she never had cancer at all but an inflammation of the brain that could have been treated with steroids.

The mother of two is one of more than 40 patients taking legal action against University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust due to prolonged or unnecessary cancer treatment.

"I was told time and time again without the chemotherapy I would die," she said.

News.title: Why a fresh wave of North Korean soldiers may fight in Russia's war in Ukraine
News.content:
An enemy that swarmed the battlefield in large groups while under fire, seemingly oblivious to the dangers of drones and fire from automatic weapons. An elite corps of ghost soldiers who chose suicide over surrender. They fought and died in their thousands, then apparently vanished from the battlefield.

North Korea's soldiers were sent to fight by Pyongyang alongside Russian forces as they sought to repel a Ukrainian offensive on Moscow's territory at the end of 2024. They paid a heavy price, as many as 3,000 killed in action from the 13,000 deployed.

Ultimately, they would adapt their tactics, and with Russia would drive Ukrainian forces from its Kursk region. In combat terms, little has been heard of them since, but according to Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, North Korean forces, and their weaponry, are soon to make a dramatic return to Russia's war in Ukraine.

Last month, Zelensky warned that up to 50,000 North Koreans will be deployed in Russia, revising an earlier estimate of 30,000 troops. He called on South Korea to provide support for his country's air defence.

But why, after such heavy losses, would North Korea send more men to fight for Russia, and what happened to its soldiers sent in the first place?

"They're still there", said Dr Yang Uk, research fellow at the Asan Institute for Policy Studies, Center for Foreign Policy and National Security in Seoul. "They are defending Russian territory for another counterattack from Ukraine. And we believe that some of the engineer corps or workers might be in [the Russian-occupied] Donbas area but that's not the combat troops."

News.title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges
News.content:
The UK needs a "culture shift" in how it does business, Andy Burnham has said ahead of a meeting with some of the UK's biggest bosses.

The prime minister said those who take risks in business should be backed by government and local leaders should have the power to work with businesses.

The current Labour government has been criticised for increasing costs for businesses, such as with the employer national insurance and minimum wage changes under Burnham's predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

Downing Street said Burnham will meet with the chief executives of BP, Shell, HSBC, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, BT, Vodafone, Rolls-Royce, and several others at Number 10.

Ahead of the meeting, Burnham said he would give people "the confidence that if they have a great idea, they'll get all the support they need to bring it to life".

"When local leaders have the tools to get things done and government works in partnership with business, you can pull in investment, create jobs and transform communities," he said.

He added the government would be "a partner for growth to make every part of Britain better off".

Burnham will host a reception for the business community where local leaders are invited before a private engagement with senior chief executives at Downing Street on Monday evening.

The meeting comes as higher borrowing costs in the UK and other countries present problems for governments looking to spend money on business support or investment.

Official data revealed a surprise boost in the economy in July partly driven by artificial intelligence (AI) investment, though experts expect growth to slow in the months ahead due to high energy prices.

The US-Israel war with Iran has led to a sharp jump in oil prices, which has fed through to higher energy and fuel prices, affecting households and businesses.

This rise in energy costs has led to fears that inflation will remain high, and increase the chance that central banks will hike interest rates to keep price rises under control.

The expectation of higher interest rates, as well as competition for debt from AI firms looking to spend money on development, has driven up the cost of government borrowing in many countries.

However, many argue the UK has a particular problem with high government debt. The UK yield for 10-year bonds, a key measure of government debt costs, is higher than countries such as the US, France, and Japan.

Experts say this is due to several factors affecting investor confidence in the UK, such as multiple prime ministers, chancellors and policy U-turns over a short period.

In an interview with the BBC last week, Chancellor John Healey called for a restoration of "confidence about Britain" despite acknowledging the challenge of "historic high" borrowing costs.

Others have argued that the Labour government has created its own problems by increasing costs for businesses.

Conservative shadow business secretary Julia Lopez said: "The way for the prime minister to get businesses thriving, delivering jobs and driving growth is to cut their taxes.

"Labour's jobs tax and employer red tape have been devastating for businesses. The consequence has been a drying-up of the jobs market, weaker investment and businesses facing ever greater costs."

News.title: Buckingham Palace works uncover trove of everyday items dating back to 1800s
News.content:
It revealed the monarch would work the room in a "clockwise direction", and that aides were asked to encourage the 350 British guests to mingle with the diplomats at the annual gathering.

"The British guests will be distributed throughout the State Rooms, except the Music Room and West Gallery, where they should be encouraged to talk to the Diplomats," the sheet reads.

Blank Littlewoods Football Pool betting slips from 1957 and a scrap of West End theatre listings from The Standard newspaper in 1889 were also found, alongside fragments of Minton decorative ceramic tiles from a fireplace hearth, with the design dated to around the mid-1800s.

A pewter tankard, a wooden junction box and a faded box containing six Christmas cards were included in the haul.

Examples of electrical wire covered with vulcanised Indian rubber cabling were found. It was replaced as priority when the restoration began as it posed the greatest risk of fire to the building.

Also discovered were pages from the Daily Express newspaper in 1966 detailing the "maximum security" prison where the Great Train Robbers were incarcerated.

The article had pictures of Durham Prison, revealing that "the men who were found guilty of stealing a fortune in mailbags spend their week stitching them for nine shillings".

Meanwhile, the whist drive ticket, priced at 6d or sixpence, would have taken place during the reign of King Charles III's grandfather, George VI, hosted by the Buckingham palace social club.

News.title: Gloomy forecast for tenants as rent rises set to speed up
News.content:
The rising cost of renting a home in the UK has accelerated after a three-year slowdown - with tenants told to expect more pain to come.

Average rental costs for new tenancies were up 2.6% in July compared with a year earlier, according to property website Zoopla.

That remains lower than the rate of rising prices in general, but the property portal has forecast annual rent rises among privately rented homes will hit 4% or 5% by the end of the year.

It said there were fewer homes available to rent and - with potential first-time buyers put off by higher mortgage rates - competition for rental places in some areas was more intense.

"Our latest report shows how sensitive the rental market is to even modest changes in how many homes are available for rent," said Richard Donnell, executive director at Zoopla.

"Growing the number of homes for rent through increased investment is the most sustainable route to boosting choice for renters and ensuring stability in rent levels over the long run."

News.title: Zverev caps transformational year with US Open triumph
News.content:
Alexander Zverev used his greater experience to beat home hope Ben Shelton in the US Open final and quiet a partisan crowd hoping to laud a rare American men's champion.

German top seed Zverev lifted a heavy burden by winning his first major title at this year's French Open and has quickly added another with a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory over Shelton in New York.

At the start of the season, there were question marks over whether 29-year-old Zverev would ever win one of the sport's most prestigious prizes.

Now he is celebrating becoming a multiple Grand Slam singles champion, having seen the path to glory partially cleared by injuries to Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz.

Sinner and Alcaraz swept the board between them at the majors in 2024 and 2025 - and Zverev has taken full advantage against the rest of the field in their absences.

Big-hitting Shelton, 23, has long been identified as a player who can win the biggest titles, but ultimately came up short in his first Grand Slam final against a rejuvenated Zverev.

Eighth seed Shelton was aiming to become the first American man to win a major singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, but losing serve in the first game of the match set the tone as Zverev controlled the opening two sets.

The momentum shifted in the third set, however, as Shelton finally started applying serious pressure on Zverev's serve.

Taking his third break opportunity provided encouragement to the 24,000 home fans on Arthur Ashe Stadium, but starting the fourth set with a poor service game allowed Zverev to reassert his authority and extinguish American dreams.

Zverev did not initially know he had secured victory when Shelton hit a return long on championship point, only breaking out into a broad and slightly surprised smile after his team pointed out the score to him.

News.title: First ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland to meet in Cardiff
News.content:
The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland will meet in Cardiff on Monday to discuss ways of "working more closely", including on constitutional issues.

It will be the first face-to-face meeting among the three nationalist leaders since Plaid Cymru's Rhun ap Iorwerth took office in May.

Ap Iorwerth will host the SNP's leader John Swinney and Sinn FÃ©in's Michelle O'Neill on Monday morning. Sinn FÃ©in president Mary Lou McDonald will also attend.

He will hold further talks with Swinney in the afternoon, with both men expected to sign an agreement on "future collaboration in areas of shared interest".

For the first time since devolution began, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland all have first ministers who want to leave the United Kingdom.

A Plaid spokesperson said ap Iorwerth's meeting with Swinney, O'Neill and McDonald was an opportunity "to come together and talk about how we can work more closely on the issues that matter to people across our nations".

The spokesperson said the "changing political landscape across these islands" meant there was a strong case for "practical political co-operation" on areas like energy, the economy and working with Europe.

They said that also included "the wider political and constitutional questions facing our nations and on the right to self-determination".

Swinney said he believed there was "undeniable" momentum behind constitutional change.

"Every nation across these islands is standing at a moment of incredible constitutional opportunity," he said.

"There is a growing consensus that the Westminster system simply is not fit for purpose and does not work for ordinary people.

"Prime Minister Andy Burnham has accepted that himself - and the people of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have made it clear at the ballot box."

The meetings come days after the matter of Scottish independence resurfaced in the Commons.

During Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday, Andy Burnham appeared to indicate a second referendum could be held in Scotland if there was clear public support for a vote.

He compared the situation to the conditions for a border poll in Northern Ireland, explaining the Good Friday Agreement made clear a poll would be "considered by the Northern Ireland secretary when there is a clear consensus in the country, when public opinion has changed to the point where the call has to be considered".

"I would say that it is exactly the same situation in Scotland," he added.

The apparent softening in tone was welcomed by Swinney before Burnham clarified that another Scottish referendum remained "off limits".

A referendum on Scottish independence in September 2014 saw the country vote to remain part of the UK by a margin of 55% to 45%.

News.title: Donations law changes to be debated after Reform's £72m windfall
News.content:
The House of Lords will debate changes to the laws on political donations later on Monday after Reform UK received Â£72m from two billionaires in 24 hours.

Calls for restrictions are growing after huge donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a Â£100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

The leader of one of Labour's biggest funders, Unite the Union, is among those backing limits on individual donations. In response, Nigel Farage's party has accused Labour of trying to "rig the system".

The sheer scale of Reform's record-breaking donation windfall has prompted an urgent debate across the parties.

On Monday, the bill that would introduce a Â£100,000 cap on donations from British voters living abroad returns to the House of Lords.

The rules were proposed in a review by former civil servant Philip Rycroft aimed at countering foreign influence in UK politics.

The Labour peer Lord Wills told Radio 4's Westminster Hour he intended to amend the bill so that donations from those living in the UK could also be capped.

Sharon Graham, the general secretary of Unite, told the BBC a limit on individual donations was necessary.

Her union has donated large sums to Labour in recent years, but she argues that "billionaires splashing out millions" is different from "everyday workers giving 10p a week to a political fund".

Reform have said "Labour and their union pals know they can't win an election fairly so now they want to rig the system".

Questions remain over whether Reform will be able to keep all of the Â£72m.

Robert Jenrick, the party's economic spokesman, told the BBC on Sunday the donations were "entirely in line with the law as it is, and as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future".

The government has also proposed a minimum residency period in which the Â£100,000 cap would still apply for those who move back to the UK.

This would be in place for the rest of the calendar year and the following calendar year after the person returns.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the rule changes would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".

Rayner added she was not commenting specifically on Delo and Harborne as she did not "understand" their "circumstances".

The Times reported in June that Harborne, who has been based in Thailand, had registered to vote in the UK, while Delo had told the Telegraph in April that he was moving back from Hong Kong.

BBC News has been told both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

The government has previously said it was "determined to tackle" the issue of "mega-donors", and has established a new taskforce to do this.

News.title: Warm start to week to make way for wetter and windier conditions
News.content:
Changeable autumnal conditions are set to continue through this coming week, with spells of wetter and windier weather developing at times.

Monday will bring a short-lived burst of warmth and sunshine before temperatures drop to levels more typical for September later in the week.

A strengthening jet stream will bring deeper, low-pressure systems as the week goes on, with the potential for minor disruption towards next weekend.

Higher pressure looks set to build again for the end of the month, but prospects of a late-September heatwave remain uncertain.

News.title: Six months without bin collections prompts council tax refund call
News.content:
A resident who has not had a bin collection for six months since moving on to a new-build estate is seeking a 100% council tax rebate as compensation.

Bins finally arrived on Hawthorn Meadows in Buckley, Flintshire, last month but Nathan Long and 60 other households can still only watch as refuse workers collect rubbish or recyclables from a nearby street.

Long said he wanted a rebate as he had been required to pay council tax since moving in and despite disposing of rubbish in skips provided by the estate developer.

The council said it was "working to resolve the situation" but a "multi-step setup process must occur" before new waste and recycling collection services are set up.

"It feels like we are not getting anywhere," said Long.

"We complain and we get responses that in part pass the buck on to others and in part pledge to do something about the problem.

"Meanwhile, we are sitting here watching bin crews collecting rubbish from across the road and wondering if they will ever come to us."

Mr Long is waiting to hear from the local authority about his request for a council tax rebate.

He added: "When we received our bins we thought that was the signal.

"But another month has passed and still nothing.

"At one point I went to lodge a formal complaint about the situation and was told I couldn't as technically we hadn't missed a collection."

Katie Wilby, council chief officer for streetscene and transportation, said: "While we normally expect developers to arrange these services before residents move in, we are currently working to resolve the situation for the occupied properties.

"A council officer will visit the site to confirm occupancy, perform safety checks, and integrate eligible homes into the collection system as quickly as possible."

Castle Green Homes said it would continue to provide skips for residents at its own cost until the matter is resolved.

News.title: Reform confident it won't need to repay any of £72m under proposed new donor rules
News.content:
Reform UK believes the Â£72m in donations it has received from two cryptocurrency billionaires were "entirely in line with the law", the party's economic spokesman has said.

Robert Jenrick told the BBC he did not expect that the party will have to return any of the money from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a Â£100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

"These two donations are entirely in line with the law as it is and, as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future," Jenrick said.

As well as limiting how much British citizens can donate to political parties from overseas, the government has proposed a minimum residency period in which the Â£100,000 cap would still apply for those who move back to the UK.

This would be in place for the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year after the person returns.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the rule changes would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".

Rayner added she was not commenting specifically on Delo and Harborne as she does not "understand" their "circumstances".

Answering questions about the donations following Rayner's remarks, Jenrick said: "It might be that Angela Rayner or the government keep trying to change the law to make it even harder for people to donate to Reform, nothing would surprise me.

"But, as it stands, we believe these are entirely in line with the law."

BBC News has been told that both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

Jenrick said Delo had returned to the UK "in part so that he can comply with the changes to the law".

In a statement after the programme, a Reform UK spokesman said: "We are 100% confident both [donations] are legal and won't ever have to be handed back."

One person familiar with the government's proposed changes said the issue of whether Delo and Harborne are affected would likely come down to how ministers choose to define UK residency.

They said one way would be to adopt the same definition used in tax laws, but stressed how complex the rules around residency are.

News.title: Meghan shares glimpse of family life after Sussexes return to UK
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has shared a glimpse of family life in footage posted to Instagram following their return to the UK.

The 34-second clip, which features Wham!'s Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go, begins with Meghan, along with her husband Prince Harry, walking along a country path as she turns and says "come on, you".

UK flag and heart emojis are shown throughout the video, which also shows their son Archie running towards deer as their daughter Lilibet rides her bike.

Another clip sees Harry fishing with the children as their dog walks alongside the water.

It's the first time the Duchess has posted her family on her Instagram grid since the Sussexes returned from the US after living in California.

It is unclear when, or where, the footage posted on Sunday afternoon was taken, external, but one clip shows a pair of wellington boots walking on the spot in a puddle and the children also appear to be in waterproof boots as they head toward the deer.

The UK has had a wet start to September after experiencing its hottest summer on record.

The post offers a rare glimpse into the lives of seven-year-old Archie and five-year-old Lilibet.

Whereas Meghan does occasionally show the couple's children on social media, their faces are often obscured as they are photographed from behind or their faces are hidden by their parents.

Alongside all the outside footage, there is also a moment showing a child's feet in front of an open fire.

News.title: Patrols to start in Essex locations visited by asylum seekers
News.content:
Speaking to BBC Look East presenter Susie Fowler-Watt, Nolan said: "Crimes and incidents associated with the Wethersfield site are very low.

"Certainly, as far as I've seen, there is absolutely no reason for anyone to be concerned about criminality associated with migrants from the Wethersfield camp in Essex."

County council leader Peter Harris said: "Six trained security guards, two each in Braintree, Chelmsford and Colchester, will provide a visible and reassuring presence on our streets, particularly for women and children.

"Our message is simple: the safety of Essex residents comes first."

David King, a senior Liberal Democrat county councillor, previously said the scheme "risks divisions and community tension".

"It could only work if the security officers integrated with already established arrangements," he said. "They won't know the place, they won't know the people, they won't be connected up."

Chelmsford City Council's Stephen Robinson, who leads the Lib Dem-run authority, said: "I think it's really important that we don't create division and that policing is carried out by the police."

Meanwhile, Conservative county councillor Lee Scott said: "We're not opposing it, but we are in the future looking at it to see if it's succeeding and making people feel safe."

The government does not record criminal offences by immigration status, but according to analysis by the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, external, foreign nationals in England and Wales are convicted at roughly the same rate as British nationals.

The council said the trial was "a direct response to concerns raised amongst local residents - particularly women and girls - over gatherings of male migrants in town centres who were regularly transported in by bus from the former military airfield to spend their free time".

"It intends to deter anti-social behaviour, provide reassurance to residents and businesses, and gather evidence about whether additional support may be required," a spokesperson said.

The local authority said it would be funded by drawing down Â£150,000 from the "community innovation and improvement fund"., external

There would be no additional cost to taxpayers and no increase in council tax as a result of the scheme, it added.

News.title: US Open final LIVE: Zverev repels Shelton fight to become a two-time grand slam champion
News.content:
"To finally lift this trophy is an amazing feeling" - Zverev wins first US Open title

Alexander Zverev denied Ben Shelton his US Open dream to win his second grand slam title and deny the American in his bid to end his country’s long tournament drought.

It has been 23 years since an American man, Andy Roddick, last won the US Open but Shelton’s run to his first grand slam final, where he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in an epic quarter-final, suggested that he could break that spell.

However, top seed Zverev was too dominant as the German added the US Open to his French Open crown secured in June, with the 29-year-old becoming just the fourth man in the Open era to win their first two grand slams titles in the same season.

Shelton, 23, overcame a very nervy start and finally arrived in the match to break his opponent for the first time late in the third set and force the fourth, but Zverev immediately pounced to claim the opening break before serving out a 6-3, 7-6 (7-2), 5-7, 6-2 victory.

Zverev did not realise he had won the title, however, after he had lost track of the score when serving for the Championship. Zverev barely responded when Shelton put his return long and it wasn’t until he looked up to the big scoreboard for him to realise he was the champion.

News.content:

When it was first announced that Saturday Night Live would transfer to the UK, I called the show “doomed”. I was writing on a heady wave of confidence. British audiences are derisive about importing American formats, the show’s cast of young comics seemed absent of the necessary star power, and the series was due to air on Sky One, a channel that no one (except, perhaps, Richard Branson and the Duke of Westminster) can afford. It looked doomed. And yet the show is back now for a second series, which kicked off last night with renewed vigour. So, is SNL UK turning into a bit of a sleeper hit?

“I’m the new PM,” Andy Burnham (George Fouracres) announces during the season-opening sketch, “and I’m nothing like the last one!” The line is delivered with a wink. Back in March, Fouracres raised the curtain on the first series playing Keir Starmer. Times have changed, but the sources of comedic inspiration are reliable. The royal family make an appearance (“don’t tell me you’ve spent all your Netflix money!”, Charles (Larry Dean) laments to a returning Harry and Meghan), as does Celeste Dring’s Claudia Winkleman impression (the return of The Traitors in a couple of weeks will likely prove irresistible to the writers’ room). The only new cast member – Freddie Meredith – debuts in a passable scene in which he plays a young man being fed pick-up lines by Jeff Goldbum, who hosts this episode.

Without wishing to demean the enormous charisma of Mr Goldblum, one does sometimes have the sense that he will do anything for attention. After Tina Fey opened the first series, there seemed to be a dearth of A-listers willing to cross the pond for this SNL franchise. And so, Goldblum (who was also the top line guest on the first episode of Claudia Winkleman’s ill-fated chat show) is, at least, a genuine international star. “Well I’m hoping to be,” he warbles at a piano during a sing-song opening monologue, “your precise cup of tea!” The problem with Goldblum as a host is that he is both incredibly game yet also has the dramatic range of a hyperactive toddler. He plays, well, Jeff Goldblum in each of his sketches, the highlight of which is a musing on imaginary friends with a genuinely heart-breaking punchline.

SNL sketches are always spotty, and this season opener is more miss than hit. There’s a good gag at the heart of Gregor J Dupont (Fouracres, again), a thespian who dresses up as a baby to prepare expectant parents, yet the delivery rips off Brian Butterfield, Peter Serafinowicz’s business guru, and the tone feels cadged from Ollie and Archimedes, a pair of verbose British tots who appeared on Very Important People. Ania Magliano and Paddy Young (who should be incorporated into more of the main sketches, in my opinion) return to Weekend Update, and the material continues to be enjoyably edgy. Magliano muses that Germany’s Alternative für Deutschland is really more of an “old classic for Germany”, while Young observes that Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu might’ve thought that “Burnham was just something you do to refugee camps”. While the gags in this section are largely quite sharp, the delivery is a tad stumbling.

Because the cast are good and growing in confidence (some, like Ayoade Bamgboye and Hammed Animashaun get almost no screen time in this episode, though that will likely be evened out over the series), the show has legs. Yet it remains unpolished and, squirreled away on Sky One, is unlikely to find the sort of audience necessary to make it a major talent factory for UK comedy. Ultimately, the show will live or die on its virality, its clippability (to coin a horrible word), yet the YouTube channel currently has just 196k subscribers (for reference, ThomasWoodenRailway, a channel dedicated to a man’s Thomas the Tank Engine model rail set, has 215k subscribers). Since it first aired, the British comedy scene has been talking a lot about SNL UK, yet it doesn’t seem to have the breakout potential of Taskmaster, Have I Got News for You, or even a podcast like Off Menu.

The cast of 'SNL UK' ( Sky )

And so, yes, it still feels a bit doomed. There are exogenous pressures beyond the control of Daran Johnson and his team of writers, or the cast. The fact that the next two episodes will be hosted by Jamie Demetriou and Amelia Dimoldenberg (both funny, yet hardly household names) suggests that the producers are struggling to pitch the project to Hollywood stars on the publicity trail. It makes the show feel parochial when it should be a showcase for the deep reserves of untapped talent still bubbling away under British soil.
