Hundreds of Indonesian rescuers including the coastguard and the navy raced on Monday to ⁠board a passenger ship that capsized in the Java Sea over the weekend as they searched for the 129 people still missing, officials said, with the confirmed death toll at six.

The weather was very poor when the incident happened, with waves as high as three metres crashing into the ship, Syafii said.

The Virgo Transport 8 ship carrying 243 people went missing in bad weather early on Sunday, the rescue agency said.

Authorities have since rescued 108 people from the ship, which was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.

open image in gallery An aerial view of the Virgo Transport 8 passenger ship that capsized in Indonesia's Java sea, 13 September 2026 ( Reuters )

Choppy waters with high waves and strong winds were impeding the search on Monday, said Mohammad Syafii, head of the national rescue agency.

The agency has deployed at least 622 personnel, 17 ships, five helicopters and aircraft to find the missing passengers, Mr Syafii added.

Some of the ships have arrived at the location but it was difficult for rescuers to make their way into the capsized ship, he said.

"We would also deploy personnel with underwater rescue skills but the current conditions do not allow us to," he said.

"While waiting for the weather conditions to improve, we are identifying more personnel with special skills," he said, adding the death toll remained at six.

open image in gallery People check the passenger manifest of Virgo Transport 8 passenger ferry which overturned in bad weather in the Java Sea, at the rescuers' command center in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, Monday, 14 Sept 2026 ( AP )

In a video shared by the rescue agency, a large red-and-black ship was capsized and partially submerged in choppy blue water, with its red-painted underside visible above the surface.

Two small boats, each carrying people, were seen floating in rough waters near the capsized ship.

The location of the capsized boat is around 80 nautical miles (nearly 150km) from the command centre at Trisakti Port in Banjarmasin, another official at the rescue agency told Reuters.

"The conditions there are quite windy, making it difficult for the vessel to dock," the official, Arianto Ardi, said.

It takes around five hours to reach the location from Trisakti Port in good weather but requires up to nine hours in rough conditions.

On Sunday, Edy Prakoso, ​another official at the agency, said the ship leaned heavily to one side after strong ‌waves hit its starboard side.

open image in gallery Survivors of the Virgo Transport 8 passenger ferry, which capsized 13 September carrying 213 passengers and 30 crew while en route from Banjarmasin to Surabaya, disembark following their rescue at the port in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, on 14 September 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the capsized boat had the capacity to contain 500 passengers, so it was not overloaded.

Indonesia relies ⁠on ferries across its 17,000 islands, with sea travel cheaper and more accessible than flying, but there have been numerous accidents.In separate incidents last month, two ferries carrying hundreds of passengers caught fire in the water.

Five people died when a ferry caught fire off Madura island, while one person died in a fire on a ferry travelling from the tourist island of Bali.

As a global public figure and one who can use his “soft power” to influence world leaders, Prince William is right to stress how the extreme weather events in the summer cannot be allowed to overwhelm people, and why a spirit of what he terms “urgent optimism” is needed to find practical solutions to the interlocking environmental crises facing humanity.

He is frustrated at slow “inch-by-inch” improvements, and he reflects and voices growing concerns about how the climate crisis is now directly hurting people in unprecedented ways.

This summer alone has seen record temperatures, heatwaves, droughts and wildfires; and the effects of global warming will exacerbate the El Niño climate pattern to unprecedented levels, guaranteeing more freakish rain and storms well into next spring.

For many, the struggle to restrain greenhouse gas emissions and climate change feels almost lost. But the message the prince delivers is that there is still the time, the technology and the opportunity to make a difference, and that this generation can still “turn the tide” on the climate crisis by 2030.

Indeed, such an existential crisis cannot be simply abandoned.

Writing exclusively in The Independent, and looking forward to the sixth Earthshot Prize event, which will be held in Mumbai in November, the Prince of Wales highlights numerous disparate examples of how innovation in the deployment of existing technologies can make a real difference to people’s lives and their quality of life.

Cleaner air in Bogotá; 200 million people given access to affordable solar power across Africa; bringing endangered species back from the brink in Kazakhstan; and the High Seas Treaty signed this year by 83 nations to protect marine life in international waters all provide cause for hope at a time when the sheer scale of the problems can feel overwhelming to the public and policymakers alike.

It is all too easy, in other words, to grow dispirited and for defeatism to prevail. This especially so at a time when other issues, from wars to the dangers of AI to the continuing cost of living crisis, can all too easily distract from environmental concerns.

Yet it is not inevitable. Hence the case the prince makes for “urgent optimism” and “seeing the danger clearly while believing in our ability to respond”.

“For the first time in history, our greatest challenge is not inventing the answers,” he says. “It is deploying and scaling the solutions we already know work. It is not naivety or blind hope. It is optimism grounded in evidence. I believe that our ability to respond can be the biggest story of this decade.”

It is about practical, scalable solutions.

Some fine examples of this spirit are also highlighted by The Independent’s Climate 100 List of individuals who’ve just got on with the job and found solutions. One such internationally honoured case is that of Joseph Nguthiru, who has found a way to harvest an invasive weed destroying marine life in a lake in Kenya into commercially valuable biodegradable packaging, thus controlling its spread.

The Climate 100 List will be backed by a keynote speech from former British foreign secretary David Miliband at an event during the annual Climate Week NYC in New York.

Most crucially, and encouragingly, for the environmental cause is that public opinion remains overwhelmingly behind it, and increasingly so as the malign effects of climate change and environmental degradation impinge on people’s lives.

Feelings about the climate crisis in Britain are more solid than some of fractious political arguments about Net Zero might suggest.

According to Ipsos Mori, three-quarters of people say they are concerned about climate change today, more than before the heatwaves; and over half report that the extreme summer weather has disrupted their ability to carry out normal daily activities such as working, exercising, or sleeping.

It is only natural, and healthy, that there should be a democratic debate about how to bear the cost of the transition to a cleaner, greener way of life, and how rapidly that can achieved.

Yet the science of climate change is clear, and while the party-political consensus that the climate crisis has to be tackled has somewhat eroded in recent years, it has not been broken.

As Prince William says, we can, and must, make the remainder of this decade count.

Catherine Zeta-Jones has shared her fears over her and husband Michael Douglas’s children being branded “nepo babies”, as she hit out at the “horrific” label.

Used (often disparagingly) to reference the children or close relatives of famous stars who enter the entertainment industry themselves, the term “nepo babies” has allowed commentators to highlight the leg up available to wannabe actors and musicians with family connections.

But the term has proven divisive, with everyone from Laura Dern to Willow Smith offering their thoughts on the moniker.

The latest star to weigh in is Welsh actor Zeta-Jones, 56, while talking in a new interview about Dylan, 26, and Carys, 23, her children with husband of 26 years Douglas, 81.

open image in gallery Douglas and Zeta-Jones with their daughter Carys (left) at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival ( Getty )

Explaining that her kids had been “plugging away” at their careers, with Dylan acting in a number of upcoming short films and Carys also working as an assistant director, Zeta-Jones told The Times: “My daughter wanted to be Amal Clooney for a while. But you have to go with your dreams, your passion.”

On the nepotism label, the Chicago star said: “It’s hard for them to forge a way forward on their own. This horrific phrase ‘nepo baby’ is horrible because these kids didn’t ask to be born into this, they’re finding their own way in life.”

Zeta-Jones added that her children both “love” and are “good” at acting, before clarifying: “Otherwise Michael and I would be the first to go, ‘You know what? Maybe law school looks really good.’”

While used sporadically online in the 2010s and 2020s, the term “nepo baby” was popularised in 2022 by a tweet about the actor Maude Apatow (daughter of Judd Apatow and Leslie Mann) and subsequent New York Magazine cover branding it “the Year of the Nepo Baby”.

open image in gallery Zeta-Jones claimed that the phrase was ‘horrible’ ( Getty )

Many beneficiaries of nepotism have hit out at the concept; Lily Allen, who is the daughter of actor Keith Allen, said in 2024 that the term was “infantilising” because it was only used about women.

But with the label being a constant topic of conversation in interviews, some such stars have spoken in agreement of the term and used it to address their privilege.

As the daughter of Hollywood director JJ Abrams, singer Gracie Abrams is often used as a prime “nepo baby” example, but spoke frankly about the realities of growing up with a famous and well connected father while appearing on The New York Times’ PopCast in July.

“I think about the privilege there… I had a safety net, and that allowed me the ability to experiment and to concentrate and I had the gift of time to dedicate to doing this thing I loved. I wasn’t growing up afraid financially, and that’s the biggest deal,” she explained.

A ticket to a card game night organised by the Royal Household’s social club nearly eight decades ago is among a collection of forgotten objects uncovered during ongoing restoration work at Buckingham Palace.

Blank Littlewoods Football Pool betting coupons from 1957, a pair of worn black hobnail boots, and an empty Silk Cut cigarette packet were among the everyday items discovered beneath the structure, alongside an almost 140-year-old fragment of West End theatre listings from The Standard newspaper in 1889.

Also retrieved was a meticulous, typed schedule detailing the timings and directions for Queen Elizabeth II’s hosting of a diplomatic reception during her Silver Jubilee year in 1977, which revealed that the monarch would navigate the room in a "clockwise direction".

The misplaced items, found underneath floorboards and in hidden spaces throughout the royal residence during construction work, offer a rare look into the personal lives of those who worked and lived behind the scenes at the palace.

open image in gallery Everyday items which have been found beneath the floorboards and hidden within Buckingham Palace during reservicing works that are ongoing till 2027 ( PA )

Having remained concealed for decades, preserved deep within the fabric of the building, the objects were uncovered by contractors executing the refurbishment.

The palace is currently undergoing a £370 million reservicing project spanning a decade, aimed at rewiring electrical systems, replacing old plumbing and heating, and restoring infrastructure to protect the historic building from long-term damage.

Workers also identified sections of electrical wiring coated in Vulcanised Indian Rubber (VIR) cabling, which represented the highest fire risk to the property. Because the rubber degrades and becomes brittle over time, removing the cabling was made an immediate priority when the project began in 2017 ahead of its planned completion next year.

Approximately 2km of the rubber cabling has been removed so far, a distance equivalent to the length of 40 Olympic-sized swimming pools.

open image in gallery A copy of the Daily Express from Tuesday February 1st 1966 with a photo feature on the prison used to house the Great Train Robbery perpetrators ( PA )

The small, once-white ticket for the Whist Drive, priced at sixpence (6d) and dated 14 April 1949 during the reign of the King’s grandfather, George VI, was found embedded inside a lump of construction rubble.

The pass for the staff social gathering at the residence, where workers would play progressive rounds of the classic card game, reads "Royal Household Social Club – Buckingham Palace: A Whist Drive to be held on" followed by the faded, stamped date "14 APR 1949".

In April 1949, Queen Elizabeth II was still Princess Elizabeth, having been married to Prince Philip for under 18 months, while their eldest child, the present King, then prince Charles, was just five months old.

Also unearthed were pages from a 1966 issue of the Daily Express detailing the "maximum security" prison housing the Great Train Robbers, showcasing photographs inside Durham Prison and revealing that "the men who were found guilty of stealing a fortune in mailbags spend their week stitching them for nine shillings".

The instructions provided to Royal Household staff for the 1977 Diplomatic Corps event showed that the Queen and other members of the royal family were to walk around the Ball Room in a "clockwise direction".

Aides were instructed to prompt the 350 British guests to mingle with diplomats during the formal gathering, where the required dress code was white tie and decorations or national dress, with royal women wearing tiaras.

open image in gallery A bottle of Schweppes Malvern English Still Spring Water ( PA )

"The British guests will be distributed throughout the State Rooms, except the Music Room and West Gallery, where they should be encouraged to talk to the Diplomats," the manually typed sheet read.

It added: "In the Ball Room, Her Majesty and other Members of the Royal Family will move round the room in a clockwise direction".

The document also said that smoking was strictly prohibited across specific state rooms and outlined a rigid schedule, saying: "Drinks will be served to guests in the Blue Drawing Room, State Dining Room and West Gallery between 9.30 and 10.00pm.

"Guests allotted to the Ball Room will be served drinks in the Ball Room Annexe from 9.30pm until approximately 10.15pm. Smoking will not be permitted in any of these rooms."

Other finds included a section of decorative Minton ceramic tiles from a fireplace hearth, with a design dating to around the mid-1800s, an old pewter tankard, a bottle of Schweppes Still Malvern English Spring Water, a wooden junction box, and a faded box containing six Christmas cards.

Fewer than one in three working adults view employer pension contributions as a top priority when deciding on a new job offer, according to research from Which?.

Just 31 per cent of respondents ranked employer pension payments among their top three workplace benefits when evaluating a job offer. This placed pension contributions behind paid sick pay (53 per cent), as well as flexible working hours and holiday allowance, which both stood at 45 per cent.

Despite this lower priority, a majority of workers (55 per cent) said they were still likely to give employer pension contributions some consideration when taking on a new role.

The survey revealed a significant age gap. Nearly half (49 per cent) of individuals aged 55 to 64 rated the level of employer pension contributions as a top-three benefit, compared with just over one in 10 (11 per cent) Gen Z adults aged 18 to 24.

At the same time, almost half (46 per cent) of employees currently contributing to a defined contribution (DC) workplace pension did not know how much their employer was adding to their pot.

Sam Richardson, Which? Money editor, said: "Our latest research shows that workplace pensions are a massively neglected employee benefit, with almost half of workers we surveyed unsure how much their employer is currently contributing to their pot.

"Every extra pound that your employer chips in can really add up in the long run, but is often a chunk of salary that lots of us overlook.

"Taking just five minutes to check what your workplace scheme entails, and whether your employer offers contribution matching, could really pay dividends in the long run.

"Crucially, if you’re job hunting, seek out this information at the outset.

"We found people are more likely to consider annual leave entitlement than pensions when looking for a new job, but a more generous employer pension is effectively a silent pay rise."

open image in gallery NS&I ‘has a real opportunity to set an example for the wider industry,’ said Sam Richardson, deputy editor of Which? Money (Dominic Lipinski/PA) ( PA Archive )

Under current automatic enrolment rules, a minimum total of 8 per cent of qualifying earnings must be paid into an employee's pension, including a minimum 3 per cent contribution from the employer. These payments also benefit from tax relief.

Industry experts often advise saving more than the statutory minimum, warning that relying solely on baseline contributions could leave workers facing a retirement shortfall.

Individual circumstances differ, and some workers plan to draw on other assets alongside pensions to fund retirement, such as property, personal savings or inheritances.

Staff and companies can pay in more than the required minimum, with many employers opting to offer higher amounts.

Several options exist to help people determine if their retirement savings are on track.

Pensions UK updates its retirement living standards to provide a guide on how much money may be needed for different retirement lifestyles.

Pension providers also supply digital tools and calculators to help individuals estimate their potential pot size, while the Government-backed Pension Wise service offers guidance for those approaching retirement.

When asked why they were unlikely to consider employer pensions, respondents most commonly stated that retirement felt a long way off.

Which? highlighted that taking advantage of extra employer contributions and giving pension pots time to grow can significantly enhance ultimate retirement wealth.

The survey gathered responses from more than 1,200 UK adults via Deltapoll in August.

News.title: ‘Your home is your palace’: Queen Elizabeth II’s housekeeper answers reader questions
News.content:
Was there one surprisingly simple trick used in the palace that made things feel instantly more polished?

Jay, West Midlands

Making sure you have a routine is the best way for everything to feel polished. At the palace, the team is trained, and everyone has the right tools and time to do their job... They learned how to lift things safely and how to be confident when they were around the Royal Collection. When you’re cleaning historic areas such as palaces and castles, you have to make sure you don’t overdo it. We had a daily routine that ensured we didn’t over-clean everything.

What is the royal protocol for dealing with ironing and maintaining perfectly crisp sheets without using harsh, eco-unfriendly chemicals?

Saleem, London

Much of what would be classed as royal protocol are things we would do in our own homes. For linen, you need to treat it well and look after it by not washing it at too high a temperature or using too much detergent. Make sure the products you’re using are eco-friendly, not only for the environment, but also to care for the linen. For historic linen, it needs to be handled very gently, as it can tear quite easily.

Did the Queen get involved in any of the details of housekeeping?

Peter, East of England

I was very blessed. The Queen did leave it up to me to make those decisions because she trusted me to keep her home and the other royal residences clean and up to a great standard. I kept in touch with her, making sure the team was involved. We would have regular update meetings to ensure everyone knew what was happening and when. There was planned cleaning throughout the year depending on what was occurring, making sure certain areas were protected or closed off, for example.

I would feel very stressed cleaning around objects of great value, history and sentiment. How do you avoid disasters?

Catherine, North West

It’s important the team feels confident when cleaning those areas. We achieve that through training and building their confidence.

In the castle, we introduced a cleaning schedule that covered different areas within the state apartments – and it meant that we didn’t over-clean. The structure of this schedule was important. Every day, we would ensure we vacuumed and damp-dusted; there were no actual chemicals or any what I call “wet chemicals”. On a Monday, for instance, we would clean vases. On a Tuesday, we would do the fireplaces. On a Wednesday, it would be light fittings.

It’s crucial the team is given the right amount of time to clean, so that they don’t feel rushed or stressed. But we also have to remember that accidents happen. And if an accident happens and it was just an accident, then what can you do? It’s just one of those things.

Ultimately, making sure people are trained and confident is the key.

With limited time, what are the housekeeping priorities?

David, South West

My housekeeping priorities when at home are to make things look really tidy quickly. Putting your newspapers away, fluffing the cushions up, tidying the curtains, making sure your washing is cleared and the dishwasher is on – these are all things that will make a big difference, even if you haven’t had time to get your mop or vacuum out.

When are you satisfied a room is clean?

D, North West

I am quite a hard taskmaster and I do like perfection, but equally, that comes with making sure people understand the guidelines and what’s expected of them, after being trained properly.

I like to be visible and around the team, showing them what I’m looking at. I would get them to sit on a toilet and then shut the door, so they could see what’s behind the door – or sit in the bath, because that way you can see what other people are seeing when they’re using it. If you’re cleaning and rushing around, you don’t always see those little details.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Man City officials were ordered to get Haaland decision WRONG – something’s seriously off with VAR
Sports.content:
A MONTH into the season, and it’s all about the referees and VAR again.

And, surely, that cannot be good for anyone.



Lisandro Martinez, left furious by the latest controversy, explained how confidently officials run through the rules at the start of each season.

But when absolutely nobody inside a stadium can understand why a decision was made, something has to be wrong.



And, surely, only the inhabitants of the VAR booth at Stockley Park could see any reason why Erling Haaland’s Manchester derby winner was allowed to stand yesterday.

The Norwegian juggernaut slid in at the back post to direct Josko Gvardiol’s diverted cross into the roof of the United net.



But the flag went up instantly, with both the Norwegian and Enzo Fernandez seemingly offside – and nobody in City even celebrating.

Yet after an age, two and a half minutes, with Old Trafford wondering why there was ANY delay, VAR Matt Donohue told ref Michael Oliver that Haaland was fractionally onside.

More bizarrely and crucially, that Fernandez’s failure to make any contact with his diving header meant he had NOT interfered with play, even though he was NEXT to Lisandro Martinez.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Martinez did pull out of making a play for the ball after it passed his fellow countryman but that, surely, was not relevant, given Enzo’s dive for the ball so close to goal.



The United defender was beyond perplexed. And justifiably so.

Martinez said: “He was offside. He was there. I went to him because he was there in front of me. That’s why Haaland was free at the back.

“I want to be calm now and control myself. It is so hard because you lose. You lose a derby and three points at home.

“Every season they come to our club and explain for one hour, one hour and a half the rules and they look so confident with that.

“Then after, to have five or six people making this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable



“Because you have the best teams in the world in this league, you have the best players in the world.

“And now we have to go home with this injustice. I can’t understand it.

“Let’s see what they want to say now, let’s see. I want to hear – their decision was based on what? I want to hear now.”



Pro Ref’s public concession late last night that it was a howler was the minimum acceptable response although it will not make Michael Carrick or United feel any better.

But such mistakes simply cannot be made at this level. It just gives the conspiracy theorists more ammunition.

Viewers at home were shaking their heads, United supporters in particular seething.

The studio pundits, irrespective of their club allegiances, were equally left wondering if the universe had been inverted.

Gary Neville, who will never hide his United colours, said: “I need the offside law explaining to me, that has lost me I have to say.



“It will need an official to explain to us why he’s not offside.

Wayne Rooney agreed: “Surely it’s offside? Martinez is impacted by Enzo’s movement, and he is offside.”

Not according to Mr Donohue. Despite all the evidence.



Maybe, looking at Enzo’s leap and Martinez’ decision, you might find an arcane rationale for the call – even if that seems ridiculous.

But in the round, taking every other aspect of the play into account – and the fact that the City players seemed to have accepted the flag without any real arguments – it makes absolutely no sense whatsoever.

And if players, managers and fans alike do not see HOW a call has been made, even by the most pedantic of readings of the Laws, something is more than a little awry.

Even without the Haaland winner, there would have been a sense of disbelief.

Not so much that Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes in the first half – Enzo Maresca accepted that one WAS right.



But that the United skipper was entirely unpunished for booting the England man in the backside AFTER kicking him to the ground.

Rooney felt Foden was unfortunate, arguing “That can’t be a red card. It was more of a flick or a gesture, than a kick out.”

Then again, he has previous of his own.

But Roy Keane pointed out: “Bruno catches him, gives the foul away and gives him a little kick.

“For me Bruno is the one who is violent here, Foden is a bit daft but so is Bruno. He has got to do better there.”



Micah Richards argued: “When he got kicked, the second action from Fernandes, if Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed.

“Fernandes kicks him. I don’t agree with the reaction from Foden but it was Fernandes who started it.

“As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes starts screaming and rolling about so if you are the referee of course it looks worse than it is.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That was an arguable one. But the Haaland winner was clear-cut.

The officials at Old Trafford got it right. But they were ordered to get it wrong. How can that make any sense?

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta’s ‘incredible’ new Arsenal model reaping rewards already as David Raya hails Gunners’ strength in depth
Sports.content:
DAVID RAYA used the word “incredible” to describe it.

But the Arsenal goalkeeper was not talking about his stunning penalty save to deny Sunderland midfielder Enzo Le Fee.



Nor was the Spaniard paying tribute to Bruno Guimaraes’ bullet of a strike just 121 seconds later.

Raya was instead hailing the Gunners’ frightening firepower off the bench, which ultimately secured them this 2-0 win to maintain their perfect start to the season.



Guimaraes opened the scoring 13 minutes after coming on at half time, before he combined with Mikel Merino late on to create the penalty that Bukayo Saka won and scored.

Merino and Guimaraes were two of the five substitutes Mikel Arteta used – and their combined transfer fees total around £250million.



Raya said: “It is incredible. All the players coming off the bench were really important.

“That is the model that we have. It is not only the starters, but the people coming from the bench who are really important.

“We had Bruno scoring, and then he and Merino made the pass for Bukayo to win the pen. The whole squad is going to be very important throughout the season.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arsenal’s strength in depth is what makes it hard to see who can stop them defending their Premier League crown.



No other side can compete with what Arteta has at his disposal, and last week underlined that.

This trip to Sunderland came off the back of a tough Champions League opener at Napoli in midweek.

The Gunners came through those tests with victories and clean sheets, and Arteta was able to make four changes for both games.

The Spaniard will no doubt make even more changes for tomorrow night’s Carabao Cup third round clash at Ipswich – but don’t expect the quality to drop.

Martin Zubimendi, who was signed for £51million from Real Sociedad a year ago, is one of those hoping to make his first start of the season.



Arteta will argue it is no surprise he has players shining off the bench given the importance he places on that.

One of the many changes the Arsenal boss has made since being hired seven years ago was renaming the substitutes.

They are referred to as ‘finishers’ and that is a product of Arteta being in a coaching WhatsApp group with former England rugby boss Eddie Jones.

It is drilled into the squad how, even if they do not start, they have a crucial role to play off the bench.



That message is clearly getting through and in the Prem last season Arsenal had 23 combined goals and assists from their substitutes, more than any other side.

Raya said: “You have to follow and trust what the boss wants you to do.

“Sometimes you are going to start, and sometimes you are going to be on the bench.

“Having that mentality to be important no matter when and how many minutes you play, is very important – especially when these seasons are so, so long.



“You are going to have your opportunity and you have to take it like everybody does.

“Last season we scored a lot of goals with people from the bench, who changed games. So, hopefully, this season it is the same.”

Guimaraes was a ‘finisher’ on Saturday night, but it surely won’t be long before he is a starter.

Injuries have led to him having a disrupted start since his £75m move from Newcastle this summer.

He looks fully fit now, though, and a cracker of a goal against Sunderland could be the perfect springboard.



Myles Lewis-Skelly has been partnering Declan Rice in midfield this season, however it will surely now be Guimaraes starting at Brighton on Saturday.

Raya said: “Obviously, Bruno has been very unlucky with his start. He had two little injuries that kept him out of the team.

“He brings a lot of things. He brings maturity, competitiveness and leadership. He is a warrior, but he is so technically gifted.

“He reads the game very, very well and he will put his life [on the line] to defend and attack.

“He is a fantastic player to have with us – and hopefully he stays free of injury so we can enjoy him a lot.”

Sports.title: Ref bosses admit Erling Haaland winner in Manchester derby was MISTAKE as Man Utd told investigation to follow
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have been told Erling Haaland’s winner in the Manchester derby should NOT have stood.

The Norwegian star handed Man City a 1-0 win at Old Trafford after slotting home at the back post.



But Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, dived for the ball on its way to Haaland, drawing the attention of Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lemmens.

Now, a Pro Ref statement has indicated that Fernandez’s involvement DID influence Man United’s defence and the goal should not have stood.



A Pro Ref spokesperson said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.

“The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

Just earlier in the day, the Premier League had backed the decision to award the goal.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Prem statement read: “VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.



“The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.”

But Gary Neville knew it was an error from the start and forsore this apology from the Pro Ref.

He told Sky Sports: “They have given the goal… I’m lost. I’m going to need the offside rule explained to me.

“The officials will be nervous about this goal.

“When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong. The question is does Fernandez, who is offside, stop Martinez getting the ball? He does.”



Former referee Mark Halsey also told The Sun that they had got the major decision wrong. It seemed Pro Ref admitting the mistake themselves was all there was to wait for.

But of course, that does not help Manchester United and it does help Manchester City continue their perfect start to the season.

Martinez, the defender who was drawn to the offside Fernandez instead of Haaland, insisted straight after the game that the goal had to be offside.

He said: “It’s the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice.



“I think it was offside. What I can’t understand is the rules. He [Fernandez] was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

‘It’s so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they’re coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half.

“They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It’s unacceptable.”

Boss Michael Carrick, who has started the season with four points from four games, also rejected the Premier League’s analysis of the goal.

Speaking to Sky Sports in his post-match interview, Carrick blasted: “I’m confused.



“We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision.

“It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now.

“If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a STAGGERING explanation.”

Sports.title: Should Erling Haaland’s controversial winner vs Man Utd have been disallowed? VOTE NOW
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND scored a controversial winner for Manchester City as they edged past Manchester United.

The Norwegian ace crashed home the winner on the hour mark of the Manchester derby, seeing City leave Old Trafford with three points despite Phil Foden‘s first-half sending off leaving the visitors with 10-en for most of the game.



However, Haaland’s goal only stood after a lengthy VAR check.

Referee Michael Oliver had initially called the 26-year-old as offside.



But the City ace was actually being played on by Patrick Dorgu‘s outstretched toe.

Although the controversy came down to Enzo Fernandez’s involvement in the sequence of play.



City’s record buy had been seen standing in an offside position when he lunged towards the ball and impacting Lisandro Martinez’s attempt to clear it.

He did not touch the ball as he attempted to dive towards it before it fell to Haaland who crashed it home into the roof of the net in front of the visiting fans.

And the goal was then given by VAR, with a statement from the Premier League Match Centre explaining: “VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

“The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, this seemingly contradicts Ifab’s definition of the offside law.

Law 11 states a player should be penalised for offside if they prevent an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing their line of vision.

ProRef – fronted by Howard Webb – have now confirmed it WAS a mistake and that a review of the incident will take place.

Former Prem ref Mark Halsey told SunSport: “We saw more controversy in the Manchester derby. Haaland has put Manchester City 1-0 up only for the assistant referee to rule the goal out as offside.

“Now when we look at it, Haaland is not offside but Fernandez is offside. When the ball comes across, he’s in an offside position.



“Being in an offside position is not an offence in itself. It only becomes an offside offence if the player involved becomes involved in active play by interfering with an opponent or making a deliberate play to play the ball.

“In my opinion, Fernandez does that. And I believe that the assistant referee was correct in flagging Fernandez as offside.

“Obviously all goals are checked. VAR have looked at it, and they have decided that the goal is onside.

“In my opinion, it’s subjective to whether you feel Fernandez is making a deliberate play for the ball, or becoming involved in an active play and interfering with defenders.

“If that’s the case, the subjectivity – VAR – should not have got involved. They should have stuck with the on-field decision of offside, which I believe was the correct call.”

Sports.title: Man Utd launch major US court blitz against websites accused of flogging fake shirts and merchandise
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER United have launched a major US court blitz against websites accused of flogging fake club shirts and merchandise.

The Premier League giants have filed at least 11 lawsuits this year, including three in the space of six days last month, against online traders allegedly selling counterfeit United gear.



It comes after The Sun revealed the Red Devils are the Premier League club worst hit by fake football shirts, with 38.4 per cent of shirts checked using an authentication app suspected of being counterfeit.

US court records show the club filed three of its latest cases on August 26, 28 and 31 in Chicago.



The most recent accuses a group of unidentified businesses and traders of trademark infringement.

In one case launched in February, United targeted 24 online sellers with names including yami_jerseys, jersey.factory44 and soccer.shirt.foot.

The club secured an asset freeze before later winning default judgments against almost all of them.

Another action in June initially targeted 57 alleged counterfeit sellers.

City of London Police revealed in July that more than 220,000 fake football shirts worth an estimated £18.5million had been taken off the market since January.

United say fake shirts do not undergo the same quality checks as official merchandise.



Experts have also raised concerns about potentially unsafe dyes and other substances in counterfeit clothing.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick’s sarcastic swipe at Howard Webb before Pro Ref confessed Erling Haaland winner vs Man Utd was a mistake
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED coach Michael Carrick sarcastically said he “couldn’t wait” for an apology from referees’ chief Howard Webb before Pro Ref admitted to the mistake.

Erling Haaland’s 60th-minute winner was initially disallowed but then given following a VAR check after the Norwegian was deemed to be onside from Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross.



The offside Enzo Fernandez dived towards the ball before it reached Haaland but the Premier League Match Centre confirmed that the goal stood as Fernandez did not connect with the ball.

ProRef has since contacted Man Utd to ‘acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement’ – and will launch an investigation into the incident.



Carrick was bewildered by the decision to let Haaland’s eventual winner stand, consigning United to as bad a start in the Premier League as last season.

The 45-year-old also questioned the line drawn to determine that Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu.

Carrick said: “The explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play. So I just don’t get it. I really don’t get it.

“I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, so many bodies, so many screens, and so many whatever offices they are to try and come up with the right decisions.

“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Licha (Martinez) has to react from.

“On top of that, the line was a bit dubious where they drew the line to start with. It’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carrick did not speak any further with on-pitch referee Michael Oliver and indicated he had little appetite to contact Professional Game Referees, previously known as Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL).

“I don’t know how you can (get in touch with them). I don’t know where you go.

“I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one, I have to say.”



When someone suggested United could receive an apology, Carrick replied: “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one.

“I think we all understand what that rule means, and it’s pretty obvious.

“So I don’t think there’s a tweaking of the rules where sometimes there’s a little change. Maybe you only hear it in the meetings and as a general public, you’re a bit confused sometimes.

“But for that, I think it’s as obvious as it gets.”

A Pro Ref spokesperson said in a bombshell statement: “The onfield decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.



“In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

United struggled to create a standout opportunity until the fifth minute of added time after Haaland’s poached strike.

Carrick admitted the manner of the breakthrough affected the United players: “It’s part of the game but it did have a major impact, for sure.”

Sports.title: 'Pietersen will add spark' as he begins England white-ball coaching role
Sports.content:
Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.

Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Joe Root expresses his delight about the appointment of Kevin Pietersen as a specialist mentor for the white-ball teams.

"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."

Is Pietersen appointment a risk? | 'He'll add a little more spark', says Trescothick

The appointment has raised a few eyebrows, coming 12 years after Pietersen was effectively sacked by the ECB in the wake of England's disastrous 5-0 Ashes drubbing in Australia. At the time, the ECB said he had become "disconnected" from the team and accused him of failing to support then-captain Sir Alastair Cook.

Image: Kevin Pietersen's England playing career was ended after the 2013-14 Ashes defeat in Australia under then captain Alastair Cook

Pietersen had previously been dropped in 2012 after sending text messages to members of the South African team, while he resigned as captain after just five months in 2008 following a breakdown in his relationship with then head coach Peter Moores.

Since his retiring a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, also been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after Brendon McCullum had just taken over as head coach, who he'll now be working under.

Having hammered India 4-0 in a T20 series earlier this summer, briefly leapfrogging them at the top of the world rankings, and won their last two ODI series against Sri Lanka and India, England's decision to hire Pietersen appears a risky move at a time when the team is enjoying a strong run of form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fifth T20I between England and India earlier this summer as the hosts romped to a 4-0 series win.

"You can see the team moving in the right direction; we've had great results in the last sort of 18 months - in both formats," Trescothick said, before adding: "I think you're just adding a little more spark and a little bit more variety from a different coach's point of view.

"Kevin has seen white-ball cricket around the world for a long period of time, playing in all the big competitions, he's won a [T20] World Cup [in 2010], you're going to gain something extra.

"It's up to the coaching setup with Brendon to draw out the best from him.

"Management of different players, coaches and setups is is the great art, isn't it? If you get that right, then you get a lot of good things come from coaches and players alike."

‌German Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the final on Sunday to the bitter disappointment of the home crowd in ‌New York.

Zverev finally broke through to win his first major at the French Open, then reach the final at the All England Club, losing to Sinner.

Sports.title: Zverev ends Shelton’s run and American dreams with US Open triumph
Sports.content:
Top seed Alexander Zverev dashed American dreams on Sunday, overcoming Ben Shelton in a four-set battle to claim his maiden US Open title.

The German proved too strong for the eighth-seeded American prevailing 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 in the final at Flushing Meadows.

Zverev added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open earlier this year. In a bizarre ending, Shelton's return sailed long on match point, but Zverev, seemingly unaware that he had won, hit the balls back to the other end of the court, ready for another game.

It was only when Zverev glanced up at the big screen that he realised he had actually won.

Shelton was bidding to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, while also aiming to become only the second black man to triumph at this level after Arthur Ashe in 1975. He walked onto the court to a rapturous reception from a partisan crowd of 23,000 spectators inside the stadium named in Ashe's honour.

Among the star-studded crowd were actors Brad Pitt and Rami Malek, as well as James Bond star Pierce Brosnan, who received a mischievous camera shot from the TV director with the match clock showing just 0.07.

Despite spending 19 hours and 38 minutes on court en route to the final - the fourth-longest total recorded by a player reaching a Grand Slam final since 1991 - Zverev made a blistering start. He broke in the opening game and then broke again on set point to seize control.

Shelton could not even earn a break point in the opening two sets, as Zverev, the No 1 seed at a Grand Slam for the first time, relied on his powerful serve to keep the American at bay.

Shelton had lost all five of his previous meetings with Zverev, but he had also arrived in New York having never beaten Stefanos Tsitsipas or, most notably, Carlos Alcaraz - until this tournament. That run gave him plenty of reason for optimism heading into Sunday's final at Flushing Meadows.

But Zverev, now playing with freedom after shedding the unwanted tag of the 'best player never to win a major' with his French Open triumph earlier this year, dominated the second-set tie-break to move within touching distance of the title.

Shelton dug in, to his credit, and finally brought up three break - and set - points as the Zverev serve suddenly faltered, and the crowd were in full voice again when he converted the second.

But the match was effectively over as a contest when Zverev, who has capitalised on the fitness struggles and absences of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner at various points this year, broke early in the fourth set.

His incessant ball-bouncing - statistics showed he spent around three hours of his 23-plus hours on court this fortnight bouncing the ball between serves - finally resulted in a time violation.

Shortly after his victory, Zverev reserved his most heartfelt thanks for his mother Irina, a former professional tennis player, crediting her with ​refusing to let type 1 diabetes dictate his future.

Sports.title: Wade ends 10-year European title drought with victory in Flanders
Sports.content:
James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy.

The 43-year-old, who last tasted continental glory at the European Darts Matchplay in Hamburg in 2016, produced a 95.50 average and five 180s in the final in Antwerp on Sunday evening.

Earlier in the day he'd beaten Damon Heta 7-4 in the semi-final, having whitewashed Danny Noppert 6-0 in the quarter-finals and edging Rob Cross 6-5 in the last 16.

"Some weeks it's good, sometimes it's bad. That's how it is for me," he said after claiming the £35,000 prize money.

"If it was good all the time, I'd smash them all to bits. We can't always select how we feel."

Wade played in the first European Tour final in Austria in 2012 and this win means he was victorious in the 150th event.

Smith, who won the Hungarian Darts Trophy two weeks ago, beat Gian van Veen, Ryan Joyce and Gerwyn Price in last-leg deciders earlier on Sunday.

"I rode my luck today and the players have let me off, but Wadey, doesn't let you off ever," Smith said.

"I admire him. I watch his game and I can only admire the guy.

"James thoroughly deserved the win today. He's just-he's absolutely class, isn't he?"

The European Tour returns at the Swiss Darts Trophy in Basel, Switzerland from October 9-11.

Sports.title: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body
Sports.content:
Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.

The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville slams VAR's decision to give Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville reacts to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United

A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

What is Pro Ref? Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees) is English football's refereeing body, which was formerly known as PGMO (Professional Game Match Officials) after a rebrand in the summer.

Ex-Premier League referee Howard Webb leads the body, which oversees the four men's top divisions, the National League, the WSL and the U21s Premier League 2.

What did the officials say?

Who were the match officials at Old Trafford? Referee: Michael Oliver

Assistants: Stuart Burt, Tim Wood

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

In their post on X explaining why the goal was awarded, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: 'VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball.'

That stress on Fernandez not playing the ball chimed with replays shown during the VAR review, in which the VAR officials apparently sought to detect whether or not the City midfielder played the ball.

However, the offside rule clearly stipulates that a player can be offside despite not playing the ball and can interfere with an opponent by:

preventing an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent's line of vision or

challenging an opponent for the ball or

clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent or

making an obvious action which clearly impacts on the ability of an opponent to play the ball

Neville predicted error admission

Speaking at the time of the goal on co-commentary, Sky Sports' Gary Neville believed the VAR officials were "wrong" to award Haaland's effort.

Pro Ref's statement, however, fell short of Neville's prediction that they would apologise.

The former Man Utd defender told Sky Sports: "We will see an apology from Pro Ref.

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off.

"It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong."

Speaking on his podcast, Neville continued: "I think they are ignoring the rule.

"They are digging themselves a bigger hole [with the Match Centre statement]. I'm really surprised they put that out.

"They will have to retract that."

"I just think they've got it so wrong."

Roy Keane concluded: "Fernandez is interfering with play. Basically, United have been punished for holding a good line. When you are in that position, you are impacting the game. You're in the middle of the box, you're going for the ball.

Sports.title: Nordqvist hits back at USA ‘dig’ over Solheim course set-up
Sports.content:
Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist was quick to shut down suggestions the Bernardus Golf course set-up had been tailored to suit the home team at the Solheim Cup.

Nordqvist's side completed a 15-13 victory over Team USA after prevailing in Sunday's singles in the Netherlands.

The scores were tied at 8-8 following the opening two days, but USA captain Angela Stanford felt her side had been at a disadvantage throughout the tournament due to the slowness of the greens.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sunday singles from the Solheim Cup

Stanford said at her post-tournament press conference: "Europe played well. I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts.

"And if you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better. I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now.

"Apparently I didn't get to know the superintendent [grounds manager] as well as I should have."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe started dancing and celebrating after their Solheim Cup win

When pressed further about whether she was referring to the green speeds being different to what she had been expecting, Stanford added: "Even when we showed up in July here, they were faster.

"And I don't think it had anything to do with the rain either. Now, saying that, it's my responsibility to get the team ready.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team USA's Nelly Korda appeared to tell a fan to 'have some class' after playing a shot on the 16th hole at Bernardus Golf

"This is the one thing I am kicking myself is that I just didn't keep pushing, you know, we got to figure out how to hit our putts a little bit harder, which is really difficult, to change the way you putt.

"So I'm a little frustrated with myself that I didn't drive that point home."

'We're in Europe in September'

Nordqvist was a little surprised by the apparent dig at the greens when it was put to her at her own press conference.

"We're in Europe and in September. We know how the weather can be," she said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist reacts to winning the Solheim Cup

"I'm not sure I believe a lot in setting up a way to fit Europe because these girls play the same golf courses week-in and week-out competing.

"We came here in July, it was a very hot and dry summer, so the course played a little bit different then.

"So if anything it was just really trying to manage firmness. But then it's obviously been raining a lot in the past couple weeks and then this week we saw a lot of rain.

"So if anything they were probably just playing a little bit softer than we all thought coming here. But that's obviously the weather, we can't control that."

Image: Anna Nordqvist proudly holds the trophy

Stanford: You don't want to take away those moments

The Americans were pictured celebrating on Saturday evening after Jennifer Kupcho had sunk two brilliant putts to snatch a late victory for the visitors and level the match at 8-8 rather than going into the final day trailing 9-7.

Sports.title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner
Sports.content:
Pro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the build-up. The elite officiating body will review the decision and has contacted Manchester United.

Haaland’s 60th minute goal for Manchester City at Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder.

A Pro Ref statement said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.

“The on-field decision was offside against Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Fernández did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

After the match but before the Pro Ref statement, an unhappy Michael Carrick expressed concern over Haaland’s winner.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“At the time I hadn’t totally seen it. But the explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play, so I just don’t get it,” the United manager said. “I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, screens, and so many whatever offices to try and come up with the right decisions.

“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Lisandro has to react from – it’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”

Carrick was asked if an apology from Pro Ref would be welcome. “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one,” he said. “I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one. I think we all understand what that rule means [regarding interfering with play], and it’s pretty obvious. It’s as obvious as it gets.”

Enzo Maresca, though, was adamant that Fernández was not interfering. “Yeah – and the fourth official said Erling is onside,” the City manager said.

The 199th Manchester derby’s other controversial decision was Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card. The forward kicked Bruno Fernandes in the stomach, but only after United’s captain had kicked him. Maresca backed Michael Oliver’s red card but suggested the referee should also have sent off Fernandes.

“Phil Foden red card is a red card, but I also think it is red card from Bruno,” City’s manager said. “Reviewing the action, it is a clear red card for Phil because it is a reaction but you can also see Bruno’s [action].”
