World.title: GOOD news for pensioners in TWO major metros
World.content:
There's some encouraging news for pensioners engaged in rates rebate schemes in these major metros. Image: File

Good news for the country’s embattled pensioners doesn’t come around often. So, when two of South Africa’s biggest metros hand them a break in the same week, it’s certainly worth celebrating.

That’s right, both Johannesburg and Cape Town have moved to ease the property rates burden on elderly pensioners.

Firstly, the City of Johannesburg has confirmed that current rates rebate recipients do not need to reapply for their benefit until 30 June 2027.



GOOD NEWS FOR PENSIONERS

Likewise, the City of Cape Town has pushed back the deadline for pensioners who still need to renew theirs. The deadline was originally set for the end of August 2026.

However, as that’s since rolled over, an extension to 30 November 2026, gives residents who haven’t yet reapplied some extra time to get their paperwork in order.

The aforementioned is tied to the rollout of the City’s 2025 General Valuation.



This requires every elderly rebate holder to have their eligibility reassessed.

Cape Town’s income bands dictate that pensioners and social grant recipients aged 60 and older, earning R10 000 or less per month, qualify for a 100% rebate.

While those earning between up to R27 000 a month are subject to a sliding scale from 10% to 90%.



Once approved under the new cycle, the rebates stay valid until 30 June 2029.

PENSIONERS IN JOBURG

Pensioners with fixed income are some of the hardest hit by inflation fluctuation. Image: File

“The City of Johannesburg is pleased to inform pensioner homeowners who are currently receiving property rates rebates that they do not need to reapply for the benefit during the current financial year,” confirmed the City. However, if you recently turned 60 the exemption doesn’t cover you. Any new applicant will still need to submit a full application, including valid ID documents with biometrics, through official City of Joburg municipal channels.

A reminder that the metro’s criteria for pensioners aged 60 and over is for property valued at a threshold of R1.5 million. Applicants must earn under R13 519 per month to qualify for a full 100% rebate. Anything up to R23 172 drops on a scale to 50%. For homeowners 70 and older, the threshold rises to R2 million, provided their municipal account is in good standing.



HOW MANY PENSIONERS BENEFIT FROM REBATES?

In pure numbers, the rates rebate programmes in the major metros is not small change:

In the 2025/26 financial year, Johannesburg granted rebates to 38 308 elderly homeowners roughly R329 million in relief.

elderly homeowners roughly in relief. Cape Town does not publish exact figures, however, its Integrated Indigent Assistance scheme has provision for 192 500 households.

But what do you think? Can such rebate schemes for pensioners be improved upon in your opinion? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Yellow Level 4 warning as cut-off low threatens flooding in two provinces
World.content:
Dark clouds gather over the landscape as a cut-off low brings a risk of heavy rain and severe weather to parts of South Africa. Image: Unsplash

A Yellow Level 4 warning for disruptive rain is in place as a cut-off low develops west of South Africa, with flooding, damaging winds, severe thunderstorms and rough seas expected in parts of the country.

A Yellow Level 4 warning for disruptive rain is in place over the eastern parts of Namakwa in the Northern Cape and the Central Karoo District in the Western Cape.

Heavy rain could lead to flooding of roads and settlements and cause major disruptions to traffic.



Yellow Level 2 warnings: Thunderstorms, damaging winds and rough seas

According to South African Weather Services (SAWS), several areas face Yellow Level 2 warnings for severe thunderstorms, damaging winds and dangerous coastal conditions.

The warning covers the Nama Khoi and Kamiesberg municipalities in the Northern Cape.

In the Western Cape, it covers the West Coast, Cape Winelands and Overberg districts, as well as the City of Cape Town.

These storms could produce excessive lightning, leading to injuries to people and livestock, power disruptions and other service interruptions.

A separate Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds covers parts of the North West, Northern Cape, Free State, Limpopo and Eastern Cape.

The winds could damage informal settlements and disrupt power and communications.



A Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds and waves is in place along the KwaZulu-Natal coast.

It covers the area between Port Edward and Richards Bay and the adjacent interior.

Conditions could disrupt small harbours and ports, make navigation difficult and damage infrastructure and settlements.

Yellow Level 1 warnings

A Yellow Level 1 warning for severe thunderstorms covers parts of the north-eastern coast and adjacent interior of the Eastern Cape.

The storms could damage settlements and temporary structures and disrupt power and communications.

Another Yellow Level 1 warning for damaging winds covers parts of the extreme north-eastern Eastern Cape coast and adjacent interior.

Cut-off low to bring heavy rain and rough seas

The cut-off low developing west of the country will affect the Western and Northern Cape from Sunday into Monday, 14 September.

It could bring intermittent showers and thundershowers, with heavy downpours at times, possible large amounts of small hail and lightning.

Temperatures could fall significantly over high-lying areas, while strong winds could affect the coast and interior.

Very rough seas, reaching 4.0 to 4.5 metres south of Table Bay, are also expected.

Extremely high fire danger in Limpopo

Limpopo faces extremely high fire danger over the western parts of the Waterberg District and the Blouberg municipality.

World.title: Expats praised for Springbok support: ‘Leaving SA doesn’t mean SA leaves you’
World.content:
South Africans living in the US have been praised for their support of the Springboks. Images via IG

Minister of Sport Gayton McKenzie has thanked South African expats who travelled to Baltimore to support the Springboks at their Greatest Rivalry series finale over the weekend.

Rugby fans, many of whom supported the Boks, filled the 68 000 M&T Bank Stadium, setting a record for an audience for a rugby match.

GAYTON MCKENZIE THANKS DIASPORA

Days after appealing to South Africans living in the US to show up for the Springboks, Gayton McKenzie has issued a heartfelt thank you.



The Minister of Sport acknowledged the expat community who had travelled from around he country to attend the Baltimore match on Saturday, 12 September.

Gayton shared a picture of a family that had driven across multiple states to support the Boks in their match against the All Blacks.

He posted: “Leaving SA doesn’t mean SA ever leaves you. The Bok spirit was burning in this great family, who drove 2400km from Houston to a stadium that looked like a home test. Thank you to all the South Africans abroad.

“You showed the beautiful, friendly face of the SA diaspora to the world”.

Leaving SA doesn’t mean SA ever leaves you. The Bok spirit was burning in this great family, who drove 2400km from Houston to a stadium that looked like a home test. Thank you to all the South Africans abroad. You showed the beautiful friendly face of the SA diaspora to the world pic.twitter.com/pL9IK3ddwP — Gayton McKenzie (@GaytonMcK) September 13, 2026

Springboks captain Siya Kolisi also thanked supporters, saying in a post-match interview: “It was super special. It was crazy the amount of people who came out to support us. I want to thank every single South African here and back at home. We are so grateful. We do it for you each and every time.”



As did coach Rassie Erasmus, who added: “It was awesome to see so many South Africans here. I don’t know how they afford it or how they got here, but it’s great.”

SOUTH AFRICANS WHO LIVE IN THE US

According to statistics from a 2023 US consensus, around 85 000 South Africans live in the US.

The state of Maryland – where the Springboks will play – has an expat community of 2000.

World.title: Rassie and Siya sport chiskops after taking a bet! [photos]
World.content:
Siya Kolisi and Rassie Erasmus shaved their heads after losing a bet. Images via IG

Springboks captain Siya Kolisi and team coach Rassie Erasmus, as well as support staff, have shaved their heads bald after taking a bet…

The 53-year-old celebrated his 100th test cap at the helm of the Boks, who won the Greatest Rivalry series 43-28 in Baltimore.

RASSIE ERASMUS AND SIYA KOLISI SHAVE THEIR HEADS

On their Instagram accounts, Rassie Erasmus and Siya Kolisi have sparked speculation after posting pictures of their shaved heads.



The Sprigboks coach hinted that the bold, bald move was a result of winning a bet.

In another post, Rassie posted a picture with Bok staff who also sported chiskops, like him.

“Rules are rules”, he casually captioned the post.

Siya also posted a picture of himself and Rassie posing with their bald heads, thanking the coach for his hard work and efforts.

In the comments section, Springbok fans were amused, with many asking for details of the mystery bet.

FOR ALL SOUTH AFRICANS

Speaking after the Springboks’ Greatest Rivalry series win and his 100th test appearance as coach, Rassie Erasmus thanked South Africans for their loyal support.

He said in a post-match interview of rugby fans who had travelled to Baltimore to watch the Boks: “It was awesome to see so many South Africans here; I don’t know how they afford it or how they got here, but it’s great.”

Rassie emphasised that the victory was for all South Africans, including those who could not afford to watch their team play.

He added, “We really care the most about South African people. There’s only one reason we do this.

“We want to win and feel great for us as a team, but that’s why we play rugby. We just want to please South African people.’

World.title: When will the Springboks play the All Blacks again?
World.content:
When will the Springboks play the All Blacks again? Image via X

The inaugural Greatest Rivalry series is officially over, bringing an end to weeks of camaraderie and fierce competition between the All Blacks and the Springboks.

WHEN WILL THE SPRINGBOKS AND ALL BLACKS PLAY EACH OTHER AGAIN?

Despite winning the Greatest Rivalry series 3-1, the Springboks could face the All Blacks again, as soon as November, when the Nations Championship’s finals weekend takes place.

In November, the All Blacks play Scotland, Wales and England, while the Springboks face Italy, France and Ireland.



The Springboks and All Blacks are currently 1st and 2nd in their respective pools; however, that could change, as the November fixtures will decide where each team finishes. If both the Springboks and the All Blacks top their pool, they could meet in Twickenham for the final.

If they both finish in second place, they could play for the 3rd and 4th positions.

COULD THEY CROSS PATHS AT THE RUGBY WORLD CUP?

The Springboks could also cross paths with the All Blacks at the Rugby World Cup, which will take place in Australia next year.



The two sides have not been drawn to play each other in the pool stage. However, if both teams progress as expected, South Africa and New Zealand could meet in the quarter-finals.

The next Greatest Rivalry series will take place in four years, in 2030.

World.title: Mzansi to Baltimore: Green Citi Golf Chico steals the show [photos]
World.content:
A green Citi Golf Chico was spotted in Baltimore. Images via Facebook

A bright green Citi Golf Chico, emblazoned with Springbok imagery, has become a viral sensation after it appeared on the streets of Baltimore ahead of the match against the All Blacks at M&T Bank Stadium.

The vehicle is owned by a South African expat, who has a fleet of imported Citi Golfs in multiple colours.

CITI GOLF CHICO GOES VIRAL IN BALTIMORE

Images of a bright green Citi Golf Chico with Springbok stickers plastered all over went viral on social media.



The car bore a South African number plate – from KwaZulu-Natal specifically.

The sighting of the car has warmed the hearts of South Africans on social media, as an ode to both the country and the Springboks rugby team.

How did they get a Chico in downtown Baltimore I’m crying 😭😭 #RSAvNZL pic.twitter.com/hX1ZUy6OKu  September 12, 2026

Mad things are happening here in Baltimore, how has a Chicho ended up here 🤣



With a NZ reg plate too?! 🤔😭

#RSAvNZL pic.twitter.com/cIMMhKJweC — ❎e k ℹ️ (@XekiHlongwane) September 13, 2026

WHO OWNS IT?

The Citi Golf Chico is owned by US content creator Ali Farzad, also known as @networktheking, and his South African wife, Xaba Nonhlanhla.



Xaba hails from Durban and continues to shine her love for South Africa through her social media platforms.

The Virginia-based couple purchased the car last year, which they have added to their fleet of Citi Golf Chicos in various colours.

Ali and Xaba, affectionately known as Magesh, run an entertainment promotion company called CitiVibes, which facilitates music gigs in the Washington metropolitan area.

The couple shared: “Our inspiration comes strongly from South African township culture, where music, style, and togetherness create magic even in the simplest moments.

“As a tribute to this influence, we’ve imported seven iconic VW Citi Golfs from South Africa – symbols of heritage, identity, and timeless culture that reflect who we are and what we represent”

World.title: Sacha sends message to critics after passionate performance
World.content:
Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu sends a message to his critics. Images via IG

Springbok Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has seemingly sent a message to his critics after his passionate performance, which helped the team clinch the inaugural Greatest Rivalry series title against the All Blacks in Baltimore.

The flyhalf has been admonished by rugby fans on social media after a series of match-day blunders over the past few weeks.

SPRINGBOK SACHA SENDS MESSAGE TO CRITICS

On his Instagram account, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu shared a post that celebrated the Springboks’ Greatest Rivalry title win and sent a message to his critics.



The post included a picture of the Boks lifting the trophy, with a tongue-in-cheek caption that read: “Can’t spell trust without us”.

It was liked by Sacha’s girlfriend, Sarah Langa, who has also faced flak over their relationship.

Over the past few weeks, the 25-year-old has been criticised for his poor kicking decisions, as well as overall errors and attitude during the test series against the All Blacks.



TEARS DURING THE ANTHEM

Ahead of kickoff, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu trended on social media after becoming visibly emotional during the performance of the national anthem, sung by Jesse Clegg.

The famous flyhalf could not hold back the tears as seen in the video below..

World.title: Cosatu kicks off congress to elect new leadership
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Delegates are gathering in Midrand, Johannesburg, for COSATU’s 15th National Congress, where the trade union federation is expected to elect a new leadership.

The congress will be held from 14 to 17 September. At least 1,800 delegates from various affiliated trade unions are expected to gather at the venue.

The conference comes at a challenging time for workers, with the rapid adoption of new technologies putting jobs and livelihoods under increasing pressure.

Several companies have announced retrenchments and restructuring, while households continue to grapple with a rising cost of living.

Political strategy is also expected to dominate the conference, particularly the question of who COSATU will support ahead of this year’s local government elections.

The issue comes as tensions within the Tripartite Alliance continue to surface.

The SACP has announced that it will contest the local government elections independently, rather than relying on the traditional alliance arrangement.

COSATU has called for an Alliance Political Council meeting, bringing together the ANC, SACP and the federation to find a way forward on the elections without undermining the Tripartite Alliance.

But so far, the federation has been unable to get all three alliance partners around the same table.

World.title: 'Cat Matlala, co-accused trial-within-a-trial resumes
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The attempted murder trial against Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala and his co-accused returns to court on Monday, with the trial-within-a-trial set to resume.

The State is expected to either close its case or call another witness.

The proceedings have centred on the circumstances surrounding the arrest of alleged hitman Musa Kekana in April 2024.

Last week, the spotlight was firmly on the conduct of police officers involved in the arrest.

The defence has accused police of tailoring their evidence and has questioned the credibility of their accounts of what happened that day.

Kekana, meanwhile, alleges that he was assaulted and suffocated by police during his arrest.

His lawyers are arguing that evidence obtained during and after the arrest should therefore be excluded from the main trial.

World.title: ANC branches protest disputed ward councillor candidate lists
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - ANC members from Tshwane and Johannesburg are marching to Luthuli House, raising objections to the party’s ward councillor candidate lists.

The members allege that the lists do not reflect the outcomes of voting processes held at their branches. They are also accusing some officials of fraudulently compiling the candidate lists.

The protesting branches are calling for urgent talks with the office of ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula and the party’s provincial leadership.

The dispute comes as the ANC prepares for a legal battle with the Independent Electoral Commission over its candidate lists.

The party missed the deadline to submit some of its candidate lists. The ANC has blamed the delay on a glitch in the IEC’s electronic system.

The IEC, however, disputes this explanation, maintaining that its system did not experience a failure.

World.title: Fear grips Kempton Park as police investigate deaths of four women
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng police are investigating possible links between the deaths of four women whose bodies have been discovered in the Kempton Park area over the past two months.

Concerns have intensified following the discovery of another unidentified woman’s body in Rhodesfield on Saturday night.

The development comes as police step up efforts to find missing jogger Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, who disappeared last week after leaving her home for an afternoon run.

Moselakgomo’s disappearance has added urgency to the investigation, as police work to establish whether the body found in Rhodesfield could be connected to the other cases.

Her family visited the scene where the body was found and is expected to assist police with the identification process this morning.

Investigators are now working to establish the identity of the woman and determine the circumstances surrounding her death, including whether it is linked to the other cases.

The investigation remains ongoing, with police expected to provide further details as efforts to identify the woman and locate Moselakgomo continue.

World.title: Zverev holds off Shelton to win US Open title
World.content:
NEW YORK - Alexander Zverev held off Ben Shelton to win the US Open on Sunday, capturing the second Grand Slam of his career just months after winning the French Open.

The top-seeded German ruthlessly snuffed out a late surge by Shelton to triumph 6-3, 7-6 (7/2), 5-7, 6-2, crushing the eighth seed's hopes of becoming the first US man in 23 years to win a Grand Slam title.

Zverev expunged the bitter memory of his 2020 US Open defeat, when he was two points from victory before falling to Dominic Thiem in five sets.

It would be six years -- with two major finals disappointments -- before he would break through this season.

"I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said at the trophy presentation.

The 23-year-old Shelton was one month shy of his first birthday when Andy Roddick hoisted the 2003 US Open trophy in the last major triumph for a US man.

Hopes were high that Shelton could end the drought after his epic five-set quarter-final victory over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, and a come-from-behind win over compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals.

But Zverev's all-court excellence proved too much for Shelton, despite the support of a star-studded Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd trying to will the American to victory.

World.title: US hosts G20 'energy abundance' talks amid Iran war shock
World.content:
HOUSTON - The United States on Monday kicks off a set of G20 meetings touting "energy abundance," even as President Donald Trump's war against Iran continues to disrupt global fuel markets.

The discussions are slated to run through Wednesday in Houston, in the oil-rich US state of Texas.

The meetings gather delegations from the world's largest economies -- including China, India, Japan and Germany -- with major oil producers set to attend, such as Canada and Saudi Arabia.

Russian diplomats indicated Saturday that Moscow would also send some officials.

The unexpected presence of Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov caused a stir at a previous G20 meeting two weeks ago.

Ukraine's European allies expressed disappointment in the US decision to invite Russia, which ran against efforts to exclude Moscow over the war on its neighbour.

The Houston meetings come as oil and gas prices surge over the Middle East war, with Europe struggling to fill its gas storage facilities ahead of winter.

One of Washington's stated priorities as G20 host is to expand access to affordable, reliable and secure energy, but supply has been dramatically impacted since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Prices at the pump have skyrocketed in the United States, where the price of a gallon (3.78 liters) of diesel has hit a record high, and now runs an average $6.20, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).

Regular gasoline is also 44 percent more expensive than it was before the war.

The unpopular war and its consequences have Trump's Republican Party fearing a defeat in the November midterm elections.

The US president has accused Iran of extending the conflict to hurt him politically, claiming recently that the war would end "immediately" after the election.

Trump also accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of causing a diesel shortage with strikes on Russian refineries.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, a key player in Washington's energy dealings with Venezuela, and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum are expected to attend the meetings in Houston.

World.title: DC's Kennedy Center faces bankruptcy, closure: media
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Leaders of the Kennedy Center who have sought to add President Donald Trump's name to the storied institution say it is facing bankruptcy and possible closure in days, the Washington Post reported on Sunday.

According to documents obtained by the paper, the centre's board of trustees is expected to vote Tuesday on whether to close the main building of Washington's performing arts centre, due to financial and safety needs.

Officials warn in the documents that the centre "could be unable to make payroll or pay routine maintenance contracts" within weeks, the Post reported.

Publicly recognising Trump at the centre, they argue in the 57-page pre-meeting packet, would help ensure fundraising help to keep it afloat.

"Trustees are being asked to choose among 10 texts that could be placed on the building's exterior beneath its name," to publicly credit Trump with the renovation, the Post reported.

Shortly after beginning his second term, Trump installed himself as chairman of the centre, which is named in honour of late President John F. Kennedy, who championed civil rights before he was assassinated in 1963.

In December, Trump's hand-picked board voted to rename it the "Trump-Kennedy" Center, a move that was later blocked in court.

A host of artists have cancelled concerts at the venue in response to Trump's takeover, and US media reported that Kennedy Center ticket sales had plummeted to their lowest levels since the Covid pandemic.

The Post reported the center was slated to collect about $124 million of the projected $220 million in revenue that it had budgeted, "leaving a roughly $23 million deficit even after substantial spending cuts" this past fiscal year.

Additionally, the building itself was damaged in a severe storm earlier this month, when a "roughly four-by-five-foot section of ceiling plaster broke loose in the Grand Foyer and fell about 60 feet," the Post reported, among other needed repairs.

Asked about the Post's reporting, the Kennedy Center declined to comment and referred AFP to a recent statement from spokesperson Roma Daravi blaming "decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership."

"Adding Chairman President Trump's name to the building attracted new donors and was crucial to raising additional funds for the Center's renovation," a spokesperson, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP.

World.title: Sweden's election too close to call as far right loses ground
World.content:
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's general election was too close to call early Monday, as the incumbent prime minister and the left-wing opposition leader both said they were ready to govern and the far right was seen losing ground.

With almost 90 percent of votes counted, four opposition parties led by Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson, held a one-seat majority in the 349-seat parliament over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing alliance, which includes the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats.

"For now, we are in the lead. And if that is confirmed, Sweden will have a new government," 59-year-old Andersson, who was Sweden's first woman prime minister in 2021-2022, told her supporters.

But her party -- which ruled the Scandinavian country for most of the 20th century and remains Sweden's largest -- also looked to be heading for its worst score in over a century with 28 percent of the vote.

Outgoing prime minister Kristersson, whose Moderate Party was credited with 19.9 percent of the counted votes, meanwhile said that if the result stood, he would respect Andersson's attempts to try to form a government with the three other parties on the left.

But he noted that the four had irreconcilable differences, primarily between the Left Party and the Centre Party, and were unlikely to agree on a government programme.

"I will therefore, even if tonight's result stands, examine whether there are any possibilities within this non-socialist parliamentary majority to find some workable government constellation," Kristersson told his supporters.

"Which government is going to govern Sweden in the coming years is still an open question," Kristersson declared.

In a big surprise, the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats, which entered parliament in 2010, lost support for the first time, garnering 17.6 percent of the vote, down from 20.5 percent in 2022.

"We don't yet have the full election result, but it's obvious that we've lost a few percentage points compared with our result four years ago," party leader Jimmie Akesson told an election night watch party.

World.title: Nairobi captured: Sifuna storms city in bold show of strength
World.content:
Linda Mwanachi Presidential candidate Edwin Sifuna,address his supporters on September 13th 2026 at Jacaranda grounds in Nairobi,during Linda Mwanachi rally in City. [Edward Kiplimo,Standard]

Nairobi on Sunday offered the clearest sign yet of Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s bid to emerge as a major opposition force, as the Linda Mwananchi movement turned the capital into a stage for an open challenge to President William Ruto ahead of the 2027 General Election.

From All Saints Cathedral to Jacaranda Grounds, it was a sea of humanity as thousands of supporters followed the Nairobi Senator and his Linda Mwananchi team through the city in a largely peaceful procession, chanting his name and cheering his declaration that he is ready to become Kenya’s sixth President.
