World.title: Japan scandal-hit nuclear plant operator head to resign: reports
World.content:
The president of a Japanese nuclear plant operator will step down following a quake data-tampering scandal, local media reported on Monday (September 14, 2026), with the firm expected to abandon plans to restart two reactors.

Japan is moving to revive nuclear power 15 years after an enormous earthquake and tsunami sent reactors at the Fukushima atomic plant into meltdown in 2011.

Chubu Electric Power's Hamaoka nuclear plant — located in an area of central Japan at risk of a potential "megaquake" — has been undergoing regulatory safety checks, with the aim of restarting two reactors.

But in January, the operator said that it had submitted data to regulators that underestimated earthquake risks.

Public broadcaster NHK and other local media said that president Kingo Hayashi and chairman Satoru Katsuno will step down.

The company is reportedly holding a press conference later in the day. The firm was not immediately available for comment.

A 250-page report by an independent panel, released on Monday (September 14, 2026), said the management's "reprimand" over delays in the restart review had created pressure on staff, and was "one of the factors contributing to the misconduct".

The Nikkei business daily reported that the company will withdraw its application for the review process.

Japan pulled the plug on nuclear power in the wake of the meltdown at the Fukushima atomic plant.

However, the resource-poor nation now wants to revive atomic energy to reduce its heavy dependence on fossil fuels, achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and meet growing energy needs from artificial intelligence.

The world's biggest nuclear plant, Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, restarted operations earlier this year.

The estimate of maximum seismic ground motion is important for the earthquake-resistant design of nuclear plants.

In September 2023 the Nuclear Regulation Authority approved Chubu's estimate of 1,200 gal, a unit of acceleration used to measure the intensity of quakes.

But in February last year the NRA received information about possible data fraud from a whistleblower.

The NRA suspended its safety review process for the Hamaoka plant in late December.

The plant is located in Omaezaki, Shizuoka prefecture, near a seismic fault line where a massive Pacific earthquake is expected to occur in the coming years or decades.

In 2024, the Japan Meteorological Agency issued its first special advisory for a possible "megaquake" in the area, known as the Nankai Trough, before lifting it a week later.

World.title: West Bengal government issues closure notice to 252 unaided and unrecognised madrasas
World.content:
The West Bengalgovernment has issued closure notices to 252 unaided and unrecognised madrasas. Another hundred similar madrasas have received show-cause notices and may face closure if they fail to explain the irregularities and answer the queries.

“A survey was conducted through district administration across 22 districts and in Kolkata. Details of teachers, students, infrastructure and funds available was inspected by a special team on the basis of which 252 madrasahs have been closed in the first phase,” said Kshudiram Tudu, Minister for Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education.

Unrecognised and unaided madrasahs are commonly called Khariji Madrasahs; they are independent Islamic educational institutions that operate without government funding, formal recognition, or official regulatory control. Of the madrasas that have been given closure notice, 44 of these are located in Malda, 37 in Uttar Dinajpur, 32 in South 24 Parganas, and 25 each in Nadia and Murshidabad.

Soon after coming to power, the Suvendu Adhikari government had ordered a survey of the Khariji madrasas. There are over 2000 such madrasas in the State. There are hundreds of State-aided and recognised madrasas in the State which are administered by the West Bengal Board of Madrasah Education. The Madrasah Education system in Bengal has a history of almost 250 years, and it grew and flourished with the foundation of the Calcutta Madrasah in 1780 by the British East India Company .

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had earlier this month said that there will be a ‘One State, One Education' policy in West Bengal. Mr. Adhikari said that Aliah University, which was under the Madrasah Education Ministry, has been brought under the Higher Education Ministry.

Several leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party, including the president of the State unit of the party, Samik Bhattacharya, welcomed the move by the West Bengal government. Mr. Bhattacharya said that former West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee had pointed out that extremist elements were promoted through madrasas but later had to retract under pressure from the Left Front.

The State BJP president also added that in a State there cannot be two forms of education.

“India is a secular country. In this country, there is no discrimination among people based on religion. Therefore, it is extremely essential to ensure equal opportunities, equal rights, and a uniform standard of the education system for every child in the country,” the BJP leader posted on social media.

Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh said that the BJP leaders' claim that extremists are found in madrasahs and are targeting an existing education system is not correct. The Mamata Banerjee loyalist MLA said that there is a tradition of giving education through ‘Sanskrit Tols’ as well.

World.title: Dalits counter BJP protest in T. Narsipur over Ganesha procession
World.content:
Tension prevailed in T. Narsipur town near here on Sunday as BJP leaders and supporters staged a protest against the town police inspector’s remarks during a peace meeting ahead of the Ganesha procession, while a counter-protest was also staged by Dalit organisations against former MP Pratap Simha’s allegedly fomenting communal trouble remarks.

Superintendent of Mysuru district police Mallikarjuna Baladandi, who visited T. Narsipur to supervise security arrangements, said additional forces had been deployed in the town to maintain law and order in view of the protests.

T. Narsipur town police inspector Dhananjaya’s reported warning to the processionists against bursting crackers in front of the mosque on Link Road in the town had sparked a strong response from the BJP, with Mr. Pratap Simha allegedly threatening to storm the police station in protest against the police inspector’s remarks.

As BJP leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok and Mysuru MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, made their way to T. Narsipur town on Sunday, a group of Dalit activists sporting Jai Bheem flags and blue shawls gathered near the police station and shouted slogans against Mr. Simha.

The activists of the Dalit groups accused the former MP of deliberately spreading communal poison in T. Narsipur with his allegedly inflammatory statements. The police managed to swiftly disperse them.

Meanwhile, BJP supporters gathered in the town and started raising slogans in support of Mr. Pratap Simha and against the town police inspector.

Mr. Ashok, who arrived in the town, criticised the Congress government for imposing restrictions on the celebration of the Ganesha festival in different parts of the State while addressing the large gathering of BJP supporters. He also sought action against the police inspector for threatening the groups celebrating the Ganesha festival.

Mr. Pratap Simha too addressed the crowd of BJP supporters gathered in the town to protest against the police inspector’s warning.

The police later arrested BJP leaders, including Mr. Ashok. They were subsequently released.

Meanwhile, Mr. Baladandi said the police inspector of the town had convened a peace meeting on September 7 and asked various groups installing Ganesha idols to inform the police about the date of the immersion to ensure proper security arrangements along the route.

As one group had taken out the Ganesha procession without intimating the police last year, no security could be provided for the procession, which also passed through a mosque. Hence, the police inspector asked the group not to take out the procession unilaterally without informing the police.

About 15 to 20 Ganesha pandals are put up in T. Narsipur town every year, and there is no restriction on the processions. The processions can be taken out on the same route this year as well. The police have imposed no restrictions, he clarified.

However, he regretted that the police inspector’s statement was being shown in a “different” manner on social media. He said necessary instructions had also been issued to police officials against issuing statements that could create confusion in the minds of the public.

World.title: Aland MLA B.R. Patil flags lapses in crop insurance disbursement in Karnataka
World.content:
Aland MLA B.R. Patil has alleged serious lapses in disbursing crop insurance claims under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), accusing officials of failing to follow prescribed guidelines and causing hardship to farmers.

Addressing a press conference in Kalaburagi on September 13, Mr. Patil said Aland taluk had only three agriculture officers, resulting in inadequate service to farmers. He alleged that lapses by village accountants had denied insurance benefits to several eligible farmers while the tahsildar tried to defend the officials involved.

He urged the administration to conduct gram sabhas to hear farmers’ grievances and ensure their timely resolution. The legislator said that farmers in the taluk were aware of the insurance scheme and had been paying premiums voluntarily. Many had borrowed money to purchase seeds and undertake cultivation; failure to release insurance claims on time in such circumstances is a matter of serious concern, he said

Mr. Patil said nearly ₹300 crore had been sanctioned under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana scheme, but the entire amount had not reached farmers. He cited Hadalagi and Yelasangi villages as examples, questioning why claims had been settled in one village but not the other despite similar circumstances. He sought a review of the entire process and urged the Deputy Commissioner to take stringent action against intermediaries, if found to be interfering with the claims process.

He alleged negligence and corruption among some field-level officials and called for the appointment of agriculture graduates for effective implementation of the scheme. Deploying inadequately trained staff with lower qualifications was affecting the delivery of benefits to farmers, he said.

Mr. Patil said the Agriculture Department had faced a shortage of officers for nearly three decades, adversely affecting its functioning.

Advocate and consumer activist Vaijnath Zhalki was present at the press conference.

World.title: Historic first Ganga Aarti held on River Thames in UK
World.content:
Thousands gathered on the banks of the River Thames on Sunday (September 13, 2026) for the first-ever Ganga Aarti, a ceremony of light and thanksgiving, in London.

'Ganga Aarti on the Thames: A Ceremony of Light' was organised by Chinmaya Mission UK in collaboration with the annual 'Totally Thames' festival, as part of the global celebrations marking 75 years of the charity. Recreating ethos of the world-famous aarti by the River Ganges in India, the event in London was conceived as a symbol of the life-giving flow of nature, knowledge and consciousness.

"For generations, communities have gathered on the banks of Ganga to offer light in gratitude for the river, for nature and for all that sustains life," said Brahmacharini Shripriya Chaitanya, Resident Teacher of Chinmaya Mission UK.

"Ganga Aarti on the Thames carries that same spirit, bringing people together in a shared moment of gratitude, hope and unity," she said.

Chaitanya explained that for the Chinmaya Mission, the River Ganges also symbolises the flow of knowledge.

"Our founder, Swami Chinmayananda, dedicated his life to bringing the timeless wisdom of Vedanta -- one of the great philosophical traditions of Hinduism -- from the Himalayas into people's everyday lives. As we mark 75 years of Chinmaya Mission, this event is also a celebration of that legacy: of knowledge, service and gratitude flowing beyond boundaries," she said.

The aarti, a traditional Hindu ceremony of gratitude involving large multi-tiered oil lamps, prayer, music and chanting, is an expression of reverence for the river and wider gratitude for Mother Nature.

"Reverence for nature is not simply an additional theme of Ganga Aarti. The ceremony itself is an expression of gratitude towards Mother Ganga, honoured in Hindu tradition as sacred, life-giving and sustaining," said a Chinmaya Mission spokesperson.

The aarti by the Thames took place entirely on land, with nothing from the ceremony placed, poured or released into the Thames.

"The ceremonial lamps will remain on the riverbank rather than being floated on the water, allowing us to honour the spirit of the tradition while ensuring the Thames remains undisturbed. That same principle extends across the event, with measures to minimise waste, reduce single-use plastics and ensure the site and surrounding environment are treated responsibly," the spokesperson said.

Accompanied by music and chanting against the backdrop of the historic Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich, the event brought together senior spiritual leaders and representatives from Hindu organisations and communities across the UK.

It was intended as a wider celebration for the British Hindu and South Asian community and an invitation to people of all backgrounds to come together in gratitude and reverence for nature.

"At its heart, Ganga Aarti reminds us not to take the natural world for granted. Gratitude towards nature should be expressed not only through prayer, but through the care and responsibility with which we treat the environment around us," Chinmaya Mission UK said.

Chinmaya Mission is a global movement, founded in 1951, dedicated to inner transformation and spiritual awakening, rooted in the timeless wisdom of Vedanta and inspired by the vision of Pujya Gurudev Swami Chinmayananda.

Today, the Mission has more than 350 locations worldwide, supporting communities through spiritual education, cultural programmes, academic institutions and service initiatives. In the UK, Chinmaya Mission UK offers programmes for every stage of life: from children and teenagers to young adults, families and senior citizens.

Totally Thames, organised by a trust, is a festival to celebrate the River Thames through arts events, environmental initiatives, heritage and education programmes since 1997. The sell-out first-ever Ganga Aarti event as part of its programme this year is likely to lead to a more regular feature annually.

World.title: Pakistan’s westward turn — strategic depth or overstretch
World.content:
The defence cooperation agreement signed by Pakistan and Kuwait on August 27, 2026, is the latest manifestation of Pakistan’s rapidly expanding strategic footprint in West Asia. The agreement assumes greater significance when viewed alongside Pakistan’s membership of the Saudi Arabia-Türkiye-Pakistan defence arrangement and its recent role as an intermediary between Iran and the United States.

Pakistan’s West Asian orientation has deep historical roots. From its inception, it attempted to combine its South Asian geopolitical identity with that of a major Muslim power. During the Cold War, Pakistan, Iran and Türkiye were linked through the Central Treaty Organization (CENTO) and subsequently through the Regional Cooperation for Development.

World.title: Gadkari delayed by Mumbai traffic by nearly an hour, pitches new technology to replace ageing flyovers
World.content:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari arrived nearly an hour late for an event in Mumbai after getting caught in the city’s traffic, an experience he used to acknowledge the limitations of infrastructure built during his own tenure as Maharashtra’s public works Minister and call for ageing flyovers to be replaced using newer technology.

Mr. Gadkari was travelling from Worli to attend the 22nd Indo-American Corporate Excellence Awards in Mumbai when he was delayed in traffic. Addressing the gathering after reaching the venue, he pointed to his delayed arrival before turning to Mumbai’s larger congestion problem.

“Today I got late by an hour,” Mr. Gadkari said, before joking that he was “paying for my mistake” — a reference to the road infrastructure developed when he was Maharashtra’s PWD Minister in the 1990s.

The event, held on September 11, was organised by the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce’s West India Council to recognise companies and business leaders contributing to India-U.S. trade and economic ties. Mr. Gadkari attended as the chief guest, while YES Bank MD and CEO Vinay Tonse was the guest of honour. Thirteen award winners were felicitated at the event.

Mr. Gadkari recalled that during his tenure in Maharashtra, he had been involved in the development of 55 flyovers in Mumbai, as well as major road infrastructure projects including the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and planning associated with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link.

However, he said the technology available at the time was different from what is available today and suggested that some of Mumbai’s older flyovers were no longer adequate for the sharp increase in traffic volumes.

The Minister said he had discussed the issue with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and suggested that ageing flyovers be replaced with structures using newer technology rather than continuing with conventional designs.

As an example, Mr. Gadkari referred to infrastructure being planned in Pune, where he said multi-level structures could accommodate different modes of transport vertically — with roads constructed at different levels and a Metro corridor above them. He said projects worth around ₹50,000 crore were being considered in Pune and referred to technology brought from Malaysia for such structures.

His remarks came against the backdrop of Mumbai’s continuing struggle with road congestion despite decades of investment in flyovers, elevated roads, coastal connectivity and public transport. Mr. Gadkari’s own delayed journey on Friday (September 11) became an illustration of the challenge, with the minister arguing that cities would increasingly have to use newer engineering solutions to add transport capacity within limited available space.

Mr. Gadkari also used his address to emphasise greater cooperation between India and the United States, saying India’s engineering and entrepreneurial capabilities could be combined with American technology and resources to create a “win-win” situation.

The awards ceremony brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs and industry representatives from the Indo-U.S. business community and was aimed at recognising contributions to bilateral trade, innovation and economic cooperation.

World.title: Waterlogging, poor drainage have halted industrial activity in West Bengal Panihati municipality for months
World.content:
After every moderate shower during the monsoons, there is ankle-deep water outside the main gate of Texmaco Rail & Engineering Ltd. located at Panihati Municipality in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas.

Texmaco is a multi-unit engineering and infrastructure company. When the correspondent visited its unit at Panihati in the first week of September, there was ankle-deep water extending up to 500 meters from the main gate of the company.

Texmaco Rail and Engineering Limited submerged the pavements and the ground floor of a small office inside the gate. The security guards present at the gate were seen wearing gumboots and rolling their pants up to their knees to avoid the water. Texmaco shut down six units operating in Panihati for a month in the last two years. In mid-August this year, they also closed the units again for a week due to heavy rain. It took about five to six days for the area to dry out again. Approximately 6,500 laborers work in their factories.

A similar situation was also seen at Swalka Kel Pvt. Limited and Jindal Group Pipe Manufacturing Plant, which are located a few metres away from Texmaco in Panihati’s Nilgunj area.

Several shops at the Sen Bajar market near the Panihati Railway Station were also shut for the last two days after a shower. Even as the monsoon are receding there is knee deep water in the market.

Some sellers arranged an extra table and chair to keep the vegetables and fish off the water that submerged the floors of their shops. Several shop owners also complained that they barely get any customer when the roads are waterlogged.

“The waterlogging is resulting in severe losses for us. I have been living here for the last 50 years. The situation was not as bad earlier; it has deteriorated in the last one or two decades. The market association has approached the municipality several times, but nothing has been done,” said Deepak Saha, the secretary of the Sen Bajar shopowners’ association.

Sudipta Mukherjee, the MD of Texmaco admitted that work for several units of the company remains suspended for weeks due to waterlogging.

“Even a minimal amount of rain can cause issues. In August of this year, the units were closed for a week after rainfall. Before this, we had to close the units for over a month due to waterlogging,” Mr. Mukherjee said. He added that the company employs about 6,500 people in Panihati. According to Mr. Mukherjee, the company has taken steps on its part and started projects, including rainwater harvesting, which has eased the situation a bit.

Panihati Municipality, located about 20 km from Kolkata on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, has 35 wards, and more than half of the wards are affected by waterlogging during the monsoon. Over a dozen wards in the civic body remain submerged for months, including wards 23, 24, 25, 26, and 31.

Debasish Dutta, local activist and resident of ward number 23 in the Ramchandrapur Sodepur area of Panihati Municipality has been running from pillar to post for the past several years so that the authorities take note of the problem of waterlogging

“I have sent several letters and communications to leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Minister for Urban Development Agnimitra Paul, but to no avail. I suffered attacks during the previous regime when I kept protesting and highlighting the issue of waterlogging,” Mr. Dutta said.

The activist said his house and the residence of thousands of people in Panihati lies submerged for months and there is nobody to take note of the issue. Many other residents of the area have claimed that illegal construction, encroachment on railway land and lack of any sewage management has made the situation worse with every passing monsoon.

Like several other civic bodies of the State, the local councillors of Panihati Municipality have resigned and the municipality is run by an administrator.

Reacting to the matter, a senior officer from the Urban Development Department said that a detailed report was sought from the Panihati Municipality last month on the situation of the drainage system in Panihati. “We are reviewing the situation. A report is also being prepared. Necessary steps will be taken,” said a senior engineer from the municipality.

Mr. Dutta has recently written to advisor of the Chief Minister of West Bengal, Subrata Gupta, seeking an appointment to discuss the situation with a group of representatives as well business men from Panihati.

“The BJP government wants to revive West Bengal as a destination of industries, however existing industrial units are having to suspend operation due to water logging and Panihati is a prime example of that civic mess,” he said.

World.title: New provinces debate may take eight months, says PM’s aide
World.content:
LAHORE: Prime Minis­ter’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah Khan has said any move to create new provinces is still at an early stage and may take six to eight months to go through parliament and its committees, making it clear that his party PML-N has not initiated the project.

Speaking at a meeting with journalists here on Sunday, he said that if a proposal for new provinces was formally brought before parliament, every political party and member would have an opportunity to express an opinion.

He said the matter could then be referred to a parliamentary or standing committee for detailed consideration.

“There is still a lot of time before the issue of provincial division comes before parliament,” he said, adding that the debate could ultimately produce proposals for new administrative units or lead to discussion on local government elections.

The PML-N leader questioned the decision to initiate the debate at an economic forum, saying such a platform was not meant for launching projects involving major constitutional and political changes.

“Those behind the project may have spoken to the PML-N, but if we have not introduced it, it does not mean we should stand against it with a stick,” he said.

He made it clear that no major proposal favouring the division of provinces had emerged from the PML-N. “When the PML-N has not started this project, you should understand what our line is,” he remarked.

On the question of Bahawalpur (division), he said the PML-N’s local leadership in Punjab did not want the region to be included in a proposed South Punjab province. He said some within the party favoured a separate Bahawalpur province, while others wanted it to remain linked with Lahore.

He said the Pakistan Peoples Party had benefited politically from the debate over provincial division because its workers had become emotionally aligned with the issue.

Referring to the controversial canal project, he said President Asif Ali Zardari had supported its construction but the PPP subsequently mobilised public opposition that resulted in the project being halted.

Asked about reports of back-channel contacts with PTI founder Imran Khan, Rana Sana said there might be behind-the-scenes communication, but “there is a price” for adopting such a course and whoever chose it would have to pay that price.

Regarding differences involving the federal interior minister, Rana Sana said the minister could be asked for an explanation when he spoke in the cabinet or Senate. He said Federal Minister Sheikh Qaiser met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif every other day in his presence and that he did not understand his claim of not having met the premier.

“Some matters are meant for deliberation. Everything should not be made public,” he said.

The meeting was attended by Punjab Assembly Chief Whip Rana Muhammad Arshad and PML-N leaders Zubair Gul, Rana Imran, Ghulam Mustafa and Dr Saeed Elahi, besides senior journalists Mujeebur Rehman Shami, Sohail Warraich, Saleem Bukhari, Hafizullah Niazi, Naveed Chaudhry, Pervez Bashir, Mansoor Ali Khan, Salman Ghani and others.

Published in Dawn, September 14th, 2026

World.title: Winners India refuse to collect Women’s Asia Cup trophy from ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi
World.content:
India again refused to accept a tournament trophy from Asian Cricket Council President Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday, with their women’s team this time throwing the closing ceremony into uncertainty and delay.

The trophy presentation at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium was delayed by more than half an hour after India secured a 72-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final, Hindustan Times reported.

Naqvi, also the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman and the country’s interior minister, stood on the stage as the audience waited for India to collect their trophy.

ESPNCricinfo reported that the presentation ceremony wrapped up “without the Indian team collecting their winners’ medals or the trophy”. Live visuals from the stadium confirmed the same.

However, Sri Lanka’s Chamari Athapaththu picked up the runners-up cheque from Naqvi, the outlet added.

The final ball of the match was done by 9:55pm UAE time (10:55pm PKT), and by 10:30pm (11:30pm PKT), there were “no signs of the presentation ceremony starting”, Hindustan Times noted.

The outlet pointed out that broadcasters interviewed Indian skipper Harmanpreet Kaur “immediately”, even though the interview is usually kept for the end of the presentation ceremony.

Asked whether his team’s refusal to accept the trophy was “pre-decided”, head coach Amol Muzumdar said the “stand has been taken by the BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India), and we stand by it”.

“For us, this tournament is over. We are the champions; that’s good enough. It was on the big board that India are the champions of Asia Cup 2026,” he told a post-match press conference in Dubai.

Asked whether the trophy will end with the same fate as the men’s trophy from last year, Muzumdar said, “No news as yet. So I cannot answer that.”

On a query about the decision impacting sportsmanship, the coach reiterated that the team stood by the BCCI’s stance and that the tournament was “officially over” for them.

Sunday’s scenes illustrated a replay of the events of October last year, when India refused to collect the trophy at the closing ceremony of the Men’s Asia Cup final as tensions from their May 2025 military conflict spilt over into the cricket field.

At the time, India had beaten Pakistan by five wickets, but they caused the post-final formalities to be inordinately delayed due to their refusal to budge from their stance.

There were also no customary handshakes between the teams after India refused to do so, with tensions high from their previous two clashes in the competition, which witnessed political posturing and aggressive on-field behaviour.

‘Destroying the sports culture’

Reacting to the development, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said India’s “diplomatic defeat and military defeat will not be erased” by refusing to accept the trophy.

Speaking to Geo News, he slammed India for “destroying the sports culture”. “Sports spirit matters. If you do not have that spirit, then victory or defeat means nothing,” he added.

Chaudhry said New Delhi had “filled jingoism in their entire nation”. “Our sports culture, which was a symbol of peace and love and which ended many wars, has been eroded.”

The state minister asserted that Pakistan had not “politicised” sports or made it the target of conflict between the two countries, and was open to dialogue on “every controversial issue”.

The finale

Shree Charani’s fantastic four-wicket haul helped India crush Sri Lanka by 72 runs to lift the Asia Cup title for the eighth time.

Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma both towered the innings with 59 and 68 runs, respectively, as the Indian team managed to post 185 runs on the board in the allotted 20 overs with five wickets to spare.

Charani, outracing Deepti Sharma, who grabbed three wickets, dismantled the Sri Lankan lineup, with only Athapaththu, Vishmi Gunaratne, and Nilakshi de Silva entering the double figures.

Athapaththu, after scoring 36 off 32 balls, emerged as the top run-getter for outclassed Sri Lanka.

Kaur maintained that India played to their standard.

“We know they are a great team. But we played to our standards. We set high standards for ourselves, and we wanted to keep matching them.

“Very happy with the way we all performed. The openers did a great job for us. The way Shafali and Smriti bat like they did. Great to see someone like Shafali take responsibility through the tournament with the bat and ball,” she said.

In her comments, the Sri Lankan skipper said they will “bounce back” for the upcoming Asian Games.

“This is the part of the game: one team wins, one team loses. But at the end of the day, we did not play our best game in all three departments. They played very well. But we will bounce back,” Athapaththu said in a post-match talk.

“We played really good cricket throughout the tournament, but today we struggled a little bit,” she added.

World.title: New constitutional scheme for GB on the anvil
World.content:
• PM’s committee to meet before September-end to build consensus on proposals

• Delayed annual budget for FY2026-27 to be tabled today as region faces financial shortfall

GILGIT: The federal government is consulting stakeholders on a constitutional arrangement for Gilgit-Baltistan with Pakistan, while the region’s deficit budget for fiscal year 2026-27 will be presented in its parliament on Monday (today).

Responding to questions from Gilgit-Baltistan Asse­mbly members during its session on Saturday, Chief Minister Advocate Amjad Hussain said the constitutional status of GB was being discussed at a high level.

A high-level committee, constituted by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, is working to develop consensus on the arrangement through a constitutional amendment.

“A committee has been for­med, and we hope that we will reach a consensus,” he said.

“We expect the meeting to take place on Sept 25 or 26. If we succeed in achieving consensus during that meeting, then all the questions related to constitutional matters of GB will be addressed,” he added.

Sources said the high-level committee, formed by PM Shehbaz in July and chaired by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, would meet in Islamabad on Sept 25 and 26 to review political and administrative reforms in GB.

Other members of the committee include the GB chief minister, Leader of the Opposition in the GB Assembly Hafiz Hafeezur Rehman, Federal Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Minister Amir Muqam, the attorney general for Pakistan, as well as representatives of the ministries of foreign affairs, law and justice, and inter-provincial coordination.

An informed official told Dawn that the meeting would also endeavour to achieve consensus among stakeholders on preparing a draft amendment bill for GB’s fresh constitutional arrangement with Pakistan without affecting the Kashmir dispute with India.

The committee has been tasked with submitting its recommendations to the prime minister within a month.

It has held various rounds of meetings to deliberate on the political, administrative and financial issues of the region.

The body has recommended a financial agreement between the federal and GB governments, similar to the one between the Centre and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), until the constitutional status of the region is determined.

The GB cabinet has already approved the proposal and the region’s parliament recently endorsed it.

The GB chief minister and opposition leader are also expected to attend the meeting. The committee has already discussed the legal and constitutional implications of the move.

Delayed budget

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Hussain announced in a statement that the delayed budget for fiscal year 2026-27 would be tabled in the GB Assembly for approval on Monday. He added that the non-development budget for GB had also been almost finalised.

In July, the GB government presented a Rs20.478 billion interim budget for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 and announced that the full budget would be presented after three months.

“We have given all members a share in the budget on an equal basis for the first time,” the CM explained in the statement.

“We have not carried out any discrimination on the basis of political affiliation of any member. The funds allocated for development schemes in all constituencies [are] on an equal basis.”

Mr Hussain said the budget would focus on social-sector development. “Funds have been allocated for those segments of society that normally do not benefit much from the budget,” he added.

He said funds had also been allocated for the development of women and youth to generate economic activities for them.

He explained that the GB government would have to present a deficit budget as it did not have the required resources.

He said negotiations were underway with the Centre to overcome the GB government’s financial crisis.

“We can’t wait for the completion of those negotiations and delay the budget any further,” he added.

The CM said the GB government was trying to secure as much as possible from the federal government.

He said the GB government had demanded a share in the National Finance Commission (NFC) award and that the prime minister also favoured the move.

However, the federal finance ministry’s stance is that a constitutional amendment would be required for an NFC share for GB.

“Until the NFC share is ensured for GB, there must still be some mechanism through which the region can function. We cannot continue under the existing arrangement indefinitely,” he added.

CM Hussain said the GB government had requested the federal government to make a financial agreement with the region similar to that with AJK.

Published in Dawn, September 14th, 2026

World.title: Afridi alters tour; security tightened in capital, Punjab
World.content:
• KP CM to visit deceased PTI worker today

• Gatherings of five or more banned across Punjab

• 23,500 cops sought for Islamabad security ahead of Sept 27 sit-in

• Sanaullah warns against violence, terror threat

LAHORE/RAWALPINDI: While Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi has hinted at altering his planned Punjab tour following the demise of a PTI worker, the authorities sprang into action on Sunday with the Centre seeking additional police force from provinces and the Punjab government imposing a ban on gatherings until Sept 17, ahead of the opposition party’s planned march on the federal capital.

The PTI had earlier announced a 13-city Punjab tour for Mr Afridi for rallying supporters ahead of a “decisive peaceful protest march” on Islamabad on Sept 27.

The caravan was scheduled to start from Daud Khel on Monday to reach Faisalabad for an overnight stay after passing through Mianwali City, Wanbachran, Quaidabad, Joharabad, Khushab, Shahpur, Sargodha, Lalian and Chiniot. The caravan was planned to move from Faisalabad towards Lahore, with a brief stop at Sheikhupura.

However, the KP CM said he would visit the residence of the deceased party worker in Lahore first. “Tomorrow, I will go to the home of martyred Ishtiaq Ahmad in Lahore, and after that, I will outline the course of action for the Punjab Street Movement right here in Lahore,” he said.

Ban on gatherings across Punjab

On the other hand, the Punjab home department banned gatherings of five or more people across the province until Sept 17 under Section 144 of criminal procedure code. The order also forbids the carrying or display of weapons in public and prohibits activity deemed to incite unlawful assembly, though it carves out exceptions for weddings, funerals, religious observance and court and government business.

Officials justified the clampdown by citing intelligence suggesting terrorist groups might target large public rallies, saying the aim was to safeguard lives and property rather than to suppress dissent.

The scale of the security operation extends well beyond Punjab. Under a federal directive, Punjab has been told to supply 15,000 police personnel for Islamabad’s security, with Sindh contributing 8,000 and Balochistan 500 with a combined deployment of 23,500 officers due to be in place by Sept 20.

In Rawalpindi, the city’s police chief, Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, has cancelled leave for all officers until October, barring genuine emergencies. The police also drew up a list of 179 PTI figures, including sitting and former lawmakers.

Also, district authorities have issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh.

At the same time, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah during an interaction with journalists in Lahore, alleged the opposition party was planning to bring “armed supporters” into Islamabad.

Also, the PM’s aide warned that terrorists from what he referred to as “India-sponsored Fitna al-Khawarij” might exploit the rally to widen the rift between the public and the state. He predicted the protest would ultimately fail.

PTI’s Punjab information secretary, Shaukat Basra, described a coordinated campaign against its leadership and rank and file, claiming hundreds of workers, including women, had been detained in raids across the province.

Other PTI leaders, too, accused the provincial authorities of using force against party workers during preparations for an Eid Miladun Nabi celebration. They alleged that a heavy police contingent accompanied the funeral procession of PTI worker Ishtiaq Ahmed, who died after remaining under treatment for burn injuries that he suffered during illegal raids by police. They further alleged that funeral prayers for him were conducted hurriedly, preventing some relatives from attending.

Amjad Mahmood in Lahore also contributed to this report

Published in Dawn, September 14th, 2026

World.title: Afghan medical students urge govt to stop their repatriation
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Afghan medical students studying in Pakistani colleges have expressed concern over directives from the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council to return to their country and appealed to the government to allow the already enrolled students to complete their degrees, especially female students, who have no prospects of continuing their education back home.

“Currently, about 1,000 Afghan students, including 350 girls, have been pursuing education in medical and dental colleges in Pakistan. The PMDC’s notification asking us to return to our country has caused unrest among us, particularly female students,” said Anayatullah Momand, final-year MBBS student at the Khyber Medical College.

Mr Momand, spokesperson for Afghan medical students, said an estimated 200 students who have completed their house jobs and are waiting to be enrolled in specialisation programmes were also among those affected.

“The government should allow the currently enrolled students to complete their studies and save their future. We don’t object to Pakistan’s policy of barring Afghans from education here, but the old students should be exempted,” he said.

Say PMDC has asked about 1,000 students to return to their home country

“Our immense concern is female students who, if sent back to Afghanistan, will sit in homes because there is no education for women due to the Taliban ban,” he said.

“All of us had valid visas, and many of the students whose visas had expired have applied for renewal,” he said. According to him, all Afghans have been admitted to colleges on merit. “Some have arrived in Pakistan on scholarship, while others on Afghan national seats reserved by the Pakistan government, and still others are studying under the Pakistan Technical Assistance Programme for Afghans.”

“In a recent meeting, the Afghan ambassador to Pakistan told us that they will give us admission in Afghanistan’s medical and dental colleges in case of our repatriation, but we don’t need Afghan medical degrees, which aren’t recognised internationally,” Mr Momand said.

“We asked the ambassador what the future will be for female students back home and he had no answer,” he said. “The ball is in the court of Pakistan’s government.”

Najma Bibi, a third-year student, said that the danger is not over yet. “Though the Lahore High Court has suspended the PMDC’s directives of July 31 and September 1, which asked the colleges to stop admitting Afghan students, it is a temporary relief,” she said.

Bibi, who is one of the 22 students of King Edwards Medical University, which ordered the Afghan nationals to vacate the campus on Sept 7, said the PMDC should take pity on hundreds of Afghans, especially female students, and reconsider its decision.

“The decision aims to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned women’s education,” said another student on condition of anonymity.

A 3rd-year MBBS student, she came to Pakistan two years ago on the Allama Iqbal Scholarship offered by Pakistan, with the hope to complete her education and serve women back home. “However, these past few months have been like hell, and we still face the risk of eviction from Pakistan,” she said.

A first-year female student said that her dream of becoming a doctor is unlikely to get materialised given the threats they are facing. “Pakistan should realise our problem, as going back can land us in a hard and challenging situation and even we can face prosecution,” she said.

On Sept 1, PMDC had asked the medical and dental colleges that enrolled Afghan students to return to Afghanistan, in accordance with the prevailing policy directions. The institutions concerned shall ensure that necessary administrative formalities, including issuance of the requisite No-Objection Certificate and facilitation of their departure, are completed accordingly, the directive said.

World.title: Arshad Nadeem finishes 5th at World Athletics Ultimate Championship; Sri Lanka's Pathirage steals the show
World.content:
Pakistan’s Olympic gold medallist Arshad Nadeem recorded his season-best throw but still finished fifth at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship at the National Athletics Centre in Budapest on Sunday.

Arshad threw 81.49m on his third attempt, but his effort was well behind Sri Lankan sensation Rumesh Pathirage, who clinched gold with a monstrous 91.09m throw in the fourth round.

Grenada’s Anderson Peters finished second with 86.18m, ahead of Germany’s Julian Weber, who took bronze with 85.89m.

Arshad again did not seem in his groove when he started with a throw of 74.42m. The Mian Chunnu-born athlete improved on his second attempt with 79.66m before making his best throw in his third and final attempt.

Under the competition format, only the top four athletes advance to the decisive fourth round, meaning Arshad’s campaign ended after three throws.

Weber set the pace early with 84.09m on his first attempt. Peters improved on that with 86.18m on his second, while Pathirage, who won Commonwealth gold last month, also threw 85.69m. Weber then improved his own effort to 85.89m.

Pathirage all but secured gold with an attempt of 87.11m before obliterating the field with a 91.09m throw.

The result caps a difficult season for Arshad, who has struggled to reproduce the form that saw him win Olympic gold in Paris with a record-breaking 92.97m throw.

His 2026 campaign began with a ninth-place finish in Switzerland, followed by a disappointing Commonwealth Games outing in Glasgow where he failed to reach the final round with a best of just 77.41m.

With the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya approaching, the men’s javelin final is scheduled for September 28, where Pathirage will be the heavy favourite.

World.title: Mangrove cutting for land reclamation at Karachi's Korangi Creek threatens environment
World.content:
An illegal dyke has been constructed in the heart of a mangrove forest in Korangi Creek, disrupting the natural flow of water and depriving the mangroves on one side of the creek of their essential water supply. As the mangroves dry out and die, they are subsequently cut down by those involved in this illegal reclamation for the sake of land grabbing.—Waqas Ali Ranjha

• Forest dept says illegal activity is taking place on its land, but police refuse to act on ‘sub judice matter’

• Experts warn continued loss of mangrove cover could leave Karachi’s coastal areas more vulnerable to natural hazards

KARACHI: While cutting mangroves for firewood is a common occurrence, encroachers are active in Karachi’s coastal areas, illegally uprooting mangroves to reclaim land, even next to a biodiversity park at Korangi Creek.

The Sindh Forest Department (SFD) confirmed that the illegal activity was being carried out on its land. However, it said police had refused to take action, claiming that the land in question had been allotted by the Board of Revenue and that the matter was sub judice.

Dawn visited the Korangi Creek area and found mangrove cutting and land reclamation taking place alongside the Mangrove Biodiversity Park that was inaugurated by Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab in September last year.

Right beside the erected boundary walls, a large portion of land has been enclosed by an earthen bund to restrict the flow of water towards the mangroves, and the mangroves inside the enclosed area have been cut while their stems are clearly visible in the standing water. In some parts of the bund, a wall is also being erected, while debris has been spread over some of the open area in between, due to which the place is taking the shape of an enclosed plot.

A security guard has also been deputed by some private owners to guard the land in question.

When Dawn approached the SFD in this regard and inquired about the status of the land and the ongoing activity there, the department sent a team to inspect the site.

A senior official of the department said after the inspection that the department was aware of the issue. He said that the land in question belongs to the Forest Department and that such “illegal allotments” were made by the Board of Revenue. The Forest Department, he said, has taken action against such activities several times.

In the current case too, they had attempted to take action and remove the bunds. However, the matter was taken by the other party to a court and, therefore, the police refused to take any further action. “And unless the legal issue is resolved, we can’t act on our own,” he added.

According to the official, the practice had been continuing for several months. He said creating bunds to stop water from reaching the mangroves was one of the techniques being used for a long time. Once the mangroves dried up, he said, the trees could be cut either by local people seeking firewood or by those involved in the encroachment.

The official said the department was making efforts within its mandate to protect the mangroves.

Mangroves serve as a natural barrier against hazards Climate change experts and conservationists have expressed concern over the matter.

Talking to Dawn, Rafiul Haq, a conservationist and climate change expert, said mangrove cutting had been taking place in the said area for some time and that considerable land had already been encroached upon over the past many years.

He warned that continued loss of mangrove cover would leave the coastal area more vulnerable to natural hazards, including tsunamis and hurricanes, as mangroves served as a natural barrier. Therefore, he called for an immediate halt to the cutting of mangroves.

Mr Haq also said Pakistan had adequate laws relating to climate change and environmental protection, but the major problem was their implementation. Influential people, he alleged, were often able to evade the consequences of violations.

Climate change expert Mas­ood Lohar said mangrove cutting was not confined to the area in question and was also taking place at other locations in Kara­chi and along the Indus Delta.

He termed the situation “very concerning” and warned that, in the event of a major tsunami or other coastal disaster, areas including Korangi and DHA could face severe flooding if the natural protection provided by mangroves was lost.

Environmentalist Tariq Alex­ander Qaiser stressed the need for greater vigilance to protect the city’s remaining mangrove and tree cover.

“All existing mangroves need to be protected. They are critical to the health of our city. They and other trees are a primary element in tackling climate change. Karachi cannot afford to lose its remaining green cover,” he told Dawn.

“We need to be more vigilant against such things,” he added.

Published in Dawn, September 14th, 2026

World.title: Major relief package announced for residents of Rawalpindi Cantonment
World.content:
• House, water and sanitation taxes slashed

• 15mgd water from Daducha Dam backed by Rs100m grant to shift tubewells to solar

• package follows talks between public representatives and RCB committee, says MNA

RAWALPINDI: A major relief package was announced on Sunday for the residents of Rawalpindi Cantonment, slashing house, water and sanitation taxes.

The package was announced by Chairman of the National Assembly Standing Committee on Cabinet Division Malik Ibrar Ahmed following successful negotiations between public representatives and a high-level committee of Rawalpindi Cantonment Board (RCB).

Under the revised framework, the residential house tax hike has been curtailed from 30 per cent to 20 per cent, three easy installments have been permitted for tax payments and surcharges on past arrears under the Amendment Act 2023 have been completely waived.

Furthermore, Daducha Dam will supply 15 million gallons per day (MGD) of water to the cantonment backed by a Rs100 million grant to shift tubewells and water storage facilities to solar power.

Addressing a press conference along with MPA Malik Iftikhar Ahmed, former RCB vice president Malik Munir Ahmed, Raja Irfan Imtiaz and former board members Malik Tahir Ayoub, Arshad Mehmood Qureshi, Rasheed Ahmed Khan and others, Malik Ibrar Ahmed expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Field Marshal Asim Munir for initiating the communication and infrastructure projects in Rawalpindi.

He said the completion of the Charing Cross and Qasim Market underpasses in NA-55 will convert the Rawat-to-Tarnol route into a signal-free corridor.

Mr Ahmed said exorbitant increases in municipal taxes had sparked widespread public resentment across all segments of the cantonment population.

Taking cognizance of public concerns, political representatives engaged the RCB administration, prompting the cantonment executive officer to constitute the high-level committee.

The committee held daily consultative sessions with former board members and reached a consensus to roll back the excessive hikes.

Under the agreed terms, the triennial tax revision for 2026-29, initially approved at a flat 30 per cent hike for both residential and commercial units, has been revised to 20 per cent for residential properties while maintaining 30 per cent for commercial units.

He said changes in commercial use will require formal revision notices, and assessment appeals will be officially registered. Taxpayers who cleared dues between 2023 and 2026 will not face retrospective surcharges following committee reassessments, and bills will be issued strictly against current payable amounts.

He said the property owners submitting title deeds, CNIC copies and formal applications will be assigned immediate cantonment board (CB) numbers, while newly-incorporated urban pockets will receive CB numbers and tax liabilities only starting next fiscal year with previous arrears fully written off.

Detailing the revised residential door-to-door sanitation rates, he announced that charges for 1 to 3 marla units had been fixed at Rs2,100 per annum (Rs175 per month), 3 to 5 marla units at Rs3,200 per annum (Rs266 per month) and 5 to 7 marla units at Rs4,400 per annum (Rs366 per month). Annual rates for 7 to 10 marla, 10 to 15 marla and 15 to 20 marla plots stand at Rs5,200, Rs7,000 and Rs10,000, respectively. For commercial properties, multiple categories have been abolished in favour of a flat sanitation levy of 1 per cent of the annual rental value (ARV), aligning with Punjab’s “Suthra Punjab” clean-up model within four months.

Annual water charges have also been revised downward: rates for 1 to 5 marla units were reduced from Rs14,400 to Rs10,800; 5 to 7 marla from Rs20,400 to Rs18,800 and 7 to 10 marla from Rs30,600 to Rs28,000, while 10 to 15 marla and 15 to 20 marla rates were fixed at Rs37,000 and Rs40,000 per annum, respectively.

For tax recovery, the local MNA said authorities must issue a mandatory 30-day notice prior to property sealing with businesses offering essential items exempted under Section 144 such as pharmacies, milk shops, bakeries, butcher shops and green grocers, protected from sealing drives.

Mr Ahmed added that water supplies from Chahan Dam and Daducha Dam will elevate the cantonment’s total clean water output to 50 MGD.

Addressing civic amenities for the cantonment’s 800,000 residents, he confirmed that land designated at Rakh Dhamial by parliamentarians for a public graveyard will soon receive dedicated ambulance and funeral bus services.

He urged residents to visit the operational constituency offices of former RCB members to seek assistance with bill rectifications and municipal concerns.
