World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019014/Pizza Bao, Spaghetti Stir-Fry: Chinese Students Hack Home Cooking Abroad
World.title: Pizza Bao, Spaghetti Stir-Fry: Chinese Students Hack Home Cooking Abroad
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019014/Pizza Bao, Spaghetti Stir-Fry: Chinese Students Hack Home Cooking Abroad
World.content:
Liu Zhenchao stands at a kitchen counter in Germany, filming himself making baozi, or Chinese steamed buns.

The 27-year-old student from Hefei, capital of China’s eastern Anhui province, chops onions and minces beef for the filling, then seasons it and mixes it by hand in a bowl.

But when it comes time to make the dough, he suddenly reaches for a cardboard box from a local supermarket.

Inside is a sheet of premade pizza dough.

“Both pizza dough and traditional baozi dough rely on yeast to ferment,” Liu told Sixth Tone, slicing the dough into neat rounds. “It allows the dough to expand, whether you steam it or bake it.”

Liu’s pizza dough baozi hack soon struck a chord with Chinese students abroad. Viewers called him a “genius,” marveling at a shortcut that eliminated the need to make dough from scratch and cut preparation time in half.

Like Liu, a growing number of Chinese students studying abroad are turning cooking videos into viral hits across Chinese social media. On Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok, the hashtag “international students hunong cooking” — using the term “to do something halfheartedly” — has amassed 2.1 billion views.

The trend dates back to March this year, when a Chinese student in Italy posted a video on how to make gong jin bao dan, or crispy-fried eggs coated with a sweet-and-sour sauce. His recipe tutorial video went viral, garnering more than 2 million likes and triggering a wave of netizens to attempt the dish and share their results online.

Chinese students are the largest overseas student population in the world, with over 570,600 Chinese going abroad in 2025 alone, according to China’s Ministry of Education.

For these students, improvised dishes from back home made with whatever ingredients they can find have become a category of their own, jokingly dubbed the country’s “ninth cuisine” after its eight official regional cuisines.

Comfort food

Liu traces his love of cooking to his childhood, when he spent hours watching cooking programs on TV.

When he arrived in Germany in October 2020 to pursue a master’s in engineering economics, it was only natural that he began cooking his own meals to cut costs; a meal at the school cafeteria cost 6 euros on average, but cooking at home kept his expenses below 5 euros, he said.

The choice was not only about saving money. Liu grew up with dishes known for their rich sauces, bold flavors, and vibrant colors.

The novelty of Western foods quickly wore off after he arrived. “The longer I stayed abroad, the more I found myself craving the familiar tastes of home,” Liu said. “Common Chinese dishes like stir-fried shredded potatoes with green peppers just suit my taste better than cheese and steak.”

Recreating those same flavors, however, was not easy. With many key ingredients unavailable in German supermarkets, he learned to improvise, replacing familiar ingredients from home with local ones. In one recipe, he uses Italian spaghetti in place of Chinese noodles, stir-frying it with green peppers and pork.

For Liu, cooking also had to fit around the intense pressure of studying. During exam periods, he would study from around 9 a.m. until midnight, so cooking had to be quick and simple, while also tasty and authentic.

“Good food is important to me,” Liu said. “During exam periods, when the pressure is already so high, if the food doesn’t turn out well, I feel like I have nothing to look forward to that day.”

When he launched his Douyin account in 2024, he initially wanted just to capture his everyday life abroad. But as he shared more of his life overseas, cooking gradually took center stage.

“I found that cooking is what resonates most with viewers online,” Liu said. He has since attracted more than 780,000 followers.

“Such content also has a particularly powerful sensory appeal,” Hu Zhiwen, a critical food studies scholar with a Ph.D. from the University of Georgia, told Sixth Tone. Images of cooking can trigger memories of smell, taste, and texture, which resonate strongly with audiences, he said.

Food has also become a way for Liu to connect with his contemporaries abroad. He often invites local friends over to try his cooking, including the baozi he made with store-bought pizza dough.

“They found it magical because store-bought pizza dough is something they’ve seen all their lives, yet no one had thought to use it this way,” Liu said. “Some even tried making them at home.”

The food sometimes gives his friends ideas for innovating foods from their own cultures, too. His Italian friends, for example, compared Chinese dumplings to their own filled pastas.

Cooking can offer overseas students a path to independence, emotional comfort, and cross-cultural connection, Hu, the food scholar, noted. “When you are in a new environment, there is a natural desire to seek out things that make life feel more familiar.”

In China, where food is deeply woven into everyday life and regional cuisines offer enormous variety, cooking can be more than a practical necessity, Hu added.

“Chinese students will be particularly drawn to cooking when they move to places where the food culture is markedly different from what they grew up with,” he said.

For Chen Wan’er, cooking abroad was a different kind of challenge. She had barely cooked before leaving China, but after a month in the UK, she was making almost all of her meals herself — and not only for the economic benefits.

In a new country, seven hours away from her family and friends and with no close connections, cooking gave her days meaning and shape. Even when a dish didn’t turn out perfectly, she enjoyed the satisfaction of making something from scratch.

Chen began filming her cooking and posting it on China’s lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote, but unlike Liu, she maintains a small audience of roughly 1,000 followers. Initially, she saw the account as a way to give her parents a window into her new life abroad, letting them glimpse her daily routine and easing their worries about how she was doing.

Her parents were surprised when they saw a video she posted of herself making mian geda tang, a northern Chinese homestyle dish of small pieces of dough cooked in soup. Chen grew up in the eastern Chinese city of Wenzhou, where noodles were not part of her family’s cooking tradition and flour was rarely bought. Now, living alone in Britain, she taught herself to make a dish she had never cooked before.

Away from home, Chen has discovered that she actually enjoys cooking without worrying about getting everything right. At home, she was often hesitant to cook with her mother nearby, reminding her not to make a mess.

“Here, I can just let myself go with no one watching over me. The fact that I can feed myself is already good enough,” Chen said. “I don’t have to worry about whether the kitchen is messy.”

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: Screenshots from Liu's cooking videos on Xiaohongshu.)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019007/Top-Ranked Chinese Netflix Series Divides Viewers at Home
World.title: Top-Ranked Chinese Netflix Series Divides Viewers at Home
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019007/Top-Ranked Chinese Netflix Series Divides Viewers at Home
World.content:
Chinese romantic drama “The Early Spring,” an adaptation of a 2021 web novel, has become the highest-ranked Chinese series on streaming giant Netflix’s weekly non-English TV chart. However, the show has divided domestic viewers over whether it romanticizes an unhealthy power imbalance between its protagonists: a male boss and his female subordinate.

The TV series, which premiered Aug. 26 on both Netflix and Chinese streaming platform Youku, follows the workplace romance between demanding advertising agency corporate executive Luan “Luke” Nian, played by Jing Boran, and 22-year-old newcomer Shang “Flora” Zhitao, played by Sun Qian.

After a drunken encounter, the two begin a secret relationship. Over time, Shang advances in her career, while Luan’s harsh and arrogant demeanor softens.

“The Early Spring” ranked No. 2 on Netflix’s global weekly chart for non-English TV series from Aug. 24 to 30, garnering 2.4 million views. The series also made Netflix’s weekly Top 10 in 22 markets, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brazil, and ranked No. 1 in Thailand and Vietnam.

In China, the series recorded 547 million views and topped domestic entertainment data platform Maoyan’s weekly popularity ranking on Sept. 7.

Many domestic social media users praised the chemistry and sexual tension between the two leads — developed with the help of an intimacy coordinator, a role still relatively uncommon in Chinese television, according to the show’s producers.

Liu, a viewer in her 30s who works in the arts in Shanghai, said that the show’s appeal lies in its escapism via a “straightforward” romance.

“It’s simply: I like you, so I like you,” Liu told Sixth Tone, in reference to the show’s driving sentiment. “Physical attraction is unavoidable.” Unlike many Chinese romance dramas that typically withhold physical intimacy between their leads, she added, “The Early Spring” brings Luan and Shang together almost immediately.

Liu also praised the 24-episode TV adaptation for bringing more warmth to its relationships. She said that compared with the original work, published under the pen name Guniang Bieku on the literature platform Jinjiang, the TV series more clearly establishes Luan and Shang as two people in love rather than primarily a sexual relationship. It also fleshes out Shang’s friendships, giving her a stronger support network.

Critics, however, have questioned whether Luan exploits his workplace authority to pursue Shang, pointing to scenes where he belittles her professional abilities. For example, when he suspects she is considering another job, he describes her as “cheap” and “obedient.”

Xu Xin, a 29-year-old media professional based in Beijing, said she agreed with much of the criticism, particularly over the couple’s first sexual encounter. “Imagine this happening in real life: a young woman fresh out of college gets drunk, and her sober male supervisor takes her home and has sex with her. That’s problematic,” she told Sixth Tone. “Even if they are attracted to each other, did it have to happen that night, when she was drunk?”

“It feels like a female fantasy,” she added. “In male-oriented fantasies, the protagonist turns his life around by becoming rich or powerful. Here, the fantasy is that a woman starts invisible, works her way up and becomes ‘better’ — and then the man comes back for her.”

For her, the series also reflects how messy real relationships can be. “People aren’t always rational, nor can they always live up to their own feminist ideals.”

The power-dynamic debate has extended to the web novel the series is based on. In it, after Shang quits her job and starts her own business, she initially decides to hire only men. The TV adaptation omits this plotline, which some had previously criticized as “discriminatory.”

Two prominent female influencers — Zhan Qingyun and Pang Ying, who are known for discussing gender equality issues in China — have also faced criticism after promoting the show.

In a Sept. 6 video posted on domestic lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, the two discussed the show, arguing that a good relationship “does not require two people to be perfect from the beginning” but can involve “two imperfect people growing together.” The video was later taken down.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: A still from “The Early Spring.” From Douban)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019008/One Last Night With Shanghai’s ‘Sleep No More’ Superfans
World.title: One Last Night With Shanghai’s ‘Sleep No More’ Superfans
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019008/One Last Night With Shanghai’s ‘Sleep No More’ Superfans
World.content:
SHANGHAI — On Aug. 30, Dong Minghai returned to Shanghai’s McKinnon Hotel one last time. It was his 518th visit to “Sleep No More.”

The 44-year-old machine vision quality engineer had been going roughly once a week since the production opened in 2016, enough to see nearly one in five of its 2,670 performances. “I’ve spent enough on it to buy an EV,” Dong said. “The number always shocks people.”

Over nearly a decade, the immersive production — co-produced by Shanghai Media Group and British theater company Punchdrunk — transformed a former power station into a six-story theatrical world set in 1930s Shanghai, drawing more than 750,000 visitors before its run ended. A new production of “Sleep No More” is planned for China’s southern tech hub of Shenzhen in 2027.

Audience members locked away their phones, put on white masks, and roamed freely through 90 rooms as 25 characters performed simultaneous storylines inspired by Shakespeare’s “Macbeth,” the novel “Rebecca,” and the Chinese folk tale “The Legend of the White Snake.” Because scenes unfolded at the same time across the building, no one could see everything in a single visit.

Macbeth scrubbed blood from his hands in a bathtub, splashing water onto nearby spectators. At the White Snake’s wedding, paper flowers rained down over the newlyweds and audience. Elsewhere, visitors could wander through a bamboo forest smelling of damp earth, a psychiatric hospital sharp with disinfectant, or a speakeasy bar scented with whiskey.

Tang, a 38-year-old supply chain manager who asked to be identified only by her surname for privacy reasons, had attended more than 160 times since 2018. She compared repeat visits to “collecting pieces of a puzzle,” returning to see how different storylines intersected and to discover scenes she had missed.

Over time, some repeat visitors became increasingly invested in the show’s private “one-on-one” encounters. A performer could single out an audience member, lead them away from the crowd, and perform for them alone — removing their mask, sometimes clasping their hand or pulling them into an embrace. The encounters could not be reserved, and the choice was entirely the performer’s.

For fans who returned again and again, that uncertainty became part of the attraction. Being chosen could bring the thrill of feeling seen; being passed over could sting. Over hundreds of visits, those moments could begin to feel personal.

“I know how the trick works,” Tang said. “And it still works on me. But perhaps that doesn’t make the happiness any less real.”

Choose me

On Tang’s first visit, she watched an actor playing Malcolm, a prince in “Macbeth,” choose her friend for a private one-on-one scene. The actor led her through a door and closed it behind them, leaving Tang outside with no idea what was happening.

It took Tang another 20 visits to be chosen for the same encounter.

Inside, Malcolm crushed a dust-covered bird’s egg in her palm, part of a scene tied to the murder of his father, King Duncan.

“That is the final piece of the ‘Malcolm’ puzzle,” Tang said. “Only the two of you know what happened in that room at that moment. You share the same secret.”

To choose someone, a performer might turn toward a room full of masked spectators and study the crowd, ignoring people directly in front of them before reaching past others for someone farther back.

When Dong entered the same one-on-one with the same performer for a second time in 2017, the actor greeted him: “It’s you again. I’m glad you are here.”

Only later did Dong realize it was a standard line. “The line is deliberately written to create the suggestion that he recognized me,” he said.

But after enough visits, recognition could also be real. Fans said performers learned to identify regulars even behind identical white masks, picking up on their build, gait, or other physical cues.

“It’s a very clever business model,” Tang said. “It gives you the illusion that the actor favors you.”

She compared the encounters with romance-themed jubensha, live-action role-playing games where customers pay for personalized attention. “Here, everyone pays for a ticket, but the actor can still refuse you,” she said.

Fans also developed favorite performers. Different actors could give the same character markedly different personalities, Dong said.

“I’ve seen the same role played as sad and desperate, playful, or even as someone who picks on the weak,” he said. “That keeps the show feeling fresh no matter how many times I see it.”

Because casting was not announced in advance, regulars called buying tickets “gambling on the cast,” trying to work out performers’ schedules before spending around 700 yuan ($98) in hopes that a favorite would appear.

Some fans began studying performers’ apparent preferences and adjusting their own behavior accordingly. They compared who favored regulars or newcomers and who seemed drawn to particular genders, body types, or styles of dress. Some stood in particular places, wore conspicuous clothing or wigs, and kept spreadsheets tracking performers’ selections. Rival groups traded gossip about one another’s visits.

When Tang first began following a performer she liked, she would position himself at the front of the crowd and wait to be chosen. After being passed over repeatedly, she learned to “manage expectations” and step back.

One performer she liked once told her: “I didn’t pick you because I thought you’d seen the show so many times that you must have already had this interaction.”

After the final performance on Aug. 30, Tang heard a young woman crying in the bathroom after apparently being passed over during an interaction. “Why did they let go of my hand?” the woman asked her friend.

“That’s why being chosen in front of so many people feels far more intense than happiness you can simply buy,” Tang said.

For Liu, a 20-year-old university student who had seen the show 254 times since 2021, the imbalance became harder to ignore when a performer she repeatedly followed through the show stopped choosing her for interactions. On one milestone visit that she had told him was important to her, he chose a stranger instead.

“I began to realize that this model gives actors too much power,” Liu said, asking to be identified only by her surname for privacy reasons. “The relationship isn’t equal. We are the ones asking for the interaction, and the performer is the only person who can decide whether we get it. So they can hurt you very easily.”

Last dance

Liu often wondered whether she had fallen for a performer’s characters or for the performer himself. “At first, I was stubborn with myself. I told myself it was only this place that had given him that magic,” she said.

But she eventually realized she still enjoyed watching him even in roles she thought did not suit him particularly well. Over time, rejection bothered her less; she found herself paying more attention to his dancing, improvisations, and the small ways he departed from the script.

“That psychological shift was a little painful for me,” Liu said. “Was it a romantic attraction? I didn’t really dare admit it.”

She eventually stopped trying to define the feeling. “Love doesn’t have such clear divisions,” she said. “It’s difficult to say, this is romantic love, and this is admiration. You can’t really separate them.”

Outside the theater, Liu found herself “unusually shy” around him and struggled to start conversations at the stage door. “But eventually I stopped trying to guess what he thought of me,” she said. “I really appreciate what he does onstage, and I’m still happy watching him. That’s enough.”

The experience also made Liu think differently about what she wanted from relationships.

“I hope that in other relationships in the future, I’ll be a braver person,” Liu said. “If I date someone next, I hope I find someone who loves me a little more. Recently, I’ve become used to being the one who gives, and even giving without expecting anything in return.”

For Tang, meanwhile, attending “Sleep No More” on important dates became “a habit, and a kind of ritual.”

“At first, it was the unpredictability of the show that attracted me. Later, it was the opposite: its certainty,” she said. “So many uncertain things happen in the real world, and I can’t control all of them. But inside this building, I know what will happen at every point in time, with every piece of music. That’s what kept bringing me back.”

All three formed friendships through the show that lasted for years. Tang became a part-time performer in another immersive production and met the man who is now her boyfriend. Dong, meanwhile, was already planning to see “Sleep No More” in Seoul and said he would return when a new production opens in Shenzhen.

On the final night, familiar scenes began to change.

In one encounter, a witch who normally trapped a mortal in an endless cycle instead left him a letter: “You are free.” Elsewhere, performers kissed and embraced, exchanged small handmade bouquets, and arranged black sand from the set into the shape of a mask.

In the finale, when Macbeth was hanged, the audience erupted in applause. On ordinary nights, the moment was met with gasps and stunned silence.

Performers, including some who had not appeared that night, emerged around the audience. Together, they sang “A Nightingale Sang in Berkeley Square,” the song normally played as spectators left the building. Some went off-key as they cried. Audience members sobbed too.

Then the lights went out.

Tang was the last audience member to leave. As staff closed the door behind her, she thought of an adapted line from “Rebecca” that appears in one of the show’s one-on-one encounters:

“We can never go back to Manderley again, that much is certain. But sometimes, in my dreams, I do return.”

Editor: Apurva.

(Header Image: Lady Macbeth washes away blood in a bathtub. From @SleepNoMore上海 on Weibo)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019002/Chinese Auto Supplier Faces Backlash for Firing 107 Recent Grads
World.title: Chinese Auto Supplier Faces Backlash for Firing 107 Recent Grads
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019002/Chinese Auto Supplier Faces Backlash for Firing 107 Recent Grads
World.content:
A Chinese auto parts maker has apologized for firing 107 recent university graduates just weeks after they began working, stating that four managers had been disciplined following public backlash.

In an apology published on its website on Sept. 7, the company, Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems, based in the eastern Jiangsu province, said the decision to reduce staff and reorganize positions was “incorrect.” It admitted it had caused “immense physical and psychological harm to the students” and “a serious negative impact on their families and society.”

The company also announced disciplinary measures against four managers, including withheld salaries and reassignments. It said it had dismissed its human resources director, while the head of the human resources department had been demoted and transferred. However, domestic media later reported that the company had no such human resources director at the time of the incident.

Xingyu is one of China’s major automotive lighting equipment manufacturers, producing 80 million headlights per year. It also supplies international automakers such as Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW.

During a university campus recruitment drive earlier this year, the company signed employment agreements with 440 students set to graduate in 2026, and later hired 372.

According to its apology, however, company management decided in July to reorganize staff and reduce its workforce based on order outlook and staffing needs.

The company said that in early August, its human resources department approached 140 of the 372 new employees and informed 33 that they would be allowed to remain in their original positions. The remaining 107 signed termination agreements.

Of the 107 terminated employees, 75 held bachelor’s degrees and 32 had master’s degrees. Sixty worked in manufacturing, 39 in research and development, and eight held other roles such as quality control and project engineering.

A recent graduate who was among those terminated by the company told domestic media outlet Beijing News that they were given only two options: to “voluntarily” sign a resignation agreement for “personal reasons” or be forcibly transferred to a manufacturing line position. The graduate said they also were not offered additional compensation for the sudden termination.

The move sparked widespread backlash online, with users noting that in China, “recent graduate” status applies only in the first two years following graduation and is voided upon employment. To improve employment prospects for recent graduates, many junior positions are available only to those with “recent graduate” status, meaning such positions are no longer available to them once terminated.

On Aug. 25, local authorities said they deemed Xingyu to have used “simple and harsh” methods and failed to communicate sufficiently and effectively with employees.

In its apology, Xingyu said each of the 107 terminated workers would receive 15,000 yuan ($2,200) to ease their living costs while seeking new employment. The company added that it would offer free accommodation in its dormitories and help connect them with other employers. Those who remain unemployed by the end of November will also receive compensation equivalent to six months of their previous salary.

As of Sept. 7, 71 of the recently terminated employees had found new jobs, the company said. Local employment authorities have also organized special recruitment events and recommended positions to those affected by the cuts.

Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW separately confirmed to domestic media that they had received details on the matter and launched their own investigations into Xingyu.

“Respecting the legitimate rights and interests of workers is a core principle that the Volkswagen Group adheres to in all its business activities,” a Volkswagen spokesperson told domestic media. “This principle also applies to the management of our supply chain system, and we require that all fundamental values and rights be fully guaranteed.”

Circulating screenshots also showed that Mercedes-Benz responded to an anonymous report regarding the incident via email, stating that Xingyu’s behavior was “inconsistent with Mercedes-Benz’s corporate principles” and that it intends to forward the report to the relevant department for further review.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: VCG)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018995/How a Rotten Apple Brought China’s Internet Into a Mushroom Lab
World.title: How a Rotten Apple Brought China’s Internet Into a Mushroom Lab
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018995/How a Rotten Apple Brought China’s Internet Into a Mushroom Lab
World.content:
What are the odds that two compatible spores from a wood-rotting fungus would land on the same apple, enter through its stem, germinate, meet, and eventually produce a mushroom inside the fruit?

“About the same as winning the lottery,” said Mu Liheng, a researcher at the Yunnan Wild Mushroom Protection and Development Association, in Kunming, capital of southwestern China’s Yunnan province.

In July 2024, Mu’s colleague Xu Rongju came across a photograph on the lifestyle app Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote, that appeared to show exactly that: a white, fan-shaped mushroom was growing from the stem of an apple beside a woman’s kitchen sink.



Suspecting the mushroom might be worth studying, he contacted the user, a woman surnamed Deng living in the eastern Zhejiang province, and asked her to send it to him. Two days later, the rotten fruit arrived at the team’s laboratory in Kunming.

Xu’s posts about the team’s subsequent experiments helped turn the discovery into an online sensation, prompting people across China to send in mushrooms found growing on grapes, mangoes, garlic, and even used coffee capsules.

Over the next two years, the researchers drew on some of those specimens, along with strains from an existing breeding program, to develop what they called eight numbered “generations” of split-gill mushrooms.

Two varieties have emerged as particularly promising, and one could eventually reach the shelves of a major supermarket chain.

Rotten luck

The day after the apple arrived, Xu commented beneath Deng’s photograph. “This strain is very strong and has research value,” he wrote, promising to report back when the team made progress.

In one Xiaohongshu update, Xu placed photographs taken a day apart side by side. A dense white network of fungal threads, known as mycelium, had spread farther across the rotten apple. Other images showed the fungus growing rapidly in a Petri dish and thick individual threads under a microscope.

DNA sequencing identified the strain as Schizophyllum commune, commonly known as the split-gill mushroom. The team planned to isolate and purify the culture before moving on to cultivation trials.

Split-gill mushrooms normally grow on dead wood, making the inside of an apple an unusual place to find one. On Deng’s apple, no mycelium appeared in sections that remained intact. It grew most densely in tissue that had already decayed, suggesting the fungus was feeding mainly on the rotten portions.

The apple culture joined more than 1,000 split-gill strains at the team’s laboratory. The team selected about 400 for further crossbreeding.

Edible split-gill mushrooms, known in China as bai shen, can have a dry texture and mildly bitter taste. Mu, who joined the work in 2023, was looking for strains with better flavor and texture, as well as lower spore production, which could reduce respiratory risks for growers.

Some strains in the collection had previously been sent into space through a collaboration with China’s human spaceflight program, including aboard the Shenzhou-12 spacecraft in 2021. After returning to Earth, they were screened for potentially useful mutations, and promising strains were used in further breeding. The apple strain itself was not sent into space.

As Xu’s updates spread online, users gave the apple mushroom a name: “Guo Jun Wang,” or the “King of Fruit Mushrooms.” In Chinese, the name sounds like “Prince Guo,” a character in the hit Qing dynasty (1644–1911) palace drama “Empresses in the Palace.” The pun helped propel the mushroom to the top of the trending rankings on microblogging site Weibo.

Xu used the nickname in a Xiaohongshu update: “You Give Me a Rotten Apple, I’ll Give You Back the King of Fruit Mushrooms.”

“Thank you, Xiaohongshu. I really didn’t expect to find research material here,” he wrote. “Once the experiment is complete, I’ll include everyone in the acknowledgments.”

People asked what the mushroom tasted like, whether it might have an apple flavor, whether it could be grown commercially, and when they might be able to eat it.

A month after mailing the rotten apple to Kunming, Deng received mushrooms cultivated from its strain. She chopped them up, mixed them with eggs, steamed the dish, and documented the entire process online.

By then, more than a dozen people a day were tagging Xu in photographs of mushrooms they wanted him to identify. Over the following year, the researchers received specimens found growing on more than 40 different fruits, foods, and everyday objects, including persimmons, pomelos, cantaloupes, garlic, and used coffee capsules.

One of the earliest contributors was Huang Cheng, a 37-year-old medical equipment business owner in central China’s Hubei province. Days after seeing the apple mushroom online, he removed a used capsule from his coffee machine and noticed several small, white, fan-shaped mushrooms growing from it.

“Normally, I might have just taken a picture and thrown it away,” Huang said.

Instead, he remembered that Deng’s apple had been sent to a laboratory. He photographed the capsule, posted it online, tagged Xu, and asked whether it might also be useful for research.

The post drew thousands of likes. Other users began directing Xu to Huang’s photographs, and within two days, the capsules had arrived at the lab. The team later received similar coffee-capsule specimens from Shanghai and Kunming.

“We were able to see different mushrooms from all over the country, growing on different fruits and all kinds of unusual things,” Xu said. “This really went from a small laboratory to a much bigger laboratory.”

Fruit loop

In the lab, the team isolated a strain from Huang’s coffee-capsule mushroom and crossed it with one of the space-bred strains in the collection.

Their offspring was crisp, heat-resistant, and faintly apple-scented. The team classified it as the fourth generation of the “Guo Jun Wang” series and named it “Xiang Fei,” or “Fragrant Concubine,” after a legendary Qing dynasty consort said to have carried a natural fragrance.

Many of the “Guo Jun Wang” generations, including the Xiang Fei, were not descended from Deng’s apple strain. As the project expanded, researchers used the name for promising varieties they developed, drawing on samples sent in by people online as well as strains already held by the association.

Producing those varieties meant repeatedly crossing and testing hundreds of strains. Mu often worked until midnight, preparing thousands of Petri dishes and checking newly cultivated samples.

“It was too much,” he said. “We didn’t really keep count at the time. There was no set amount of time we spent on it.”

For Xu, the experiments came on top of his doctoral research. “I just thought that if we could grow it and give the internet users an answer, that would actually be something meaningful,” he said.

The first generation of Guo Jun Wang mushrooms “tasted bad and bitter,” Xu recalled. By the second half of 2025, the team had selected more than 10 promising varieties and invited dozens of mushroom enthusiasts to cook and taste them.

“Some have an average texture but look beautiful. Some grow particularly fast. Some have high levels of polysaccharides,” Xu said, referring to the complex carbohydrates that can give mushrooms immune-boosting benefits. “The one that grew on grapes has a very good, crispy texture.”

After more than a year of breeding and selection, another variety stood out in February 2026. Provisionally designated the eighth-generation Guo Jun Wang, it had an unusual growth form and produced very few spores.

The two traits were unrelated, Mu said. The low spore production resulted from a gene segment involved in spore formation failing to be expressed, while a different gene controlled the mushroom’s unusual shape.

In July, Deng received both the eighth-generation and Xiang Fei mushrooms from the laboratory, two years after sending her rotten apple to Kunming.

Small batches of the mushrooms have also been sold through Xu’s Xiaohongshu account for 19.9 yuan ($2.80) per 100 grams. Mu said split-gill varieties identified in China are edible, and that large-scale production would require routine safety checks, including tests for heavy metals and pesticide residues.

However, the number of buyers remains limited because public awareness of split-gill mushrooms in China is still relatively low, Xu said. “If someone has eaten bai shen before, they might have tried them once and thought they don’t taste very good, so won’t eat them again.”

The team has been in contact with e-commerce giant Alibaba’s supermarket chain Freshippo about potentially selling Xiang Fei, which the researchers say tastes better and stores more easily than conventional varieties.

But commercial production remains beyond their current capacity. The team lacks the funding and manpower to grow the mushrooms at scale, while questions remain over who would cultivate them, how they would be transported, and how consistent quality could be maintained. For now, the researchers grow small batches by hand; outsourcing production, they say, could make quality harder to control.

They are also studying why crossbreeding produces such pronounced differences in the split-gill mushroom’s shape, work they hope could eventually help guide the breeding of other fungi.

“We’re happy that after all the attention in 2024, the story didn’t simply disappear,” Mu said. “There have been new developments over the past two years, and at least we’ve gotten two results that we wanted.”

In the hunt for a suitable name for the eighth-generation mushroom, the researchers have turned to the internet again.

One Xiaohongshu user suggested “Popcorn,” because its unusual shape resembles popped kernels. Another proposed “Ba Xian Wang,” or “Eighth Prince” — another Qing dynasty prince and a brother of Prince Guo.

Editor: Apurva.

(Header image: Split-gill mushrooms growing from the apple after it arrived at the laboratory, July 2024. Courtesy of Xu)

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.

World.title: LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections
World.content:
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is holding its first parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026, after being postponed at least four times: first in May 2022, then in May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026.

The historic polls are seen as a pivotal moment in the decades-long peace process in a region that was mired in conflict and socioeconomic and political challenges. The upcoming elections are also a test for the Bangsamoro transition and the institutions and systems established in the last seven years.

World.title: Zverev banishes US Open demons with victory over Shelton
World.content:
CHAMPION. Germany's Alexander Zverev celebrates with the trophy after winning the men's singles final against Ben Shelton of the United States in the 2026 US Open.

Armed with a champion's mentality following his breakthrough triumph in the French Open, Alexander Zverev redeems himself from his 2020 US Open letdown and breaks American hearts with a devastating display against Ben Shelton in the final

Top seed Alexander Zverev banished bitter US Open memories to beat American Ben Shelton, 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2, in the final on Sunday, September 13 (Monday, September 14, Manila time), capturing the title six years after letting a golden opportunity slip through his fingers.

The German squandered a two-set lead in the 2020 title match against Austrian Dominic Thiem, but now armed with a champion’s mentality following his breakthrough triumph in the French Open in June, he broke American hearts with a devastating display against Shelton.

“I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through, and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before,” Zverev said during the presentation ceremony.

The home fans were desperate to see Shelton end a 23-year American men’s Grand Slam drought, but the eighth seed never found his top form in his first major final.

“I know that today 99.9% of the people wanted Ben to win so I’m very sorry,” said Zverev. “Even though I know that the crowd was against me, the crowd was always incredibly fair and we as players we appreciate it.”

Zverev was so focused on the job at hand, he did not even realize he had won the title when Shelton smacked a service return long.

As the umpire announced “Game, set, and match Zverev,” the German headed back to the baseline, ready to receive Shelton’s serve.

It took him a few seconds to register why the cheering fans were giving him a standing ovation — as he belatedly cracked a smile and ran to the net to embrace Shelton.

He was beaming again as he was handed a Grand Slam record $5.5 million winner’s prize.

Hot start

In a battle between two of tennis’ most explosive players, it was Zverev who had all the early firepower, as Shelton’s inexperience showed with a double fault on break point in the opening game.

Shelton produced one of the points of the match in the sixth game, scrambling to reach a drop shot and prevailing in a tense exchange at the net.

Encouraged by his team, the American mixed in serve-and-volley tactics in an attempt to shift the momentum, but the move proved ineffective and he handed Zverev the set with a double fault.

The partisan crowd tried to get under Zverev’s skin in the second set, cheering wildly after he produced a double fault in the ninth game. But the German refused to get distracted, surging to a 5-0 lead in the tiebreak as the fans desperately chanted “Let’s go, Ben!”

Zverev looked like he would roll to the finish line in the third set as he saved a break point in the sixth game with a lethal backhand winner.

Shelton’s frustration boiled over two games later when he slipped and crashed to the court, prompting the American to let out an expletive.

But Shelton dug in his heels, subduing his opponent with a series of powerful groundstrokes from the baseline to break serve and force a fourth set.

Shelton’s resilience only delayed the inevitable as Zverev came through a 25-shot rally to secure an early break in the deciding set. He never let go of that advantage as he finally got the chance to hoist the US Open trophy on his 11th appearance at the hardcourt major.

“My successes are a gift, the failures are a gift, and being here playing in front of you guys is a gift,” said Shelton, the first Black American man in 54 years to contest the New York final after Arthur Ashe.

His girlfriend, Olympic champion football player Trinity Rodman, made it to his player’s box after racing 200 miles from her Washington Spirit game, which largely overlapped with the start of his match.

‘Jannik still ahead’

The victory will no doubt help Zverev move beyond a series of Grand Slam disappointments. The German’s career has also been overshadowed by allegations of domestic violence, which he has repeatedly denied.

His two majors this season have made a dent in the duopoly of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, who won all eight Grand Slam titles across 2024 and 2025.

Alcaraz, who won this year’s Australian Open, exited the US Open in a quarterfinal defeat by Shelton after a long injury layoff, while Sinner pulled out injured before the tournament began after winning Wimbledon.

Asked if he considered himself the world’s top player now, Zverev said, “With Jannik Sinner being injured and Carlos Alcaraz coming back from injury after four months, right now this moment, probably yes.

“Both of them healthy and both of them at the top of their game, maybe not.”

“If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead. It’s as simple as that.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Martin Romualdez ordered transferred from PGH to Payatas jail
World.content:
CONFINED. An officer of the Philippine National Police reads an arrest warrant to former House speaker and Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City on September 7, 2026.

PGH doctors found that Romualdez is in stable condition and no longer needs confinement

MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division on Monday, September 14, ordered the transfer of custody of former speaker Martin Romualdez from the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) where he is confined, to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas.

The lawmaker will be detained there as he faces his plunder case due to alleged P7.44 billion in kickbacks.

Romualdez was ordered transferred after the PGH doctors found that he is in stable condition and needs no confinement.

Authorities said the Leyte lawmaker will be transferred on Monday too, after his discharge from PGH. – Rappler.com

World.title: KKR exits First Gen, sells stake to Gateway-linked firm for P25.8B
World.content:
Only a month before its exit, the private equity giant had been seeking to increase its First Gen stake and take the Lopez-led power company private, but the proposal was rejected

MANILA, Philippines – Global private equity investment giant KKR has exited First Gen Corporation, selling its entire 19.9% stake in the Lopez-led power company for about P25.77 billion, just weeks after an attempt to increase its investment and take First Gen private fell through.

In a regulatory filing, KKR-linked Valorous Asia Holdings said it disposed of 715.8 million First Gen shares on September 10 for P25.77 billion, equivalent to P36 per share. Valorous said the transaction included shares held indirectly through Philippines Clean Energy Holding Inc. and left it with no remaining stake in First Gen.

The buyer was Angsana Finance Limited, which separately disclosed that it had acquired the same 715.86 million shares, equivalent to 19.9% of First Gen’s outstanding common shares. Angsana is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and is wholly owned by Gateway Holdings Limited, the parent of emerging markets investment firm Gateway Partners. Gateway, which operates out of Singapore and Dubai, is already an investor in the Philippines as one of the backers of UNO Digital Bank.

Only a month earlier, KKR had sought to increase its stake in First Gen.

In August, First Philippine Holdings (FPH), First Gen’s parent company, rejected KKR’s non-binding proposal to purchase another 8.43% of the power company from FPH and launch a voluntary tender offer for First Gen’s entire public float at P35 per share. FPH said the proposed price did not represent First Gen’s “true value.”

Had the proposal pushed through, the tender offer would also have supported a potential voluntary delisting of First Gen from the Philippine Stock Exchange.

Now, KKR has instead sold its existing shares at P36 apiece, P1 higher than its proposed tender price.

The exit was also followed by a change in First Gen’s board. Manolo Michael de Guzman resigned as a director and member of the Board Risk Oversight Committee effective September 11.

De Guzman is a senior adviser at KKR and president of Philippines Clean Energy Holding Inc., one of the vehicles through which KKR held its First Gen stake. His resignation came a day after KKR sold its entire stake, although First Gen did not state a reason for his departure. – Rappler.com

World.title: [Rappler’s Best] A vote buried in the noise
World.content:
BARMM. The Philippine flag stands alongside the flag of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao outside the Office of the Chief Minister in Cotabato City.

You can’t be blamed for having lost track of the crucial events that led to today’s BARMM elections — because Manila continues to dominate the attention economy with the antics and shenanigans of politicians based here

The first of its kind parliamentary elections in the Philippines are finally happening today, Monday, September 14, in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), after repeated postponements in the last four years.

Something hopeful is happening in the country, and it’s happening in BARMM, was how civil society groups put it in this curtain-raiser by Iya Gozum. We’re covering the polls live here.

The late former president Noynoy Aquino must be wincing in irony, he who paved the way for this historic vote when he shook hands with the rebel commander Ebrahim Murad and signed a peace deal with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in 2012. After all, it’s under the son of the dictator who fueled the Mindanao rebellion that these elections are now taking place.

The Aquinos have had a soft spot for the MILF. Nearly a year after she was catapulted to power in the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, then-president Corazon Aquino met in Cotabato City with the unarmed Murad, who gave her a bouquet of flowers tied with a yellow ribbon. I recalled that moment, and what happened (or did not happen) after, in this piece.

Murad and the MILF have controlled the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) that was set up in 2019 after the “yes” vote won in the Bangsamoro plebiscite. The BTA was meant to prepare the region — its bureaucracy, its people — for self-governance and today’s historic polls. What has the BTA accomplished? Watch here.

Yet, the MILF found itself repeating the mistakes of its predecessor in the region, the Moro National Liberation Front, as its leaders squabbled over funds, appointments, and Malacañang’s interference.

In March 2025, what had been brewing happened: a leadership shake-up ousted Murad as BTA chief minister and put in place the Marcos administration’s bet, Abdulraof Macacua.

Today, Murad and the MILF fight for survival and relevance through the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), which is fielding the most number of candidates for district, party, and sectoral seats at 81. Macacua’s Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) is not far behind with 74 candidates.

Violence persists, with the region still hobbled by persistent threats from extremists, as pointed out by Reemar Alonsagay in this piece.

How can the next BARMM government make sure no one’s left behind? Shay Du lays out the challenges and opportunities in this report.

Our reporters Iya Gozum and John Sitchon, who are in Cotabato City, covered the colorful grand rallies of the political parties last Saturday, September 12, (watch their report). While an important political process, the polls have been clouded with uncertainty and fear, Herbie Gomez wrote in this story.

These elections are unique for at least five reasons, as explained by Shay Du in this story.

Over 600 candidates are vying for just 80 seats — 70% of whom are men and 38% of whom belong to Gen X. Here are the other numbers that matter.

In this story, John Sitchon and Shay Du introduce us to the dynasts, elites, and power blocs competing for the polls. What parties are running? Check them out here.

You can’t be blamed, though, for having lost track of the crucial events that led to today’s elections — because Manila continues to dominate the attention economy with the antics and shenanigans of politicians based here.

Former speaker and presidential cousin Martin Romualdez was charged with plunder on September 7, a non-bailable offense, but, quick to the draw, he had himself confined in Cardinal Santos hospital before he could be served an arrest warrant.

Jairo Bolledo walks us through a bizarre timeline of events that led us to yet another Saturday spectacle (after Sara Duterte’s dramatic court entrance the previous Saturday) of authorities moving Romualdez from Cardinal Santos to the Philippine General Hospital, which is now the Sandiganbayan’s refuge for “independent” medical examination of high-profile public officials facing prison.

Jairo shows us in this report how to delay detention, Romualdez edition.

While Romualdez and his counsels are now in uncharted legal territory, the judiciary handed the other side of the Marcos clan an astounding victory: the Supreme Court reversed a previous court ruling that convicted the President’s 97-year-old mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos, of graft in 2018 — and acquitted her.

This adds to the list of record-high wins for Marcos family members and their cronies accused of corruption under the Marcos dictatorship.

In Mrs. Marcos’ latest victory, what was overturned was the Sandiganbayan’s ruling that she had taken part in the management of Swiss foundations that were set up with public funds amounting to $200 million. The SC’s 1st Division said the evidence against her was not properly authenticated, among other reasons cited for the acquittal. Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda wrote the decision that was concurred in by associate justices Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting, Ricardo Rosario, and Jose Midas Marquez.

By the way, Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo is retiring in November. The Court in August opened applications for the post.

We take this moment to express our condolences to the family of the revered sports journalist Recah Trinidad, who died on Sunday, September 13.

Here are some of Rappler’s bests that you shouldn’t miss:

Val Villanueva takes a deep dive into documents pertaining to Villar Land’s revaluation and recognition of enormous accounting gains. Read Part 1 here and Part 2 here.

Mon Abrea tackles a common question nowadays: should billionaires pay more taxes?

Lance Spencer Yu explains why removing the much-hated travel tax can be easier said than done.

Lourence Angelo Marcellana profiles the Singsons and their unrivaled dominance in Ilocos Sur. Read about other political dynasties here.

– Rappler.com

World.title: [EDITORIAL] Pinagpala talaga si Imelda Marcos at Martin Romualdez
World.content:
In a way, it was a good week for the Marcoses and Romualdezes — napawalang-sala si dating first lady Imelda Marcos mula sa pitong counts of graft.

With every intention of sounding sarcastic, we’re quoting Imelda herself, “God is love. I have loved. Therefore, I will go to heaven.” Nabilaukan man kayo o hindi, tandaan ninyo ang sense of entitlement sa pahayag na ito that only Imelda can deliver.

Ito namang si dating House speaker Martin Romualdez, sinusuwerte pa rin kahit hinahabol ng Ombudsman, dahil sa oras na inilabas ang arrest warrant niya para sa 7.44-billion plunder case, bigla siyang naospital. ‘Yan ba ang klase ng suwerte na galing sa bilyon-bilyong yaman?

Anong larawan ang ipinipinta nito? “Victory for impunity,” sabi ng analysts at advocates. Ito ang sistema kung saan laging talo ang accountability kapag bumangga sa kapangyarihan, yaman, at pagde-delay gamit ang legal muscle.

Mabilis ring nabasa ni Rappler investigative head Chay Hofileña at ng kanyang team ang template, “Top officials, including past presidents charged with plunder and/or graft and corruption, suddenly fell ill or developed illnesses that merited confinement.” (BASAHIN: Romualdez joins list of officials who cite illness to delay custody)

Ipagpalagay na natin na talagang may sakit ang mga opisyal na ito. Sabi ni Southern Illinois University criminology associate professor Raymund Narag, ipinapakita nito na “selectively available to the rich and powerful” ang medical considerations. Kung mahirap ka at may kondisyong pangkalusugan, makatatambay ka ba sa ospital kahit may arrest warrant?

This is a graphic story of how power, privilege, and family shield the elite. Konektado ang dalawang kaso sa nakaupo ngayon sa Malacañang. Imelda Marcos is the mother of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Martin Romualdez is his first cousin.

Despite the fallout between Marcos Jr. and his cousin, talaga bang walang kinalaman ang pagiging Romualdez niya sa desisyong pagbigyan siyang manatili sa Cardinal Santos at pagkatapos ay ipa-test pa sa University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital? Gagawin ba nila ito para sa lahat ng magdadahilan na hindi sila puwedeng ikulong dahil may sakit?

Mabalik naman tayo kay Mrs. Marcos. Sabi ng human rights lawyer na si Ruben Carranza, ipinapakita ng acquittal ni Imelda Marcos ang “long-standing problems in the Philippine justice system.”

Ano’t ano man ang naging hatol ng mga korte, hindi nito binabago ang true historical narrative: ang human rights violations noong Martial Law, ang civil forfeiture rulings, at ang mga nabawi ng estado at ng mga biktima na ill-gotten wealth.

Sabi ng representante ng ACT Teachers Party-List, ipinapakita ng acquittal na tila hindi kayang ikulong ng justice system ang “biggest plunderers.”

Hindi maihihiwalay ang magkasunod na dagok ng impunity na ito sa Marcos legacy.

Ngayong nagbabanggaan ang dalawang legacy sa buhay ni Marcos Jr. — ang “mahiya naman kayo (shame on you)” SONA speech na nag-trigger sa flood control corruption exposés at ang baluktot na pamana ng Martial Law — ano ang gagawin ng Pangulo?

Pero kung nais in Marcos na ipamukha sa mundo na hindi niya kinukunsinti ang pinsan at labas siya sa mga kalokohan ng kanyang dating most trusted lieutenant — dapat niyang seryosohin ang pagpapataw ng patas na batas.

Kapag ang batas ay istrikto sa mahihirap, pero nababaluktot para sa presidential relatives — hindi lamang ‘yan suwerte. ‘Yan ang kaibahan ng langit at lupa ng mayaman at mahirap. That is impunity, that is injustice. – Rappler.com

World.title: BARMM polls: 4 hurt in Cotabato polling center shooting
World.content:
(1st UPDATE) Voters run to safety as shots are fired, while soldiers continue to secure the premises of the polling place

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – At least four people were hurt after gunfire broke out inside the Central Pilot Elementary School in Cotabato City, a voting center for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao’s (BARMM) first parliamentary elections on Monday, September 14.

Voting in the school was already delayed as the automated counting machines arrived nearly an hour after the scheduled early voting at 5 am. The shooting happened minutes before 7 am.

Play Video

Before the shootout, a commotion occurred involving groups of men, who, at one point, were throwing stones at each other.

Rappler saw a wounded man in that commotion, who said he was punched. He claimed that he was not a voter in the school but a poll watcher.

Play Video

When gunfire erupted, voters ran to safety, while military personnel from the Philippine government continued to secure the premises.

Cotabato City, Bangsamoro’s regional center, has been placed under control of the Commission of Elections over incidents of violence. – with reports from Iya Gozum and John Sitchon/Rappler.com

World.title: From Wheat to Direct Flights: Ambassador Maaninou on Morocco-Kazakhstan Ties
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan and Morocco are looking to turn growing political ties into more practical economic cooperation, with logistics, grain supplies, investment and renewable energy emerging as areas of particular potential, according to Mohammed Rashid Maaninou, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Morocco to Kazakhstan. Speaking to The Astana Times, the ambassador described Morocco as a “geostrategical hub” in Africa whose industrial base, port infrastructure and trade links can create opportunities for Kazakh businesses seeking access to wider markets.

That positioning is increasingly relevant to Kazakhstan, particularly as the two countries explore ways to expand agricultural trade and address the logistical distance between Central Asia and African markets.

Morocco imported Kazakh wheat for the first time last year, receiving two shipments of around 30,000 tonnes each. The scale could increase significantly this year, Maaninou said.

“We used to import our cereals from Ukraine, but now it’s impossible. Prices in the United States, Canada and Brazil are higher than the price of Kazakhstan’s wheat,” he said.

The ambassador identified logistics as the main challenge in expanding this trade, given Kazakhstan’s landlocked geography, but said that Morocco’s Atlantic position could turn that constraint into a commercial opportunity.

“That’s why two years ago, we signed an agreement that there will be a huge stock of cereals that will be put in Morocco, managed by Kazakhstan in one of the Moroccan ports,” Maaninou said.

Under the proposed arrangement, Kazakhstan would be able to bring grain in larger volumes, store it in Morocco and use the country as a distribution point for African markets.

The idea is increasingly being accompanied by direct business engagement. A Kazakh business delegation of around 30 people recently visited Morocco, while a Moroccan delegation is expected to visit Astana later this year. The two countries have also established a Kazakhstan-Morocco Business Council. For the ambassador, these mechanisms are meant to create the conditions for businesses to develop commercial links.

“Government is here only to open the doors and to make things legal, framework done and everything prepared,” he said.

Beyond geography: a shared pragmatic outlook

The discussion about connectivity also led to a broader question of how Kazakhstan and Morocco navigate their respective geopolitical environments. Both countries have sought to maintain room for maneuver in their foreign relations, balancing ties with larger powers and pursuing practical partnerships without tying their strategies exclusively to one geopolitical bloc. Maaninou described such pragmatism not as neutrality, but as an ability to turn geopolitical constraints into strategic opportunities.

“To be honest, it’s very difficult to be neutral,” he said, noting that Kazakhstan operates among major powers such as Russia and China, while Morocco is closely connected to the European Union, as well as the United States.

“For me, pragmatism is how to change something that looks in the beginning as something that will stop you to something that will help you to grow. How to shift from something that you are afraid of to something you use to be more powerful,” the ambassador said.

He also pointed to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s diplomatic background as an important factor in Kazakhstan’s approach.

“Don’t forget that His Excellency Mr. Tokayev was a diplomat. So he knows how to change these situations,” Maaninou said, describing Kazakhstan’s foreign policy as “very good” since his arrival in the country.

Morocco, he added, has a much longer history of navigating changing international and regional environments.

“Morocco has a long tradition of diplomacy and exists for 14 centuries as a country. So we have a long experience being an African, North African country with all whatever happening around,” he said.

Rather than presenting this experience as a hierarchy, the ambassador’s comments point to a degree of strategic affinity between two countries that have developed different but comparable ways of maintaining autonomy in a complex geopolitical landscape.

Morocco’s industrial experience and Kazakhstan’s market

Maaninou also outlined how Morocco has sought to strengthen its position not simply as a geographical gateway, but as an industrial and investment platform. Around two decades ago, Morocco conducted a strategic assessment of sectors in which it could become internationally competitive, he said.

“You cannot be good in everything. So you have to specialize in the global world,” Maaninou said.

The country subsequently developed major automotive and aerospace industries, while expanding its logistics infrastructure around the Tangier port complex. Morocco is also positioning itself as an investment and distribution hub connecting African, European, American and Arab markets.

Its network of trade agreements is part of that strategy. Maaninou said companies can use Morocco as a production and export base, with local value added allowing access to several markets under preferential trade arrangements. The ambassador stressed that Morocco’s growing industrial base has been accompanied by an emphasis on investment conditions and local capabilities.

“We have also this, what we call the white book for investors. It changes every year. It depends on what we want,” he said, pointing to incentives in sectors such as pharmaceuticals.

But he framed Morocco’s experience less as a template for Kazakhstan than as a possible reference point for companies looking to operate across multiple markets.

For Kazakhstan, he sees particular potential in localization and technology-intensive investment.

“There is no international investor that can come to Morocco without bringing a transfer of technology. If you don’t transfer your technology, these investors will not come,” Maaninou said.

Morocco, he noted, has moved in some sectors from importing equipment to manufacturing components domestically, including elements used in renewable energy.

Renewable energy as another point of convergence

Renewable energy is another area where the two countries could expand cooperation, Maaninou said. He sees strong potential in combining Kazakhstan’s natural conditions and energy resources with growing investment in wind and solar power.

“The sun is here, the wind is here,” he said, pointing particularly to southern Kazakhstan and the country’s wider wind potential.

“Instead of using your own resources that you can sell and have money, it’s better to use what is free and leave the other parts to export and to have money. So you win on both sides,” he said.

Maaninou said Morocco has developed substantial experience in integrating renewable sources into its electricity system, with wind and solar accounting for a significant share of generation. According to the ambassador, 50% of electricity in Morocco comes from wind and solar. The two countries, he suggested, therefore have an opportunity to exchange experience while building projects that reflect their own respective economic and geographical conditions.

From political contacts to people-to-people links

The expansion of diplomatic infrastructure is another sign the relationship is gaining momentum. Kazakhstan now has honorary consulates in Casablanca, Fes and Marrakech, while Morocco has an honorary consulate in Almaty and is considering opening another in Shymkent. The ambassador described Shymkent as a promising regional point of contact because of its expanding business community.

“There is a lot of businessmen from this area that are very aggressive worldwide. So why not going there to see what we can do?” he said.

The opening of the honorary consulate in Marrakech also reflects the potential to widen bilateral ties beyond Astana and Almaty. Maaninou highlighted tourism and agriculture as two areas with particular potential.

Improving connectivity will be critical. The ambassador said negotiations are under way with airlines on a potential connection between Casablanca and Almaty, initially involving a technical stop before a fully direct service becomes possible with the appropriate aircraft.

“When you have direct flights, everything will be more easy,” he said.

Maaninou’s own professional background is closely linked to tourism. Before becoming ambassador, he spent two decades in the sector, including nine years at the Moroccan National Tourism Office.

He said Kazakhstan’s large outbound tourism market immediately stood out to him as an opportunity.

“In Kazakhstan, people travel a lot abroad,” he said.

The ambassador also offered what he described as a “journalist scoop”: plans are being developed for a Moroccan Year in Kazakhstan next year, combining cultural, business and other events across different regions of the country. The initiative is expected to go beyond Astana and Almaty and offer Kazakh audiences a broader picture of Morocco, from culture and traditions to business and knowledge exchange.

At the same time, the two ambassadors are considering a reciprocal initiative that would showcase Kazakhstan across Moroccan cities. For Maaninou, that reciprocal approach is important to the relationship’s next stage: not simply increasing awareness of one another, but creating more channels for businesses, tourists and institutions to interact.

As Kazakhstan and Morocco expand their diplomatic and commercial contacts, the emerging relationship appears increasingly defined by complementarity: Kazakhstan’s position as a major producer and land-linked Eurasian economy meeting Morocco’s role as a geostrategical hub connecting African, European and Atlantic markets. The challenge, as with many long-distance partnerships, will be to translate that strategic fit into regular trade flows, direct connectivity and projects that give businesses a reason to remain engaged.

World.title: Tokayev Calls for Deeper BRICS Plus Cooperation on Trade, AI and Critical Minerals
World.content:
NEW DELHI – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for deeper practical cooperation between Kazakhstan and BRICS countries in trade, logistics, artificial intelligence, critical minerals and water security, positioning the format as a platform for broader economic ties amid growing geopolitical fragmentation.

Speaking at the BRICS Plus plenary session in New Delhi on Sept. 13, Tokayev said Kazakhstan sees cooperation with the group as an opportunity to expand access to new markets, attract investment, strengthen transport links and advance technological development.

BRICS amid global fragmentation

Tokayev described the current global environment as an era of “great fragmentation,” a term used in the 2026 Global Peace Index to characterize geopolitical confrontation, rising militarization, weakening multilateral institutions and growing trade barriers.

He noted that BRICS, representing nearly half of the world’s population and around 40% of global GDP, has both the capacity and responsibility to help overcome global divisions and deliver concrete results.

“Peace and strategic stability are necessary conditions for economic and sustainable development,” Tokayev said, calling for a shift from the de-escalation of individual conflicts toward long-term stability based on political dialogue and diplomacy.

Against this backdrop, Tokayev positioned BRICS as a platform for practical cooperation rather than an alternative to the existing international system.

“As a partner country, Kazakhstan views BRICS as an open platform for practical cooperation that complements the multilateral system with the central role of the United Nations and connects peoples, regions and markets,” he said.

He added that Kazakhstan always seeks to find a “common ground on every difficult issue,” describing the approach as consistent with the country’s “balanced, goal-oriented foreign policy.”

Anastasia Golyakova, founder of the ThinkBricks YouTube channel, said the approach reflects BRICS’ broader focus on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability, priorities that have gained greater relevance amid rising geopolitical tensions.

She said closer cooperation among BRICS members could help address shared challenges while giving partner countries such as Kazakhstan greater access to the bloc’s growing trade, investment and technological opportunities.

“BRICS gives much support to each other. So, from this point of view, for Kazakhstan, it’s a prosperous future, in my opinion,” Golyakova told The Astana Times.

Ayanangsha Maitra, an editor and a geopolitics specialist, echoed this view, saying Kazakhstan’s BRICS partnership could open new opportunities for economic cooperation and market access.

“Although Kazakhstan is not a full BRICS member, its partnership with the grouping adds value at a time of growing geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty,” Maitra told The Astana Times.

“BRICS could offer Kazakhstan additional avenues for cooperation with countries beyond its traditional economic and political partners,” he added.

Expanding trade and investment

The economic dimension of Kazakhstan’s BRICS engagement was central to Tokayev’s address.

According to him, trade between Kazakhstan and BRICS members and partners was around $72 billion in 2025.

“Having significant industrial, transit and technological potential, we intend to diversify trade, economic and investment ties with all BRICS countries. As chairman of the Eurasian Economic Union, Kazakhstan supports the expansion of economic cooperation with BRICS and the advancement of work on concluding a free trade agreement with India,” Tokayev said.

Tokayev also called on the New Development Bank, a multilateral development bank established by the group, to consider financing commercially viable projects in BRICS countries, including Kazakhstan.

Maitra identified critical minerals, jewelry, fashion and textiles as areas with potential to expand Kazakhstan-India trade.

“Despite Kazakhstan’s relatively modest population of around 20 million, the country has a strong entrepreneurial spirit and growing commercial links with India,” he said, pointing to increasing connectivity between the two countries.

Turning geography into connectivity

Transport connectivity was another central element of Tokayev’s vision.

“Last year, transit cargo volumes through Kazakhstan approached 40 million tons. Our long-term goal is to increase that figure to 100 million tons annually. Overall, our transit network already handles up to 85% of overland freight between China and Europe,” he said.

As part of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, Kazakhstan serves as a link between Asia and Europe through the Caspian Sea. Tokayev called for greater synergy between the Trans-Caspian route, China’s Belt and Road Initiative and the International North-South Transport Corridor.

Maitra highlighted that Kazakhstan’s position within the EAEU, the Commonwealth of Independent States and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization provides access to major regional markets. Its participation in the International North-South Transport Corridor adds another layer of connectivity.

“BRICS could expand that network beyond Kazakhstan’s traditional regional partners. The partnership adds another dimension by opening access to markets across a wider group of countries,” he said.

AI as a new layer of cooperation

AI represents another area where Kazakhstan sees room for practical BRICS cooperation.

Tokayev said Kazakhstan is ready to use its computing infrastructure and national and UN digital centers to expand cooperation in AI and proposed establishing a BRICS Plus Partnership in Artificial Intelligence.

The initiative, he said, could connect national AI centers, facilitate access to laboratories and research projects and support the development of multilingual AI solutions.

For Maitra, AI could also become an important area of Kazakhstan-India cooperation because the two countries bring complementary strengths.

“India has a strong IT sector and a large pool of software engineers and technology professionals, while Kazakhstan has established connections across the CIS and wider Eurasian markets. That combination could help Indian technology companies reach markets where language and regional expertise remain barriers,” he said.

Water security broadens the agenda

Tokayev also linked sustainability to one of the country’s longstanding international priorities: water security.

He reiterated Kazakhstan’s proposal to establish an International Water Organization as a specialized UN agency, arguing that global water governance remains fragmented and requires stronger international coordination.

“I invite the BRICS member states and partners to join the international consultations initiated by our country,” Tokayev said.

Meeting with Narendra Modi

On the sidelines of the summit, Tokayev also met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, highlighting India’s growing economic and technological weight and the expanding relationship between the two countries.

Modi highlighted the potential for closer ties in high technology and the creative industries, including cooperation between Astana Hub and Hyderabad’s Cyberabad technology ecosystem. He also invited Kazakh representatives, particularly young people, to take part in the WAVES creative industries summit in Mumbai next year.

The two leaders also discussed prospects for expanding economic ties between India and the Eurasian Economic Union. Tokayev said Kazakhstan, as the current chair of the EAEU, supports negotiations on a free trade agreement between the bloc and India and is ready to help advance the process.

Tokayev said around 600 companies with Indian capital operate in Kazakhstan, while nearly 150,000 Indian citizens visited the country last year. He also cited the large number of Indian students studying in Kazakhstan and cooperation between Astana and New Delhi within international organizations.

World.title: From Bronze Age Settlements to Medieval Cities: New Archaeological Discoveries Across Kazakhstan
World.content:
ASTANA — From Bronze Age settlements to medieval cities, archaeological research across Kazakhstan continues to reveal new details about the societies that once inhabited the Eurasian steppe.

Recent excavations have brought new findings from the ancient settlement of Zhankent in the Kyzylorda Region and a Bronze Age site near Imantau in northern Kazakhstan, while authorities are expanding efforts to protect historical and cultural monuments.

Together, these discoveries highlight the diversity of Kazakhstan’s archaeological heritage and show how excavation, scientific cooperation and modern research methods are helping researchers reconstruct different periods of the country’s past.

Zhankent: 20 years of archaeological research

One of the country’s longest-running archaeological projects is taking place at the ancient settlement of Zhankent in the Kyzylorda Region.

Systematic research at the site began in 2005. Over the past two decades, archaeologists have excavated more than 4,000 square meters and uncovered more than 25,000 artefacts, according to the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of Kazakhstan.

The finds include ceramic, metal, stone, bone and glass objects. They provide researchers with information about the daily life, crafts, economy and cultural connections of the settlement’s inhabitants.

Zhankent is particularly important for studying the history of the Oghuz. Archaeologists have investigated citadel, shahristan, residential quarters and economic structures, gradually reconstructing the layout and development of the medieval city.

The archaeological project has involved researchers from Kazakhstan and several other countries, contributing to a broader understanding of medieval settlements along the Syr Darya and the archaeological landscape of southern Kazakhstan.

Recent work at the site has focused on several areas of the ancient city, including the eastern gate complex and shahristan. Archaeologists have uncovered ceramic fragments, traditional asyks and animal remains, adding to the material evidence of everyday life at Zhankent. The settlement is also part of the Silk Roads: Fergana–Syr Darya Corridor included in Kazakhstan’s UNESCO World Heritage efforts.

Researchers are also using electrical tomography to examine underground layers and identify possible structures without excavating every part of the settlement.

Imantau: a glimpse into Bronze Age life

While Zhankent provides evidence of medieval urban civilization, archaeological research in northern Kazakhstan is taking researchers several thousand years further back. A joint expedition involving the National Museum of Kazakhstan and the National Museum of the People’s Republic of China conducted excavations at a Bronze Age settlement near Imantau in the Aiyrtau district of the North Kazakhstan Region.

According to the National Museum of Kazakhstan, the expedition was held from July 14 to Aug. 16, 2026, as part of cooperation between the two institutions.
